R166.decision_summary: R166 = increment D's LAST piece: tmux "windows" (a session holds several windows, each an independent pane layout, exactly one current) plus a GUI TAB STRIP. Built as Slice 1 (headless substrate) + Slice 2 (GUI) per the owner's scope choice, then 3-lens reviewed and remediated. Slice 1: registry window ops (new/select/rename/kill; the last window escalates to kill_session, tmux); the scope now carries the window identity resolved ATOMICALLY with the pool off the same Window, closing the window-switch bound scope.rs itself documented as "a bound, not a done thing"; a set_layout expected_window compare-and-set for bound d; wire actions + a scoped windows slot; and sprag CLI window subcommands. Slice 2: a GUI tab strip built from per-tab pinion ButtonExternals (fires on EVERY click, so it does not silence a re-select the way a RadioGroup's fire-only-on-change would) plus "+"/"x", on a window-aware layout mirror. Both smokes discharged: a headless CLI drive over a real --daemon, and the GUI :1 PIXEL payoff (render a tab, "+" creates a window, type a marker, switch tabs, the other window's marker returns IN PIXELS, "x" closes). The 3-lens review found ONE convergent MAJOR (two lenses independently, the R148 signal): the host built and tested expected_window but the GUI never SENT it (bound d inert for the flagship client) — and tracing it surfaced a deeper bug, the GUI's per-window store_layout revision guard DROPS a cross-window layout (a switch to a lower-revision window projects the old window's tree over the new panes). Both fixed together by making the layout mirror window-aware (resets on a switch, guards within a window) and wiring the GUI to send expected_window; revert-proved. Committed 2e24e32; awaiting owner push consent.
changes_bullets: R166 = increment D's LAST piece — tmux "windows" (a session holds several windows, each an independent pane layout, exactly one current) + a GUI TAB STRIP. Slice 1 (headless) + Slice 2 (GUI) per the owner's scope choice. Commit `feat(mux) 2e24e32` on R165's `ec9df2d`. 3-lens reviewed + remediated. Gate green: fmt/clippy/doc -D 0; tests sprag-gui 124 + host-lib 99 + cli 5 + wire_client 10 + terminal 64; wire_client 10/10 + 0 leaks; sprag-terminal pinion-free.

SLICE 1 (headless substrate): `Session::{new,select,rename}_window` + `SessionRegistry::{new,select,rename,kill}_window`. `kill_window` drains a non-last window's panes OFF the registry lock (`WindowKillOutcome::Removed(Vec<Pane>)`); a session's LAST window ESCALATES to `kill_session` (`::Session(KillOutcome)`, tmux "kill the last window ⇒ the session is gone ⇒ the last session ⇒ the daemon"). `window_mut(session, window)` is now NAME-ADDRESSED on BOTH dimensions; `current_window` adjusts on a kill onto the tmux neighbour (next, or previous if the last was killed). `WindowInfo{name,current}` DTO + `Session::window_infos` = ONE shape for the wire slot, a client's mirror, and the trait.

SCOPE window-identity fix (closes the owed bound): `SessionScope` gains a `window` name, read ATOMICALLY with the pool off the SAME `&Window` (`of_session`); the layout paths (`reconciled_layout`/`set_layout`/`set_floating`) resolve `window_mut(session, scope.window())` — so a request acts on the window it was ASSEMBLED for, not "whichever is current at the moment of use". Bound d: `set_layout` gains an optional `expected_window`; a write whose named window != the current one is REFUSED (the belt to the revision compare-and-set's suspenders).

WIRE + CLI: SCOPED actions `new/select/rename/kill_window` on `WorkspaceExternal` (act on the request's session, unlike `new/kill_session` which name a session) + a `windows` read slot. `new_window` births its pane AT THE HOST (the D4 seam — create+select under the registry lock, clone the now-current pool OUT via `workspace_of`, spawn OFF the lock with the `on_pane_exit` death-signal). `handle_session_kill` factored so `kill_session` and `kill_window`'s escalation cannot drift. `sprag` CLI: `windows / new-window / select-window / rename-window / kill-window -t SESSION` (pre-flights the session, drives the scoped mux actions).

SLICE 2 (GUI tab strip, NEW `crates/sprag-gui/src/wtabs.rs`): per-tab pinion `ButtonExternal`s at FIXED tags (fires EVERY click — a `RadioGroupExternal` fires only on a change of its OWN selection, which would SILENCE a click on the tab it stalely believes is selected; the current window moves out of band via "+" auto-select or another attached client) + "+"/"×" buttons. `view.rs::compose` -> `Column[strip, fill_remaining(content)]` (main window ONLY; floaters bypass compose). `HostClient` grows `windows/select_window/new_window/kill_window` (in-process `Host` + `WireHost` impls) + `SlotView` passthroughs. Tabs are mouse-first (not `with_focusable`, like the context menu).

3-LENS review (correctness/SSOT · seam/lifetimes · test/doc): 0 CRITICAL. ONE convergent MAJOR (Lens 2 + Lens 3 INDEPENDENTLY — the R148 signal): the host built + tested `expected_window` but the GUI's `WireHost::set_layout` never SENT it, so bound d was inert for the flagship client. Tracing it surfaced a DEEPER bug (mine): the GUI's per-window `store_layout` revision guard DROPS a cross-window layout — switching to a window whose `layout_revision` is LOWER projects the OLD window's tree over the NEW window's panes (`adopt_layout` finds no slots -> collapsed dock). Both fixed together (see verification). Lens 3 MAJOR: 5 stale roadmap/invariant docs (this change shipped the ops those docs called "a later increment"). Lens 1: 0 MAJOR, all seams SOUND. All findings remediated in the same commit.
verification_bullets: Gate: `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p sprag-terminal -p sprag-host -p sprag-gui --all-targets -- -D warnings` = 0; `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --no-deps` = 0; tests sprag-gui 124 / host-lib 99 / cli 5 / wire_client 10 / terminal 64 / resize 4, 0 failed; `wire_client` 10/10 repeats + 0 socket/proc leaks; `sprag-terminal` `cargo tree` pinion-free. Pre-commit hook (validate-workspace + rustfmt + clippy) passed on `2e24e32`.

REVERT-PROVED the load-bearing new guards: (a) the host `expected_window` guard — neuter `expected_window != scope.window()` => BOTH the unit `set_layout_refuses_a_write_authored_against_a_different_window` AND the real-socket `a_layout_write_tagged_with_the_wrong_window_is_refused` FAIL; restored => green. (b) the window-aware layout mirror — neuter the reset-on-switch (`mirror.window != current`) => `the_layout_mirror_resets_on_a_window_switch_but_guards_within_a_window` FAILS (the lower-revision switch is dropped as stale); restored => green. (c) the registry `> widx` kill branch is now exercised by `kill_window_below_the_current_keeps_current_on_the_same_window` (every other kill test kills the CURRENT window).

Coverage added for the review's holes: registry `>widx` kill; the wire actions reject non-string args (`expected_window`/`window` = 42 -> TypeMismatch); the real-socket bound-d refusal + its control (the SAME gesture tagged with the current window applies); the pure `store_layout` window-aware reset/guard.

HEADLESS smoke over a real `sprag-term --daemon` (isolated short-path socket): `sprag new work` -> `new-window -t work editor` (2 windows, editor current) -> `windows -t work` -> `select-window -t work 0` -> `rename-window -t work shell` -> `kill-window -t work editor` (non-last, removed) -> `kill-window -t work` (the LAST window ESCALATES to killing session work). Correct; the daemon then self-exits (work held the only live panes; empty-boot default + "0 live panes ⇒ exit").

GUI :1 PIXEL smoke (the owed tab-UX payoff; the window is unseen, so verified by RPC `scene/snapshot` for the strip tags + `scene/screenshot` for the pixels): boot renders the strip (`sprag_gui.{wstrip,wtab.0,wnew,wclose}` in the paint scene) and window 0's `echo WINOMARK42` in the left pane; clicking "+" (its rect center) => 2 tabs, "1" current, window 1 fresh (no marker); clicking tab "0" => WINOMARK42 COMES BACK IN THE PIXELS (window 0 restored — the plan's owed payoff); clicking "×" (its RE-FETCHED center; the strip shifts right as tabs are added) => the current window closes. `gui.log` records `sprag_gui.wnew.click` / `wtab.0.click` / `wclose.click` = direct proof the clicks route to the reducer.

Re-verified LIVE after the layout-mirror remediation: boot (1 tab) -> "+" (2 tabs, window 1, 47KB fresh) -> tab-0 (host windows "0* 1", window 0 restored, 60KB) — the window-aware mirror did not break switching; 0 residual procs/sockets on `kill-server`.
carry_forward_bullets: PUSH: NOT YET PUSHED — awaiting owner consent. Local commit `feat(mux) 2e24e32`; this `docs(mnemosyne)` changelog is the second commit of the round. origin/main = R165 `ec9df2d`.

INCREMENT D IS COMPLETE with this round: D1-D3 session lifecycle (kill-session, client detach, sprag CLI), D4 empty-session policy (born with a shell), R165 attach, R166 windows/tabs. DEFERRED as a later increment (Slice 3, NOT part of D's core): break-pane / join-pane — cross-window pane MIGRATION, a pane keeping its globally-unique id as it moves between windows' `Workspace`s (the shared id counter is what makes it clean; moving a live `Pane` = PTY + emulator + reader thread between pools is the real mechanism).

SEAM (so next session need not re-derive): the GUI layout mirror is now `Mirrored{window, layout}`. `store_layout(mirror, current, snapshot)` RESETS unconditionally on a window change (the per-window `layout_revision` does NOT compare across windows) and revision-GUARDS within a window (the R154 lost-layout scar). `WireHost::set_layout` sends `expected_window` from that mirror's window (bound d). `refresh_view` (called by select/new/kill_window) re-reads windows + panes + layout TOGETHER so a switch is immediate and consistent; the poll thread reads WINDOWS FIRST each wake to tag the layout store. Host side: `new_window`/`kill_window` bind the outcome off-lock (blocking `PanePty::Drop` outside the registry lock); `new_window` births at the host (D4), the birth pane carries `on_pane_exit`.

TRACKED BOUNDS (all documented in-code, narrow): tabs are MOUSE-FIRST (not `with_focusable`) — keyboard/a11y for the tabs is a follow-up (matches the ctxmenu precedent; the CLI `select-window` covers keyboard users; making them focusable would break `panes_are_scene_derived_focus_stops`, which asserts exactly the two panes). `MAX_WINDOW_TABS = 16` is an HONEST cap (a window past it gets no painted tab, but its panes still render, "×" scans ALL windows for the current one, and the CLI reaches it — like `MAX_PANES`). The `WireHost` window METHODS have no DIRECT unit test (WireHost is hard to unit-test) — covered by the in-process reducer test `window_tab_clicks_route_to_the_host_select_new_and_close` + the real-socket `two_windows`/bound-d wire tests + the pure `store_layout` unit test.

PROCESS: owner chose "Slice 1 + 2 this round" and "kill-last-window escalates to kill-session (tmux)" via AskUserQuestion. 3-lens review run (the owner's established ritual for these rounds). GUI RPC on :1: socket `SPRAG_RPC_SOCK` (+ `SPRAG_RPC=1`); `scene/snapshot {path, from:"paint", viewport}` (path "" = the whole paint tree; an unknown tag path is UnsupportedPath -> walk the full tree for a tag's rect); `scene/click {at:{x,y}}`; `scene/screenshot {path:"", out_path, viewport}`. Button rects come from the FULL snapshot; the strip SHIFTS right as tabs are added, so re-fetch a button's center after any layout change. Commit 1-3 bullets <=72 bytes, prose/Co-Authored-By FORBIDDEN (the commit-msg hook rejects them). Work on main only. NEVER push without explicit consent. Mnemosyne is append-only — never probe with real ids (use throwaway ids / the file-based CLI flags).

R167.decision_summary: R167 = the cmux durability ring, slice 1 — the second orthogonal durability axis (tmux parity: a daemon outlives the CLIENT; cmux parity: the layout, cwd and shape outlive a REBOOT via disk serialization). A live PTY cannot cross a reboot; a logical layout can. Built design-first per the owner cost-no-object direction, then 3-lens reviewed and fully remediated. A serde Snapshot projects the SessionRegistry the way LayoutWire projects a LayoutTree; from_snapshot rebuilds the shape pane-free and the host re-spawns each pane as a shell in its recorded cwd under its OLD id (PanePty cwd reads /proc; a seeded counter plus spawn_with_dirty_id keep ids stable so the layout tree still resolves). The daemon boots-from-snapshot-or-empty and a 5s write-if-changed loop persists the shape to XDG_STATE_HOME (persistent, not the tmpfs runtime dir the socket lives in), versioned and fail-safing to an empty boot on any bad snapshot. The 3-lens review converged on the shutdown-vs-restore seam: a clean exit never invalidated the snapshot, so the daemon resurrected a session the user deliberately closed; fixed by the reaper clearing the snapshot on a voluntary close, which a reboot never fires because interactive shells ignore SIGTERM (empirically verified). Also: from_snapshot now rejects duplicate pane ids. Live-proven across a hard kill -9 (restore plus cwd survive) and a deliberate kill-server (no resurrect). Local commits only; awaiting owner push consent.

PROJECTION seam (`sprag-terminal/snapshot.rs`): a serde `Snapshot` is to a `SessionRegistry` what `LayoutWire` is to a `LayoutTree` — captured FROM the one authority, restored INTO a fresh one, never a second authority. `snapshot(registry)` is TWO-PHASE: it clones the structure + each pool's `Arc` under a brief registry lock, RELEASES it, then reads each pool's panes (cwd/dims) under its own lock — registry-then-workspace SEQUENTIALLY, never nested (the `reconciled_layout` discipline). Captures per pane {id, cwd, command_label, cols, rows}, per window the `LayoutWire` + float set, and the global `next_id` high-water mark.

RESTORE seam (`registry.rs::from_snapshot` + `host.rs::Host::restore`): `from_snapshot` rebuilds the session/window/tree/float shape PANE-FREE and returns a `RestorePlan`; the host re-spawns each pane at the HOST (the D4 birth seam) as a shell in its recorded cwd, under its OLD id, with the daemon's own on_dirty/on_exit hooks. `spawn_with_dirty_id` + `Workspace::with_seeded_counter` keep pane ids STABLE across the reboot (the layout tree references panes by id; deriving `next_id` from live ids would REISSUE a retired top-gap id, so it is stored, not derived). `PanePty::pid` + `cwd` (Linux `/proc/<pid>/cwd`) read the fact restore re-spawns into.

DAEMON (`bin/sprag-term.rs`): `--daemon` boots-from-snapshot-or-empty; a 5s `save_if_changed` loop persists the shape to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/sprag/<stem>.snapshot.json` (PERSISTENT — the socket's `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is tmpfs, wiped on the very reboot the ring targets), atomic temp-then-rename, writing only when the shape changed. A versioned JSON that fail-safes to an EMPTY boot on any bad/old/corrupt snapshot (never bricks the daemon). Installs a `SPRAG_LOG` subscriber (default `warn,sprag_host::durability=info`) so the ring narrates its restore/save.

The daemon reaper's on_empty now CLEARS the snapshot (daemon only) before raising SIGTERM = deliberate-close invalidation; `install_shutdown` (external SIGTERM = reboot) leaves it.

NEXT (SLICE 2 of the ring): allowlisted opt-in EXACT-COMMAND restore (persist argv, re-run a curated safe set — editors/ssh/agents — not blanket) WITH a deliberate env policy (do NOT write env secrets to the plaintext state file; re-derive from the daemon env). The snapshot already carries `command_label` for this, so the on-disk format needs no migration to add it. This is where sprag reaches cmux's "agents come back" — but via a safety allowlist, not blanket re-run.

TRACKED BOUNDS (narrow, documented in-code): (a) a LAST pane running a foreground program that TERMINATES on SIGTERM, during a reboot, racing the daemon's own handler, could still fire the reaper and clear the snapshot (lose that restore) — rare; the common interactive-shell case is safe. (b) the restore reaper race (a pathological self-exiting `$SHELL` dying mid-restore) — Lens 1 verified unreachable for a normal blocking shell. (c) homes (the float dock-back memo) are NOT persisted — float MEMBERSHIP survives, only the exact dock-back slot degrades to an append (the "a home is a memo, not a promise" fallback). (d) the `/tmp` final fallback for the state dir is often tmpfs (durability silently degrades to pre-durability there, only when both XDG_STATE_HOME and HOME are unset).

SEAM (so next session need not re-derive): `snapshot(registry)` two-phase locks (registry -> clone Arcs -> release -> per-pool), never nested. `from_snapshot` rebuilds PANE-FREE + a `RestorePlan`; `Host::restore` swaps the registry CONTENTS (preserving the `Arc` the reaper holds) then births each pane at the host via `spawn_with_dirty_id(id, ..)` with the daemon hook FACTORIES. `next_id` is STORED (not derived) to keep the never-reused invariant across a reboot. The daemon reaper's on_empty now CLEARS the snapshot (daemon only) before raising SIGTERM = deliberate-close invalidation; `install_shutdown` (external SIGTERM = reboot) leaves it.

NEXT (SLICE 2 of the ring): allowlisted opt-in EXACT-COMMAND restore (persist argv, re-run a curated safe set — editors/ssh/agents — not blanket) WITH a deliberate env policy (do NOT write env secrets to the plaintext state file; re-derive from the daemon env). The snapshot already carries `command_label` for this, so the on-disk format needs no migration to add it. This is where sprag reaches cmux's "agents come back" — but via a safety allowlist, not blanket re-run.

TRACKED BOUNDS (narrow, documented in-code): (a) a LAST pane running a foreground program that TERMINATES on SIGTERM, during a reboot, racing the daemon's own handler, could still fire the reaper and clear the snapshot (lose that restore) — rare; the common interactive-shell case is safe. (b) the restore reaper race (a pathological self-exiting `$SHELL` dying mid-restore) — Lens 1 verified unreachable for a normal blocking shell. (c) homes (the float dock-back memo) are NOT persisted — float MEMBERSHIP survives, only the exact dock-back slot degrades to an append (the "a home is a memo, not a promise" fallback). (d) the `/tmp` final fallback for the state dir is often tmpfs (durability silently degrades to pre-durability there, only when both XDG_STATE_HOME and HOME are unset).

STALE MEMORY to fix: the [[arc-debt-register]] item (F) "cmux disk-durability ring ... parked" is now superseded — slice 1 landed. Update it to point at slice 2 (exact-command restore + env policy) as the remaining cmux front.

R168.decision_summary: R168 = the cmux durability ring, slice 2 — allowlisted EXACT-COMMAND restore (the agents-come-back half). Slice 1 re-spawned every pane as a shell in its cwd; slice 2 records each pane launch argv and, on restore, re-runs the exact command for an allowlisted NON-shell program, else falls back to a shell. A shell is NEVER re-run with its recorded argv (the structural guard that a bash dash-c destructive command can never be re-executed on a reboot); env is not persisted (a restored command inherits the daemon env). The 3-lens review, with Lens 2 scoped to the allowlist as a SECURITY boundary, found THREE MAJORs — all remediated. The worst was a DATA-LOSS regression: a restored program that exits (an ssh whose network is not up yet at boot) triggered the reaper, which slice 1 fix made DELETE the snapshot, permanently destroying the session; fixed by making the reaper never delete — a natural exit KEEPS the snapshot and only an explicit kill-server clears it, and the reaper is gated during the restore loop. Also: ssh and mosh dropped from the default allowlist because they re-run remote commands (opt-in like tmux-resurrect); the snapshot file hardened to owner-only 0600 because argv can carry flag secrets; the allowlist injected into restore so tests are hermetic (the env-race flake removed). Live-proven: exact-command restore across kill -9, a natural exit keeps the snapshot, kill-server clears it, and the file is mode 600. Local commits only; awaiting owner push consent.

ARGV capture: `Pane` gains an `argv: Vec<String>`, read from the `CommandBuilder` (`get_argv`) INSIDE `Workspace::spawn*` — so the mux `spawn` path (where a `claude`/`vim` argv enters) captures it with NO signature change. `PaneSnapshot.argv` is `#[serde(default)]` (a pre-argv slice-1 snapshot still loads -> empty argv -> shell), so NO version bump.

THE ALLOWLIST (`durability::restore_command`): re-run the exact argv only for a NON-shell program whose `argv[0]` basename is in the allowlist (editors / pagers / `claude`); a SHELL, an empty argv, or a non-allowlisted program restores a plain shell in the cwd. Shells are NEVER re-run with their argv — the structural guard that a `bash -c '<destructive>'` can never be re-executed on a reboot. Env is NOT persisted: a restored command inherits the DAEMON's env (where API keys live). Override via `SPRAG_RESTORE_PROGRAMS` (comma basenames; empty disables all).
3-LENS REVIEW (Lens 2 = the security boundary) found 3 MAJORs, ALL remediated:

§1 (the worst, a DATA-LOSS REGRESSION vs slice 1): a restored program that EXITS (a `ssh` whose network is not up yet at boot) triggered the reaper, which R167's fix made DELETE the snapshot -> the session was permanently destroyed. FIX: the reaper NO LONGER deletes; a natural last-pane exit KEEPS the snapshot (the next daemon retries), and only an EXPLICIT `sprag kill-server` (or a kill that ends the last session/window) clears it — CLI-side. The reaper is also GATED during the restore loop (`restoring` flag) so a fast-exiting re-run program cannot self-kill the daemon mid-restore.

§2: `ssh`/`mosh` re-ran their REMOTE command on every reboot (`ssh host 'systemctl restart …'`). FIX: DROPPED from the default allowlist (opt-in via `SPRAG_RESTORE_PROGRAMS`, like tmux-resurrect). The doc no longer claims allowlisted programs have "no side effects" — the allowlist gates the PROGRAM, and its own argv is re-run verbatim.

§3: the argv (which carries flag secrets — `mysql -pSECRET`) is persisted to what was an umask-dependent (often world-readable) file. FIX: the snapshot is written OWNER-ONLY — the temp is created mode 0600 (no readable window), fsync'd before the rename, and the dir tightened to 0700. The "no secret on disk" doc is corrected: env is not persisted, but argv IS (hence 0600).

Also (Lens 1/3): the allowlist is now INJECTED into `Host::restore` (the daemon reads the env once and passes it) so the host is hermetic; the env-override test became a PURE `parse_allowlist` test (no `set_var` race — the flake scar); the dead `PaneRestore.command_label` was pruned. +5 tests (serde-default upgrade, host end-to-end re-run, pure parse, empty-argv-is-a-shell, footgun guard already present).

THE §1 DATA-LOSS FIX proven live: (B) a session whose only pane EXITS on its own (a `sleep 6`) — the daemon self-exits (reaper) but the snapshot SURVIVES (the reaper no longer deletes it), so a transient program exit no longer destroys the session. The generalizable rule: a heuristic that keys off "the last pane exited" cannot tell a deliberate close from a program crash — so it must never DESTROY durable state on that signal. (c) a non-UTF-8 ARGUMENT is `to_string_lossy`-mojibake'd (an exact restore opens the wrong path); the program + ASCII flags are exact. (d) argv is on disk (0600); a secret passed as a FLAG lands there — prefer env/config over CLI secrets. (e) a natural close now RESURRECTS on next launch (tmux-continuum behavior, not data loss); `kill-server` is the explicit clear. NEXT (durability ring, remaining): the ring's CORE is done (shape + cwd + exact-command, both slices). Remaining polish/parity: per [[arc-debt-register]] the ring is item F — update it (slice 2 landed). R169.decision_summary: R169 = the kill-server --purge affordance plus a polarity refinement of the durability snapshot lifecycle, per the owner start-fresh ask. R168 made kill-server DELETE the snapshot, which made --purge redundant and, worse, made stopping the daemon destroy the durable workspace — incoherent for a durability ring. R169 inverts to the cmux-durable model: the daemon lifecycle always PRESERVES the snapshot (a reboot, a crash, a natural close, and a plain kill-server all leave it, so the workspace comes back next launch), and kill-server --purge is the ONE explicit destroy-the-saved-workspace path. The CLI rejects any non---purge arg before connecting, so a typo cannot end the daemon; the clear was also removed from the kill-session and kill-window server-ended arms (ending the daemon is incidental to those, and a non-last kill already updates the snapshot via the live save loop). The R168 data-loss fix is unchanged: the reaper never deletes; only --purge does. A consequence, intended and documented: a deliberate close now resurrects the workspace next launch — that is durability, not a bug, with --purge as the escape hatch. The cmux durability ring is now complete across three slices (shape+cwd, exact-command, lifecycle+purge). Live-proven: plain kill-server keeps and resurrects, --purge clears and starts fresh. Local commit only; awaiting owner push consent.

THE REFINEMENT: R168 made `kill-server` DELETE the snapshot, which made `--purge` redundant and, more importantly, made STOPPING the daemon destroy the durable workspace — incoherent for a durability ring. R169 inverts it to the cmux-durable model: the DAEMON LIFECYCLE always PRESERVES the snapshot (a reboot, a crash, a natural close, AND a plain `kill-server` all leave it, so the workspace comes back next launch), and `kill-server --purge` is the ONE explicit "destroy the saved workspace / start fresh".

CODE (`sprag.rs`): `kill_server` parses `--purge` (rejecting any other arg BEFORE connecting, so a typo cannot end the daemon); `--purge` clears the snapshot and prints "server stopped (workspace purged)", plain `kill-server` prints "server stopped" and keeps it. The `clear_snapshot()` calls were REMOVED from the `kill-session` / `kill-window` server-ended arms — ending the daemon is incidental to those, so they keep too (a non-last kill already updates the snapshot via the live save loop).
The §1 DATA-LOSS fix from R168 is UNCHANGED: the reaper still never deletes the snapshot; only `--purge` does. So a transient re-run-program exit still cannot destroy the session.
Docs refreshed to the durable model (the `sprag-term` module + reaper comments, `clear_snapshot`, `kill_server`, the CLI usage + module command list).

NEW CLI tests: `the_cli_kill_server_purge_ends_the_daemon` (the `--purge` flag is accepted and still ends the daemon) and `kill_server_refuses_an_unknown_arg` (a `kill-server --force` is refused BEFORE any kill, names `--purge`, and the daemon is still reachable afterwards — a typo cannot end the server).

LIVE SMOKE over a real `--daemon` (isolated socket + `$XDG_STATE_HOME`; pid via the socket): (1) a `tail` session saved; (2) plain `kill-server` KEEPS the snapshot; (3) a fresh daemon RESTORES the tail session (resurrect — the durable default); (4) `kill-server --purge` DELETES the snapshot ("server stopped (workspace purged)"); (5) a fresh daemon after `--purge` starts EMPTY (no resurrect). The two polarities are correctly distinguished.

Non-vacuous: reverting the `if purge` guard (always clear) would make smoke step 2/3 fail (the plain kill-server would delete and the session would not resurrect); reverting it to never-clear would make step 4/5 fail (the purge would not delete and the session would resurrect).

THE DURABILITY LIFECYCLE MODEL (now settled, so a future session need not re-derive): the snapshot is the DURABLE record. It survives the entire daemon lifecycle — reboot, crash, kill -9, a natural last-pane close, and a plain `kill-server`. The live save loop keeps it current WHILE the daemon runs; on exit the last-saved shape persists; the next daemon restores it. The ONLY delete is `sprag kill-server --purge` (CLI-side `clear_snapshot`). The reaper NEVER deletes (the R168 §1 data-loss fix). This is the cmux-durable model, coherent across all three slices.

CONSEQUENCE (documented, intended): a deliberate close (typing `exit` in every shell) RESURRECTS the workspace on the next launch — that is durability, not a bug; `--purge` is the escape hatch. This supersedes the R168-era "kill-server clears" (which was incoherent — stopping the daemon should not destroy the durable state).

STALENESS bound (inherent to periodic save): killing the LAST session/window (which ends the daemon) leaves the snapshot up to one save-interval stale, so that just-killed session can resurrect on the next launch. Acceptable in the durable model; `--purge` clears it.

R170.decision_summary: R170 = the cmux-parity VERTICAL SESSION SIDEBAR plus in-place session switching, the first of the separate parity fronts opened after the durability ring completed at R169. A left rail lists every daemon session with the attached one highlighted; clicking a row switches this GUI to that session IN PLACE (tmux switch-client), and a "+" creates and switches to a fresh one. GUI-only, no host behaviour change: the SESSIONS_SLOT the sidebar reads was already on the wire (sprag ls uses it) and only the GUI now consumes it. The switch is attach-minus-the-process: WireHost stops and joins its poll thread, re-scopes the request connection, re-boots its mirrors from the target session, and respawns the poll, falling back to the previous session on any failure. Chosen per the owner as the most long-term-correct option: in-place switching is not a cmux novelty but core tmux (switch-client), and the wire protocol was purpose-built for it (the session param rides every request; one daemon holds all sessions), so read-only or a new window per click would be a tmux regression. Built, 3-lens reviewed on the uncommitted tree, remediated in place, and live-pixel-smoke-proven on :1. Slice 1 of 3 (metadata cwd/git/ports deferred to additive slices on the same extensible SessionInfo query).

R171.decision_summary: R171 = Slice 2 of the cmux session sidebar: each session row now shows its working directory and git branch, derived host-side and carried on the same extensible SessionInfo wire query, with the client a pure projection. The builder is two-phase like the durability snapshot so the registry and workspace locks never nest; the branch is read from the repository HEAD with no subprocess. The GUI shows the cwd basename plus branch on a second row line; sprag ls shows the full path plus branch. Live-proven over a real daemon socket and by a headless GUI pixel smoke.
changes_bullets: R171 = Slice 2 of the cmux session sidebar (R170): each session row now shows its working directory and git branch. GUI-only display of a HOST-derived fact — the client never reads a path or runs git. 1 feat commit on R170's changelog.

sprag-terminal: SessionInfo gains cwd + branch (Option<String>; serde default + skip_serializing_if=Option::is_none, so an empty session with no pane serialises to the EXACT pre-Slice-2 shape — the addition is truly additive). New SessionRegistry::session_infos_live(&Arc<Mutex<Self>>) is TWO-PHASE exactly like snapshot(): phase 1 under the registry lock captures the structural infos plus each session's current-window pool Arc; phase 2 locks each pool ALONE for its first pane's live /proc cwd; phase 3 derives the git branch off every lock. The structural session_infos() stays the SSOT for name/windows/default.

New crate-internal git.rs (pure fs, no subprocess): branch(cwd) walks up to the first .git (a directory, or a gitdir: pointer FILE for a linked worktree/submodule), reads HEAD (ref: refs/heads/NAME -> NAME with slashes kept; a detached HEAD -> its short (sha)). Both host arms — the wire SESSIONS_SLOT handler and the in-process Host::sessions — now call session_infos_live, so the enriched shape cannot drift between them.

sprag-gui stabs.rs: the session row becomes two lines — name + window count on top, a muted subtitle (cwd basename joined with the branch) below; ROW_HEIGHT 30 -> 44, and clickable() generalised to wrap any content. sprag ls (the CLI over the same slot) appends the FULL cwd plus [branch], so the sidebar's basename has its full path a `sprag ls` away.

sprag-host: HostClient gains kill_session(name); the in-process Host implements it as a documented no-op (a default-only debug hatch owns no client to detach nor daemon to end; the registry keeps default_session total across a kill anyway, so even reaching it would be safe).

sprag-gui WireHost::kill_session sends the invoke, then splits on whether name == the attached session: OWN -> self.quit.request_quit() (immediate detach; R163's poll detach_reason is the backstop / the out-of-band path when another client or the CLI kills this session), OTHER -> refresh_sessions() (a UI-thread sessions re-read so the killed row leaves at once; the poll's revision-bump re-read is the backstop). The invoke's answer is ignored (a last-session kill can sever the reply, indistinguishable from success). SlotView::kill_session passes through.

sprag-gui stabs.rs: each row is now TWO hit-targets -- a flex-grow SWITCH body tagged sprag_gui.stab.{i} and a fixed-width (KILL_WIDTH) "x" tagged sprag_gui.skill.{i} -- inside one UNTAGGED row that carries the highlight fill (AlignItems::Stretch, so the whole band hit-tests). create_session_externals registers 2*MAX+1 buttons. The reducer routes a body click to switch_session and an "x" to kill_session, each by resolving the paint-time index into the LIVE session list by NAME; row_index / kill_index are prefix-disjoint (stab vs skill), so every click resolves to exactly one action.

sprag-host: HostClient gains kill_session(name); the in-process Host implements it as a documented no-op (a default-only debug hatch owns no client to detach nor daemon to end; the registry keeps default_session total across a kill anyway, so even reaching it would be safe).

sprag-gui WireHost::kill_session sends the invoke, then splits on whether name == the attached session: OWN -> self.quit.request_quit() (immediate detach; R163's poll detach_reason is the backstop / the out-of-band path when another client or the CLI kills this session), OTHER -> refresh_sessions() (a UI-thread sessions re-read so the killed row leaves at once; the poll's revision-bump re-read is the backstop). The invoke's answer is ignored (a last-session kill can sever the reply, indistinguishable from success). SlotView::kill_session passes through.

sprag-gui stabs.rs: each row is now TWO hit-targets -- a flex-grow SWITCH body tagged sprag_gui.stab.{i} and a fixed-width (KILL_WIDTH) "x" tagged sprag_gui.skill.{i} -- inside one UNTAGGED row that carries the highlight fill (AlignItems::Stretch, so the whole band hit-tests). create_session_externals registers 2*MAX+1 buttons. TRIGGER 1 (sidebar own-kill), WireHost::kill_session is now 3-way: under a switch policy with a live neighbour it STOPS+JOINS the poll BEFORE the kill (so the kill's revision bump cannot wake the dying-scope poll into flagging a racing switch), kills, then switch_session(next); otherwise detach (own kill, last session) or refresh_sessions (another session). The successor is picked from the current list BEFORE the kill removes the name.

TRIGGER 2 (out-of-band kill), the poll thread: PollEnd splits SessionClosed (the daemon serves on) from HostGone; handle_poll_error, on SessionClosed under a switch policy, sets lost_session + repaints (NOT request_quit) and the UI-thread reconcile_lost_session (reconcile_frame, BEFORE slots.reconcile so the switched cache maps the same frame) does switch-to-next or detach. attach_in_place clears the flag so a manual switch cannot leave a stale one. HostGone ALWAYS detaches whatever the policy; the default Detach path is byte-identical to the pre-change poll detach.

HostClient trait: a defaulted reconcile_lost_session (no-op) so the in-process host inherits it (it has no daemon and one client, so it never loses a session out of band); SlotView passthrough; reconcile_frame calls it first. next / previous are by the sidebar LIST order (creation order, a stable Vec), the honest analog of tmux's session-name order given sprag has a visible sidebar.

sprag-gui wire.rs: a per-client MRU VISIT stack (WireHost.mru, RefCell<Vec<String>>) -- push_mru (most-recent-first, deduplicated) on every attach_in_place plus the boot session. New DetachOnDestroy::Off + parse "off".

destroy_successor gains an mru arg: off returns the most-recent OTHER session still live, else FALLS BACK to the next list-neighbour (so off still SWITCHES whenever another session exists), else detaches only when killed is truly the last session. next/previous ignore mru. The MRU is CLIENT-LOCAL (this client's visits), not tmux's global last-activity -- the honest divergence the fallback covers.

FIX the live smoke caught: the poll thread's out-of-band switch arm listed Next | Previous and MISSED Off, so off silently DETACHED. The switch-flag poll test now LOOPS off/next/previous so every switch policy is pinned to flag-not-detach -- the exact invariant the off-missing bug broke.

R179.decision_summary: R179 = keyboard + a11y for the session sidebar: a WAI-ARIA vertical tablist laid over the existing mouse rows. The session-list sub-container (SESSION_TABLIST_TAG) is the list SINGLE Tab stop; a client-local roving cursor (use_session_cursor = the aria-activedescendant) moves within it. handle_sidebar_key owns the model: arrows / Home / End rove, Enter or Space switch to the cursor session, Delete arms a kill, and while a kill is pending Enter confirms and Escape cancels. Every activation reuses handle_session_intent via a synthesised {tag}.click intent, so pointer, keyboard, and AT (a screen-reader Click lowers to apply_key Enter) share ONE routing SSOT. The + footer is a separate focusable button Tab stop. route_key dispatches to the rail before its pane focus gate for an is_sidebar_focus tag. a11y = a TabList parent + Tab children (aria-selected on the attached session, posinset / setsize, aria-activedescendant on the cursor). Chosen as the most long-term-correct and tmux choose-tree faithful model (not a per-item button toolbar); the rich rows keep their per-row externals via a manual composite over them, not a rewrite onto pinion simple-tab widget. GUI-only, additive. Proven by 8 revert-proof unit tests plus a live headless smoke (focus/set the tablist, scene/key ArrowDown moves the cursor border row 0 to 1, Enter moves the attached fill to row 1 = switched).

R180.decision_summary: R180 = per-client session attachment (R-PR67), the fact tmux calls "attached", carried end to end. The daemon keeps a conn->client->session map fed by client/hello and client/attach intercepts, and releases it from on_disconnect on the frame FIFO so a crashed client cannot leak a hold. SessionInfo gained an additive attached field on the wire; sprag-gui attaches on boot and on every switch, and the sidebar paints an "N viewing" badge - the first surface in sprag that shows another client exists at all. Stage 2 made destroy-time behaviour follow from it: a client switches only to a session no other client is viewing, and detaches otherwise (MRU-preferred, list-order fallback). CLI surface is sprag list-clients [-t SESSION] plus an (N attached) count in ls. Arrived alongside the pinion pin fc5f47ac -> fff2359c (R1393), whose RpcFrame gained conn: ConnId - stdin stamps one id and dispatch drops it.

R181.decision_summary: R181 = a pane can raise its hand. The emulator latches OSC 9, OSC 777;notify and OSC 99 (kitty) as a Notification {title, body, seq}, and counts bare BELs as a separate bell_seq with OSC terminators excluded - deliberately two facts, because tmux distinguishes monitor-bell from an application notification and so must sprag. Both propagate vt -> terminal -> host -> gui -> mcp. The client mirrors pane_notification with a per-slot seq-ack cleared on view, so an unattended pane is marked and looking at it is what clears the mark. The marker rides pane_display_title, which puts it on every title surface at once, and the a11y name announces it in WORDS rather than as a glyph a screen reader would have to guess at.

R182.decision_summary: R182 = the in-line editing and scroll-region halves of the VT audit, both driven through the real parser rather than a hand-built state. ICH / DCH / ECH / REP give row-local insert, delete, erase and repeat; DECSC / DECRC (ESC 7/8 and CSI s/u) save and restore position AND pen together, because a half-restored cursor is worse than none; DECSCUSR carries shape. The scroll region followed in the same arc: DECSTBM margins with a region-aware line feed, IND and reverse index, region-bounded IL/DL that home the column, and SU/SD. The revert-proof that mattered was on line_feed - breaking its region check fails the tests, which is what proves the margins are actually consulted rather than merely stored.

R183.decision_summary: R183 = OSC 133 shell integration, and the two agent-facing capabilities it unlocks. The emulator parses the A / C / D marks and keeps them PER ROW so they survive scroll, scrollback and reflow - a mark that moved with its text is the whole point. Shell state (idle / running) and the last exit code are DERIVED from the marks rather than stored beside them, so there is one truth. Screen::last_command slices command / output / exit at the A..C..D boundaries and becomes the fifth MCP tool, read_last_command: an AI in a pane can now read what the last command was, what it printed, and whether it worked. R185.decision_summary: R185 = two protocols that both hinge on refusing to lie. OSC 52 clipboard: the emulator records set and query, the host arbitrates exactly ONE reply per read, the GUI applies writes and answers reads, and SPRAG_OSC52 gates policy with read DENIED by default - a terminal that hands a page's clipboard read to any child is a data-exfiltration surface, so the safe arm is the default and the write payload is fetched on demand with acks primed against a stale clobber. The Kitty keyboard protocol added CSI >/</=/? u negotiation with the query reply riding a new device-response path, and the encoder emitting CSI u for Esc and the Ctrl/Alt/Super keys. Its flags are MASKED to what sprag actually supports (disambiguate) before the query answers, so the reply can never claim a capability the encoder does not have.

R186.decision_summary: R186 = OSC 8 hyperlinks, all the way from the pen to a click. The emulator's OSC 8 pen stamps cells and the Arc rides scroll, scrollback and reflow, so a link scrolled out and back is still the same link. sprag-grid interns them into pinion's HyperlinkId table and the snapshot carries the uri, which is what makes read_pane_links possible - an agent reads link TARGETS as data, something tmux capture cannot do because it flattens OSC 8 away. The human half is a per-pane hover oracle External co-tagged at pane_tag: it lights the whole id-group at once (wrap segments together, since one link split across two rows is still one link), captures a press only over a link so text selection still works everywhere else, shows a hand cursor, and opens through a scheme-gated platform opener. Two pin bumps carried it: b74b42c8 (pinion R1403) and 26436228 (R1404 images, R1405 link interaction).

R187.decision_summary: R187 = inline images, delivered in five staged slices under pinion R1404 and finished as a capability tmux simply does not have. Stage 1 decoded Kitty a=T RGB/RGBA single-chunk (16 MiB cap) and composited it as a pinion Scene::Image over memory://. Stage 2 added Sixel raster (6-bit vertical bands, palette, repeat) riding Stage 1's store, wire and composite UNCHANGED - which is the evidence the Stage 1 seam was cut in the right place - and fixed images being dropped on resize. Stage 3 gave them a lifecycle: scroll shifts an anchor with its region, off-edge evicts, an ED over the anchor row drops the image, reflow keeps it. Stage 4 completed the Kitty protocol - m=1 chunk reassembly (single in-flight, 24 MiB cap), a=d delete, a=q support ack written back over the pty, f=100 PNG decode. Stage 5 made transport on-demand: the panes slot carries only {id,w,h,anchor,seq} and the GUI fetches RGBA per (id,seq), with MCP read_pane_images reporting images as data.

R188.decision_summary: R188 = reflow, which is where sprag stops matching tmux and starts beating it. Scrollback and the visible screen reflow as ONE stream on resize, and a grow reclaims what a shrink wrapped - tmux reflows neither. The retention cap moved to LOGICAL lines, which is width-independent and therefore the only cap that means the same thing before and after a resize, with a physical ceiling behind it because tmux has no memory ceiling at all. Inline image anchors are tracked through all three reflow passes to their new cell, an image whose anchor reflows above the visible window is evicted, and next_image_seq is carried so a post-resize re-transmit stays monotonic. The subtle one is the resize-redraw window: a shell that redraws across several batches needs its CR-LF soft-wrap persisted across them while OSC 133 says it is at a prompt, and VtPort::note_input ends that epoch on user input. A non-integrated shell keeps the single-batch fallback, so nothing regressed for shells without OSC 133.

R189.decision_summary: R189 = break-pane and join-pane, tmux's move-a-pane-between-windows, on every surface at once. Session-side the moves live on WorkspaceExternal as BREAK_PANE_ACTION / JOIN_PANE_ACTION, with HostClient::break_pane / join_pane defaulted to None so a client that cannot do it says so rather than silently failing, and Host overriding. A pane is addressed by its registry-unique id and the SOURCE window is derived rather than passed - the caller cannot name a wrong source. CLI is break-pane PANE [name] and join-pane PANE WINDOW, both -t SESSION. The GUI got context-menu items whose action list is captured AT OPEN, so what was painted and what a click runs cannot disagree. The closing test is the interesting one: it drives the ctxmenu reducer against a seeded in-process host and asserts the window count moves 1 <-> 2, which closed the GUI context-menu smoke gap WITHOUT needing a shell or Xvfb.

R190.decision_summary: R190 = four smaller corrections that share a theme: making a resting state honest. The attention RING gives a pane with an unseen notification an Accent Border overlay keyed on pane_has_unseen_attention - pointer-transparent over the dim scrim and causing no layout shift, clearing on focus-ack; cmux has this and tmux offers only a title bell. Bracketed paste (DEC 2004) tracks the mode and wraps ESC[200~..201~ at the paste seam, FILTERING an embedded end marker so a pasted payload cannot break out of its own bracket. Session listings stopped showing the resting empty anchor: SessionInfo.panes plus is_listable means a session lists iff panes > 0 or attached > 0, which is tmux parity at rest and better than tmux when a client is viewing an empty session. And a flaky raw_output cap test was fixed properly - scroll_region_up/down now rotate the cell slice with zero heap allocation, and the test waits on the CONDITION it asserts (the cap latching) instead of on child EOF.

R191.decision_summary: R191 = xterm mouse tracking, staged, with the GUI capture layer built on the hover oracle from R186. Stage 1 reports left press/release when the child tracks the mouse, adds WireHost::mouse and a pane_mouse_active bit, and turns text selection off over a tracking pane; decoding the composite send payload here also fixed native clicks. Stage 2 sends xterm wheel 64/65 to a tracking grid with Shift bypassing to sprag's own scroll, and folds sub-line touchpad pans into whole notches so a trackpad does not emit a hundred reports per gesture. Stage 4 adds drag and motion (1002/1003) forwarded PER CELL, replacing the bool gate with pane_mouse_protocol. Stage 5 adds focus reporting (1004): the pane focus edge sends ESC[I / ESC[O, gated host-side by encode_focus. Pin 09da00e (pinion R1418, PR72) then delivered the raw pointer stream, so the oracle owns raw L/M/R with each edge carrying its real modifiers and a drag using the held button. MCP surfaces the tracking level per pane, so an agent can see what a pane is listening for.

Stage 4 adds drag and motion (1002/1003) forwarded PER CELL, replacing the bool gate with pane_mouse_protocol. Stage 5 adds focus reporting (1004): the pane focus edge sends ESC[I / ESC[O, gated host-side by encode_focus. Pin 09da00e (pinion R1418, PR72) then delivered the raw pointer stream, so the oracle owns raw L/M/R with each edge carrying its real modifiers and a drag using the held button. MCP surfaces the tracking level per pane, so an agent can see what a pane is listening for.

R192.decision_summary: R192 = device reports, and making one of them stop lying. CSI c / > c answer through the existing device-response channel, CSI 5 n reports ready and CSI 6 n the live 1-based cursor. The primary DA is deliberately TRUTHFUL - VT220 plus sixel plus ansi colour, nothing over-claimed - and that immediately exposed a gap: DA advertised sixel while XtSmGraphics went unanswered, so the handshake stalled half-done. Answering CSI ? 1/2 S with 65536 registers and 2048px geometry closes it. The window-focus half came with pin 6f9344c (pinion R1421, PR73): DEC 1004 focus reports are now intersected with window_focus_state::os_focused_window, so a blurred window emits ESC[O and a refocus ESC[I, matched per window identity. Without that gate a pane "focused" inside a window the user had alt-tabbed away from would keep telling its child it had focus.

R193.decision_summary: R193 = the colour and mode half of the VT long-tail audit, worked from the emulator's own `_ => {}` gaps rather than from a wish list - the gap list IS the spec here. OSC 10/11 set, query and render the default fg/bg; OSC 4/104 give the indexed palette, and a re-colour bumps ROW DAMAGE so the change actually repaints rather than waiting for the next write to that row. OSC 12 holds cursor colour state and answers its query (the render half needed PINION-PR74 and landed later). Modes: DECAWM autowrap (7) and DECOM origin (6); RIS hard reset (ESC c) and DECSTR soft reset (CSI ! p), which are different resets and were implemented as different resets; SCS character sets with DEC line drawing; IRM insert/replace (CSI 4 h/l); DECRQM request-mode reports (CSI Ps $ p); XTSAVE / XTRESTORE DEC private-mode registers; and LNM new-line mode (SM/RM 20) in BOTH halves - the input half and the output half, since a terminal that honours LNM on only one side is worse than one that ignores it.

R194.decision_summary: R194 = the print-path allocation debt, repaid and MEASURED - and the measurement is the lesson. Cell.cluster moved from String to a smol_str SSO string so a one-character cluster stays inline with no heap allocation, char_columns went through UnicodeWidthChar, and Print became an alloc-free print_char. Printing 256 KiB of 'a' went from 1.59M allocations to 20K, a 98.7% cut, with the NUL parser floor unchanged so the number is attributable to this change and not to the harness. It was counted with the global allocator rather than timed, because wall-clock on this machine drifted more than 20% run to run and would have hidden the result either way. The Cell.cluster hypothesis alone was also INCOMPLETE - the profile named more than one source - which is the standing reminder to measure before believing a cause.

R195.decision_summary: R195 = the rest of the VT tail, several items of which tmux and cmux implement none of. Synchronized output (DEC 2026) gives atomic frames. XTWINOPS answers 18t/19t cell size and 11t state from the grid and push/pops the title on 22t/23t, while the title REPORT (21t) stays deliberately gated off - a terminal that reads its own title back to the child is an injection vector. DECRQSS answers DCS $q for the SGR pen, cursor style and scroll region, serialising the pen to a self-contained 0-led SGR string, and replies DCS 0$r to an unknown request rather than dropping it. Reverse wraparound (DEC 45) backs a left-margin BS up only over a REAL soft wrap and never across a hard break. Grapheme clustering (DEC 2027) via UAX #29 clusters ZWJ emoji, flags and keycaps into one cell on the ON path while the OFF path stays byte-identical per scalar. VT420 rectangular editing (DECFRA/DECERA/DECCRA) does a snapshot-correct overlapping copy. DECSCA protected areas make DECSED/DECSEL/DECSERA skip protected cells while the non-selective erases still clear everything, VT220-style. Finally real pixel geometry: the GUI cell metric is carried through resize to the daemon emulator, so XTWINOPS 14t/15t/16t and the PTY winsize xpixel/ypixel stopped being zeroes.

R196.decision_summary: R196 = SSH workspaces, the cmux-parity front, in five slices. A workspace is a session whose BIRTH ARGV is `ssh -t host [cmd]`, built by an SshTarget SSOT and riding the existing new_session {cmd} - so there is no wire change and no daemon change, and the CLI verb is thin over a library parse. Port forwarding (-L) and a --tmux remote-tmux preset followed. The slice that mattered for durability is reconnect-on-restore: a structured SshRemote persists, so a restore RECONNECTS BY INTENT rather than by replaying an argv, which also means it bypasses the argv allowlist that would otherwise refuse it. Drag-to-upload closed the loop - a dropped file is scp'd to the remote pane, targeting the focused pane, running off-thread so the UI does not block.

carry_forward_bullets: reconnect-by-intent is the pattern any future structured birth (containers) should follow

R197.decision_summary: R197 = find-in-scrollback, and the design question it settled was WHERE search lives. It lives in sprag-vt, beside the CELLS, because a match's columns are derivable only there - a search done anywhere downstream has already lost the grid it would need to report a column against. It answers in the prompt_positions LOGICAL-LINE axis that R183's OSC 133 marks established, so a hit is reported in the same coordinate space the jump-to-prompt chord already used. The needle rides the RPC path VERBATIM - no normalisation, no reinterpretation - and the query is a READ, which matters because a read must not bump the scene revision and wake every other attached client. Three surfaces came out of one core: a GUI find bar with match highlight, a sprag find CLI, and a find_in_pane MCP tool.

R198.decision_summary: R198 = scrollback that survives a reboot - the CONTENT half of the durability ring, which is the axis cmux has and tmux does not (tmux's daemon outlives a client; only disk serialisation outlives a restart). A pane's history is encoded as REPLAYABLE TERMINAL BYTES rather than as a parsed structure, which is what lets a restore reuse the emulator it already has instead of needing a second decoder. The store sits beside the durability snapshot, per pane. Two query refinements landed with it: sprag find --pane narrows the sweep to one pane, and regex search is a DISTINCT query beside the literal find rather than a flag that reinterprets the same needle - the same principle R197 set when it made the needle ride verbatim.

R199.decision_summary: R199 = pin 701653a6 -> 4ff0b35f, consuming three delivered pinion PRs, plus a pre-existing flake fixed at its cause. PR-74 gave the cursor its OSC 12 colour and PR-75 the DECSCUSR blink on BOTH axes; PR-76 put the window id on the file-drop hooks, which is what lets a drop land on the window it was actually dropped on (a tear-off gets its own pane; the main window gets the focused pane, unless that pane is floating, in which case none). Two design corrections came out of consumption that the PR estimates had missed: Palette.cursor had to become Option<Rgb>, because pinion's None means "derive from the cell" and passing Some unconditionally would paint every cursor the seed grey; and CursorStyle::Default (CSI 0 SP q) is a RESET, so it is (Block, false) - the sketch had it blinking, which would make a reset SET something. The flake was a history wait clearing on the atomic write's .tmp file rather than on the real one.

R200.decision_summary: R200 = the scrollback front closed, which meant clearing R198's three deferrals under an explicit owner directive to ignore cost and take the long-term-correct option. The find bar gained the regex language as a SEPARATE seam (pane_find_regex, not a mode argument), with the toggle a real pinion CheckboxExternal so it is focusable, AT-named and drivable by intent - testable without pixels - and a rejected pattern showing the engine's own message rather than a bare "no matches". The idle re-encode was killed by Screen::content_epoch, and the sketch that memory carried was REFUTED by revert-proof: an epoch counting only scrollback fails, because encoding covers visible rows too, and the epoch has to live on the SCREEN so an alt-screen app cannot disturb main's. Inline images were restored as Kitty bytes in the SAME .hist file - no second file, no second decoder - placed at the anchor cell by the same walk that emits the text, so no CUP and no dependence on final layout, with SPRAG_RESTORE_IMAGE_BYTES bounding the raster because a screen can hold 256 images of 16 MiB.

R201.decision_summary: R201 = the command palette and per-project config, four slices. A Command is defined ONCE and offered by two surfaces (the palette and the context menu), which is what makes "does this command need a pane?" answerable in one place - needs_pane serves as both the OFFER predicate and the RUN precondition. A project declares its own commands in .sprag.toml, parsed host-side where the policy belongs, and the palette offers them beside the built-ins. The wording split between an anchored menu row and an out-of-context palette row is PRINCIPLED rather than cosmetic: a row the user reached from a pane can say "this pane", a row typed into a search box cannot. A clipboard seam was extracted so a copy path can be asserted at all. The reusable technique this front found: pre-filling an Owner::cache slot IS the injection seam for a test that needs a surface's state without driving its UI.

R202.decision_summary: R202 = destructive commands ask before they act, and the round found a dead code path while proving it. confirm.rs is the ONE guarded door - run_or_arm - that every surface activates through, so "is this destructive?" is answered by the command itself rather than once per surface, and the prompt's WORDING is data on Command. Both client modals are real modal Dialogs, with_modal() is the single AT-confinement mechanism, and the confirm's consequence rides the dialog NAME rather than aria-describedby, because a name is what an AT announces on focus. THE finding: a hand-written emitting External must implement is_dirty or the runtime never drains it - the palette's row-click / RPC path had been DEAD since it landed, and stayed invisible because its unit tests drove the seam DOWNSTREAM of that runtime gate. Roughly ten green tests had passed over a path that could not run. The palette also gained an open verb, which is what made it reachable at all in a headless smoke, since a chord cannot be synthesised there.

R203.decision_summary: R203 = the everything-remaining front, closing four leftover items, and it corrected a false premise that had shaped an entire earlier design. sprag ALREADY kept dead panes - only the child is reaped - so the "no remain-on-exit" assumption R201's front had been built around was simply untrue. With that corrected, a pane whose child exited says so on every surface at once, through the one display-title SSOT. HostClient gained new_pane / kill_pane so the split and kill palette rows have something real to call. A global config.toml lets the user declare commands for every pane, beside the per-project .sprag.toml. And the live headless smoke stopped being a script rewritten from memory each round and became a committed Rust tool, sprag-smoke, which encodes the lavapipe renderer, the three socket variables, the args-key requirement and the paint-vs-state snapshot distinction once.

R204.decision_summary: R204 = the exit-status front: a pane now reports HOW its child ended, not merely that it did. A title shows (exited 101) or (killed: Terminated), with a clean exit and a not-yet-reaped death rendering identically as the bare marker - deliberately, because (exited 0) is noise on the commonest ending there is, and their coinciding makes the reap gap invisible except for a failing command. THE finding is about reaping order: reaping a still-pooled pane makes its pid RECYCLABLE, so every /proc walk that consumes it could stray onto a stranger's process - and window_pids had written the exact fix into a comment before the code existed. Also closed: a doubled filename in the config-error report, and FIVE broken private-doc links where the register had claimed two. The rustdoc gate itself was finally AUTOMATED in the hooks, because nothing had ever run rustdoc, which is precisely how five dead links accumulated unseen.

R205.decision_summary: R205 = the focus / birth-pin / per-session waitFor front, closing three ledger items. THE finding is about WHERE a focus re-seed belongs: pinion drains a focus request only on the DISPATCH that wrote it, never after a paint, so the obvious reconcile_frame rescue would swallow the user's first keystroke. The re-seed belongs on the window / session OPS, after a remap() so pinion's retry can find the tag in a scene that already paints the incoming panes. A frame-hook backstop stays only for the pane-set changes that reach the hook with no dispatch to live in. The daemon binary had already grown an ad-hoc HALF of the birth pin as a bare AtomicBool; that became one owner. scene/waitFor learned to honour the session it is scoped to, and a per-session revision is safe precisely because break_pane and join_pane are Session methods - nothing moves a pane between sessions. Two hangs were fixed at their causes: a pane close refused by an ignored SIGHUP now escalates to SIGKILL on the process GROUP, and a daemon that stops answering no longer freezes the window. The attach-polish resize half closed with NO code - this machine had a real desktop all along.
changes_bullets: a focus re-seed belongs on the window / session OPS, inside their own dispatch
remap() first, so pinion's retry resolves the tag against a scene that paints the new panes
the frame-hook backstop stays only for pane-set changes with no dispatch to live in
one owner for "do not exit mid-birth"; the daemon's ad-hoc AtomicBool half retired
scene/waitFor honours the session it is scoped to; per-session revision
a refused pane close escalates to SIGKILL on the process GROUP instead of hanging
a daemon that stops answering no longer freezes the window (per-connection read deadline)
verification_bullets: gate green; workspace 1103; live smoke 56 checks / 0 fail; 5 revert-proofs
the pane-close hang reproduced ~1 run in 5, then 0/20 after the fix; revert-proof 3/15
SIGHUP is a REQUEST: ignored at delivery it is DISCARDED while kill(2) still returns 0
a per-session revision is safe because break_pane / join_pane are Session methods
carry_forward_bullets: PINION-PR78 written here after an unmeasured claim was challenged; measured 55/1 -> 56/0

R206.decision_summary: R206 = pin 4ff0b35f -> 6099c418, consuming PINION-PR77. SCE step 3 was NOT a no-op this time (9a0a650c -> 201783c4, because pinion R1444 moved its own), and getting that wrong would split SCE into two packages and clash sce_rust_runtime::Engine. PR-77 was delivered as the recommended option (A): the modal mailbox became an ordered queue, so a close-then-open handoff in one frame applies both edits in the order written instead of the Open overwriting the Close. sprag's consumption cost really was 0 lines - palette::run_cursor_row's close()-then-activate order never needed to change, because it was always the intended one. THE finding: when consumption costs no code, the work IS the measurement, and here only a LIVE measurement was possible - a binding can read focus_state::focused() and nothing of the modal stack beneath it, so no unit test can witness the fix, which is exactly why sprag could never have detected the leak either.

PINION-PR77 delivered as recommended option (A): an ordered-queue modal mailbox
sprag consumption cost 0 lines: close()-then-activate was always the intended order
the smoke's reverse ordering constraint was lifted and a stack-cleanliness check put in its place

reverting to 4ff0b35f breaks exactly those 3 checks in the shape the PR predicted

R207.decision_summary: R207 = pin 6099c418 -> c6cdf6a4, taking pinion R1458's frame settle loop. SCE step 3 WAS a no-op this time, checked rather than assumed. Zero break sites: the whole public delta is an added const. The consumption risk was never the build - sprag is exactly the kind of binding that could fail to converge, since a pane-viewport publish drives a PTY resize whose reflow changes the grid the next pass lays out. What makes it safe is that reconcile_frame runs OUTSIDE the loop, so its side effects still happen once per paint and only the pure view repeats; that is the thing to check first on any future bump touching the paint loop. THE finding is about proving a claim with no wire: the settled verdict is shell-owned, so the smoke reads the client's stderr instead, and NON-VACUITY is asserted first (an absent warning is evidence only if a present one would have arrived). The old-pin revert-proof was IMPOSSIBLE here, because the warning did not exist before R1458. Inducing the real condition also FAILED - a temporary counter measured one view pass per frame - so what got proven was the DETECTOR, by planting the warn line and watching exactly that check fail.

a pane_pty test fixed: its child now lives until told to end, so no reap can race the assert

is the MECHANISM, not a reproduction; the fixed form has no window at all

R208.decision_summary: R208 = pin c6cdf6a4 -> c237da6e (pinion R1459-R1462), and the round's finding is that a DELIVERED upstream fix did not fix the symptom. PINION-PR78 landed as R1462 exactly as asked - the two focus drains became one drain_focus_mailboxes applying the modal batch first and the request last - and two sprag comments said the local backstop "retires when PR-78 lands". Rewriting them from that reading would have committed a falsehood. Measured with the backstop disabled, the palette leg still failed 3 runs of 3. A probe printed the cause in one line: ring=Elsewhere occupied=[0] target=None. The pane set was correctly current, refuting a plausible staleness hypothesis; the real defect was that Ring::Elsewhere fused two facts - a live widget holds the caret, and the tag is not a pane - and a DISMISSED palette satisfies the second. A palette row closes before it runs its command, so the op read a ring on a field about to vanish and asked for nothing. There was never a request for the new ordering to order. The fix is a pure classifier, ring_of. R1459's other half put settle_passes and settled on scene/frame_timings, so the settle verdict became data. The round also cleared the citation gate: all 22 SectionMissing turned out to be live pinion sections or a matcher artifact, and the deeper defect was that nothing ran the citation check at all.

R209.decision_summary: R209 = MNEMO-GAP-002 confirmed closed, and the confirmation corrected the report's own recommendation. mnemosyne delivered it as R799 (close the reported slash) plus R800 (generalise to the whole separator class), and rejected sprag's recommended option (A) - closing the section-id charset to digits and dots - for a reason sprag could not see: mnemosyne's OWN store contains a slash-bearing id (code-citation-defense/bidirectional-binding), documented as "kebab + slash slugs" and pinned by a test. Taking (A) would have traded one false SectionMissing for another. The generalisation from a reported instance to its class is the finding worth keeping: R799 closed only `/` while `§1-§3` (a range) is commoner in prose than a slash pair, so the one-character fix was half a fix. Verified here rather than taken on report - the CLI was reinstalled from the committed rev and the original four-line table re-run, plus hyphen and underscore forms that were never in the report. sprag's own gates stayed green under the new validator.

R210.decision_summary: R210 = the two remaining upstream items checked against the live pin, with opposite verdicts. PINION-PR48 is still genuinely open: at pin c237da6e the transport's serve() still hardcodes AtomicBool::new(true) and spawns the accept thread inside the same call, no serve_with_enabled or serve_disabled exists, and sprag-rpc's mount still serves and then sets the boot state - unchanged since the 2026-07-09 filing. Reading the accept loop sharpened the report rather than confirming it: accept() runs BEFORE the enabled check, and the kernel backlog queues connections regardless of the flag, so the exposure window is defined by what sits in the backlog when the loop first turns, not by elapsed microseconds. PINION-PR71 is the opposite. pinion R1405 delivered it on 2026-07-21 and sprag consumed it the same day, so the UPSTREAM OPEN caveat added to §5 one round ago was wrong on the day it was written, not merely stale. The delivered SHAPE is why it could read as open: the owner chose a hover oracle External co-tagged with the grid over a TextGrid paint hook, so pinion-widget-paint carrying no hyperlink code is the delivered design and not the gap - exactly the observation that would invite a re-file. A mechanical census of the doc status banners was attempted and discarded: it matched the undelivered marker inside CLOSED banners, the trap already recorded against this doc set, so both verdicts were taken from live source instead.

R211.decision_summary: R211 = the window "sprag attach" launches was dying with the terminal that ran it, and the measurement is what turned this from a UX preference into a defect. Measured before touching anything, under a real PTY hangup: the window died 5/5 within 0.1s, while the daemon, the session and its window all survived and list-clients came back empty - so this was viewer loss, not work loss, and a re-attach recovered. The cause was isolated by changing exactly ONE thing in an otherwise identical harness: setsid on the spawned child flipped 3/3 dead to 3/3 alive. The fix is that one call, own_session, claiming a session for the child between fork and exec - the same claim sprag-term's daemonize makes as its first act and the same one portable-pty makes for a pane's child, so attach was the THIRD spawn site to need it and the only one that lacked it. tmux is spared this because its client IS the terminal; sprag has two windows, and shutting one was destroying the other. Scope was deliberately held to the defect: whether attach should RETURN instead of blocking - the other half of the old attach-polish ledger item - is untouched and stays an owner decision, because the measurement showed the two halves are independent. The window keeps inherited stdio, so a startup failure still lands where the user is looking, and the CLI still blocks, so a window that dies is still this command's failure; what it gives up is Ctrl-C from the launching terminal.
changes_bullets: sprag.rs: new own_session sets setsid via pre_exec between fork and exec, and attach launches the GUI through it. Its doc carries the measurement, the trade it makes (no job control from the launching terminal) and the two sibling spawn sites that already claim a session.
attach's doc no longer advises "background it with &": that advice was never measured, and with setsid the window's survival no longer depends on it.
sprag-host Cargo.toml: the libc dependency comment now names the CLI's setsid beside the daemon's, so the dependency's reason stays complete.
verification_bullets: Unit test a_launched_window_leads_a_session_of_its_own: the spawned child leads its own session (sid equals its own pid, and differs from this process's). Revert-proof MEASURED, not assumed - removing the pre_exec fails it with left == right == the parent's sid.

Real-path verification after the fix: sprag attach under a PTY hangup survived 4/4 across a 20s watch AND was still an ATTACHED CLIENT per list-clients - alive as a client, not merely undead as a process.
Gates GREEN: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, the rustdoc private-items gate, and workspace tests 1108 passed / 0 failed (was 1107; the one new test).
carry_forward_bullets: Whether sprag attach should return instead of blocking is STILL open and still an owner UX call; setsid closed the defect half without deciding it.
Whether backgrounding with & survives a terminal close was NOT measured; bash forwards SIGHUP to its jobs, so the dropped advice may have been wrong even before this fix.
Ctrl-C in the launching terminal no longer reaches the window - a deliberate behaviour change, the same trade the daemon and the pane children already make.

R212.decision_summary: R212 = attach's remaining half, decided by the owner and built as a CHOICE rather than a new default: blocking stays the default (tmux-faithful, and the reading under which the window's exit status IS the command's), and --no-wait returns once the window is up. The design turned on a measurement rather than a preference. A pure spawn-and-return would have silently dropped the one thing blocking was buying - a window that dies on startup, no display or a broken binary, would exit 0 with a prompt that looks fine - so --no-wait instead returns on the DAEMON having witnessed the window as an attached client. That was affordable only because it was measured: spawn-to-attached runs 0.13-0.22s, far under what a person reads as a pause, so the honest option costs nothing over the naive one. It is also something neither tmux nor cmux can offer, for a structural reason rather than an oversight: it needs a daemon that can see its clients as data plus a client id the launcher can recognise. That recognition forced the second half of the round. The id shape gui-<pid>-<nanos> was minted in sprag-gui and would have been matched by a hardcoded copy in the CLI - two spellings of one wire fact, the exact drift HOST_SOCKET_NAME and SESSION_PARAM are centralised to prevent - so new_gui_client_id and gui_client_prefix moved to sprag-rpc, minted and matched through one definition, with the invariant pinned by a test that can only live where both halves do. Not spelled -d: tmux's attach-session -d means detach every OTHER client, and shadowing that would mislead anyone with the muscle memory.
changes_bullets: sprag.rs: attach parses flags (--no-wait, an unknown argument refused rather than swallowed as the session name) and spawns rather than blocks; new await_window polls the daemon's clients slot for the prefix of the pid it just spawned, with three honest outcomes - attached, exited first (carrying the status, which is the diagnosis), or timed out with the window deliberately left running.

sprag-rpc client.rs: new_gui_client_id and gui_client_prefix, the mint and match halves of the window client id, defined together and re-exported; the trailing dash is load-bearing so pid 123 cannot accept pid 1234's window.
sprag-gui wire.rs: its private new_client_id deleted for the shared one, so the format has one home.
verification_bullets: Live, real GUI: --no-wait returned rc=0 in 0.13-0.24s 4/4 with the window still running and one attached client; the default still blocks (a 5s timeout fired, rc=124); a window that cannot start reports "exited with exit status: 0 before its window attached", rc=1.

Two sprag-rpc unit tests pin the mint/match invariant in the one crate that owns both: a minted id matches this process's prefix, and gui_client_prefix(123) rejects gui-1234-99999 while gui_client_prefix(1234) accepts it.
Two CLI integration tests: a window that exits before attaching FAILS with that diagnosis (not a timeout), and a misspelled flag is an argument error rather than a session name.
Gates GREEN: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, the rustdoc private-items gate, workspace tests 1112 passed / 0 failed (was 1108).
carry_forward_bullets: attach-polish (register item C) is now fully CLOSED: the resize half by measurement, the terminal-kill half at R211, and the block-vs-return half here as a user choice.
The 10s attach timeout is a judgement, not a measurement: it is ~50x the observed 0.13-0.22s to leave room for a cold GPU driver's first-launch shader setup, which was NOT measured on this machine.
--no-wait leaves a timed-out window RUNNING rather than killing it; if that proves confusing, the fix is a clearer message, not a kill, since we spawned it into its own session.
