The unit test had one; the battery printed three Korean syllables and failed. This is exactly why the design asked for a driven battery: a hand-built cell is one I invented, and it agreed with me.

TWO GUARDS, BOTH REVERT-PROVEN, AND THE SECOND PROOF FAILED FIRST. Neutering the width cross-check displaces the cell after an over-wide cluster, as claimed. The orphan-trailer guard's first proof PASSED with the guard removed, because the test put the orphan at column 0 -- where a skipped first cell leaves the run empty and the next cell restarts it at its own absolute column, masking the displacement completely. Moved inside a run, it fails as it should. A test can name the right mechanism and still not touch it.

The width cross-check itself is a guard whose live trigger I could NOT find: a battery of combining sequences, an emoji, a ZWJ family, and two East-Asian ambiguous-width characters all agree between unicode-width and termwiz's tables today. So it is proven against a directly-constructed disagreement rather than a discovered one, and the fidelity assertion -- every cell the projection placed at a column is on the screen at that column -- is checked against the projection's OWN column assignment, so it stays honest if either implementation moves.

Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, rustdoc --document-private-items, workspace 1146 -> 1169 tests passed / 0 failed, live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed. The bin-to-lib doc gate fired again exactly as it did last round, on two public docs linking into module internals; the citation gate refused the commit over two design-document section references written with the section sigil, which is the same near-miss as last round in a new file.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: SLICE 3 IS THE GATE FOR THE WHOLE FRONT and nothing about this slice weakens that: local terminal input decoded to the wire's W3C key vocabulary, resize reaching the host, and a PTY harness that types into a real sprag-tui and reads the child's answer back. This round's live drive is a manual one-shot, which verifies nothing on its own -- it found a defect, which is a different thing from proving an absence.

THE PANE IS NOT RESIZED, DELIBERATELY. A local resize resizes the local surface only, so the view is cropped or margined but never corrupted. A read-only client that resized a pane would be reshaping other clients' windows for a view it cannot type into, and the resize belongs in the slice where both halves can be proven together.

TWO NAMES ARE NOW WRONG AND BOTH ARE OPERATOR-VISIBLE: the shared client reads SPRAG_GUI_HOST_SOCK for the host socket and SPRAG_GUI_SESSION for the session to attach, and a terminal client reading GUI-named variables is the extraction of R224 showing through. A rename needs a compatibility alias and touches the smoke tool, so it is named here rather than done silently.

The client's quit keys -- q and Ctrl-C -- are PROVISIONAL and say so in code. Once keys reach the pane, q belongs to the program running in it, and the client's own commands move behind the fixed prefix table of slice 4. Raw mode is what makes this a decision at all: with the line discipline off, Ctrl-C is a byte rather than a signal.

Still open, unchanged: PINION-PR79, the unattributed dispatch envelope, the unpriced socket, and the version handshake -- which a third client, now a real binary rather than a plan, makes more urgent.

R226.decision_summary: R226: close H1's slice 3, which the design named THE gate for the whole terminal-client front -- local terminal input decoded into the wire's key vocabulary, a window change reaching the pane's pty, and a harness that runs the shipped binary on a real pseudoterminal against a real daemon, types into it, and reads the child's answer back out. All three landed and the gate is green ten runs consecutively. The design's argument for slice 3 was that a client must DECODE and re-encode rather than forward bytes, because the modes that decide a keystroke's encoding -- application cursor keys, the Kitty keyboard protocol, newline mode -- belong to the CHILD and only the host can see them; that argument is now executable as a test rather than stated as a rationale. THE ROUND'S THREE FINDINGS WERE ALL THINGS THE GATE FOUND BY RUNNING, AND ONE OF THEM WAS A DEFECT IN THE SHARED CLIENT THAT PREDATED THIS FRONT. Every resize the terminal client sent was refused whole and silently, because the wire client spelled an unknown cell-pixel metric as an explicit zero and the host's dimension parser accepts only a positive value -- so cols and rows were rejected along with it and the pane stayed the size whoever created it chose. The GUI could never have found it, since a font metric is never zero, and the CLI had always omitted the keys; the wire client was the one caller spelling "unknown" the way the host refuses.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-tui/src/key.rs (new): the inverse of sprag-input's encoder. termwiz KeyCode plus modifiers becomes a W3C KeyboardEvent.key name plus the four modifiers the wire carries, allocation-free (named keys are static strings, a character key's name IS the character and is written into a caller-supplied scratch buffer). Keys the wire cannot spell are None rather than a guess; keys it CAN spell that sprag-input cannot yet encode (F13 upward) are passed through anyway, because naming the key is the client's job and deciding what bytes a name becomes is the host's.

crates/sprag-tui/src/bin/sprag-tui.rs: keys now reach the pane, so the client needs its own way out -- a one-entry prefix table (Ctrl-B then d detaches; Ctrl-B twice types a literal Ctrl-B, tmux's send-prefix). An unbound command key is SWALLOWED rather than delivered, because a user who typed the prefix meant to address the client and their slip must not run in a shell. A window change now resizes both the local surface and the PANE, and attaching does the same reconciliation once, so a session attached over ssh is shaped like the window showing it.

crates/sprag-client/src/wire.rs: resize_args extracted and FIXED -- an unknown cell metric is spelled by OMITTING the two keys, never by sending a zero, which is the shape the CLI always used and the only one the host's opt_dim accepts. A half-known metric is treated as unknown, since a cell has two dimensions and a width with no height describes nothing.

The client no longer captures the user's mouse. termwiz's set_raw_mode enables any-event mouse reporting from the capabilities by default; a client that took click-drag selection and wheel scrolling out of the user's own terminal and then discarded every report was paying a real cost for nothing, so it now asks for capabilities with mouse reporting off. Bracketed paste stays ON and its event is handled -- that arm had been documented as unreachable and was in fact reached.
verification_bullets: THE GATE: crates/sprag-tui/tests/pty_round_trip.rs runs the shipped sprag-tui on a real pseudoterminal against a real sprag-term, and every claim of the front is observed from OUTSIDE every process implementing it. Typing reaches the child and the echo comes back painted -- and because the client is in raw mode its own terminal echoes nothing, so every character found on the screen travelled the whole loop through the daemon. A window change is asserted by asking the DAEMON what size the pane is, never by looking at the screen, because a client that repainted at the new size while leaving the child on the old winsize would look completely correct and break every full-screen program. The prefix detaches and the session outlives it. 5 tests, 10 consecutive runs green, 0 failures.

THE SCREEN IS READ THROUGH A REAL EMULATOR, NOT OFF THE BYTE STREAM. termwiz's surface sends the smallest update it can, so a word typed one letter at a time never appears contiguously on the wire and an assertion on raw bytes would be an assertion about the diffing algorithm. The master's output is fed to sprag's own emulator and the assertions read the resulting SCREEN -- two independent implementations meeting, since termwiz's terminfo renderer writes the sequences and sprag's emulator decides what they mean.

THE DECODER IS PROVEN BY A ROUND TRIP DRIVEN THROUGH THE REAL PARSER, NOT BY A TABLE. bytes -> termwiz InputParser -> wire_key -> sprag_input::encode -> bytes is an identity over everything an ordinary terminal emits. An identity alone proves only non-corruption -- it is also what a byte passthrough would produce -- so two further tests carry the actual claim: the aliases NORMALISE (LF onto CR, BS onto DEL, three spellings of Home onto one), and the same keystroke encodes DIFFERENTLY for a pane under application cursor keys or the Kitty protocol than for one that is not. Revert-proven: mapping one arrow onto its opposite fails both the identity battery and the mode test.

THE RESIZE DEFECT WAS FOUND BY THE GATE AND COULD NOT HAVE BEEN FOUND BY READING. The symptom was a pane that stayed 40x6 while the terminal was 80x24, with a successful-looking client; the cause was one JSON key whose value the host declares invalid. Fixed in the shared client with a unit test that pins absent-versus-zero, and the end-to-end consequence stays in the PTY gate, because a refusal is only observable where something depends on the resize having happened.

THREE OF THE GATE'S FIRST FAILURES WERE ONE MECHANISM AND IT WAS NOT THE CLIENT'S: set_raw_mode sets the termios with TCSAFLUSH, which PURGES the input queue, so a test that typed on the "the daemon counts a client" edge was typing into a void -- the binary attaches BEFORE it takes the terminal, deliberately, so a failure to reach the daemon can be printed on an ordinary screen. A blank screen looked like a paint bug and was a kernel discard. The readiness edge is now "the client has written a byte", which is strictly after the purge, and it was ISOLATED as the load-bearing one: with it alone and the size wait removed, 5 of 5 green.

Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, rustdoc --document-private-items, workspace 1169 -> 1192 tests passed / 0 failed, live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed. The doc gate fired once, on an intra-doc link into a crate that is only a DEV dependency -- resolvable in tests, not in docs.
carry_forward_bullets: SLICE 4 IS MULTI-PANE and it is blocked on a wire action the daemon does not have: split taking a DIRECTION, which is the same gap that makes sprag split-window -h refuse. A TUI user will expect the prefix percent and prefix quote bindings, so whichever front reaches it first should add it.

THE MOUSE PATH EXISTS AND IS NOT WIRED. MOUSE_ACTION carries a semantic event that the host gates against the pane's live tracking mode, so nothing is missing host-side; what is missing is knowing WHICH pane a cell belongs to, which is slice 4's layouter. Until then the client deliberately does not take the mouse from the user's terminal, and a test asserts that through the emulator that received the modes.

TYPE-AHEAD BEFORE THE CLIENT IS UP IS LOST, and it is worth knowing rather than fixing: TCSAFLUSH is what every full-screen program does and it is termwiz's call, but a user typing into an ssh attach while it is still connecting will not see those characters arrive.

THE PREFIX KEY IS A DEFAULT, NOT A DECISION ANYONE CAN CHANGE. Ctrl-B is tmux's and is hard-coded with one binding; H2 is the front that makes keybindings configurable, and the table is shaped so that growing it is additive.

LATEST ATTACH WINS THE PANE'S SIZE. With one client that is simply correct; with several it is a POLICY, and the same one tmux spells window-size latest. The alternatives tmux also offers -- smallest attached client, or a per-client viewport over a larger pane -- need a client-size registry the daemon does not have.

Still open, unchanged: PINION-PR79, the unattributed dispatch envelope, the unpriced socket, the version handshake, and the two operator-visible environment variable names that still say GUI while a terminal client reads them.

R227.decision_summary: R227: build the direction-taking split that the last two rounds each named as the thing blocking them -- H1's multi-pane slice needs it for the prefix percent and prefix quote bindings, and H4's CLI surface had recorded it as the reason sprag split-window -h is refused. THE ROUND'S FINDING IS THAT THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTED UNDER A NAME THAT HID IT. A floated pane docks back where it was because the window captures a memo naming its sibling, which side of it, on which axis, at which share, and re-inserts the leaf there; that memo is not a fact about floating at all, it is a leaf's POSITION, and a directional split is the same position AUTHORED instead of captured. So the split needed no new placement algorithm and no second layout author -- the objection the CLI had written into its own docs against building this, that authoring a tree in the CLI would put a second author beside the GUI's, is answered by adding ZERO authors. The type was renamed from FloatHome to LeafHome to stop the name lying about the two callers it now has, and the operation both reach is one tree method. The one genuine divergence from tmux is forced and is stated where a user meets it: tmux's bare -h splits the CURRENT pane, and sprag's daemon still has no current-pane concept, so the pane is named positionally and asking for a direction without one is refused with the reason rather than guessed at.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-terminal/src/layout.rs: FloatHome renamed to LeafHome, given a beside constructor (the SPLIT author's, beside leaf_home's capturing one), and LayoutTree::split_beside built on the SAME insert_beside a dock-back already used. It removes the pane's leaf before inserting, so a pane an interleaved reconcile already appended MOVES rather than appearing twice, and it refuses a target that holds no leaf or that is the pane itself -- the second guard matters because without it the removal lands and the insertion cannot, losing the pane from the tree.

crates/sprag-terminal/src/registry.rs: Window::split_pane reconciles and then places INSIDE ONE mutable borrow of the window. That is what makes the placement atomic: reconcile_layout is the only other thing that moves a leaf and it needs the same borrow, so nothing can land in between and append the pane behind the split's back. It also means the target is judged against the tiling as it IS rather than as it was when someone last read it.

crates/sprag-host: SPLIT_ACTION on the mux control external takes pane, dir, an optional before, and the whole spawn spec, and answers with the new pane's id. The handler is ordered pre-flight, spawn, place -- the pre-flight so a caller's bad pane id is refused with no child forked, the placement checked again because the spawn needs the workspace lock and the placement the registry's, and this codebase never nests them.

crates/sprag-host/src/bin/sprag.rs: sprag split-window -h PANE / -v PANE / -b divides; naming neither flag nor pane keeps the append it always did. Every refusal names what is missing, and the module docs that said the flags were unsupported now say which HALF of tmux's form is, and why.
verification_bullets: FIVE REVERT-PROOFS, EACH MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Dropping the leaf removal reports the pane TWICE in paint order. Dropping the self-target guard LOSES the pane from the tree entirely. Dropping the reconcile inside split_pane lets a split divide a pane that has already exited -- a ghost leaf nobody had reconciled away. Mapping -v to the wrong axis, and dropping -b on the way to the wire, each fail the CLI's layout assertion. The first three are the two guards and the atomicity claim; the last two exist only because of the gap below.

THE CLI TEST I FIRST WROTE PROVED NOTHING ABOUT DIRECTION AND I CAUGHT IT BEFORE THE GATES, NOT BY THEM. It ran each form, checked the exit and the printed id, and counted panes -- all of which a CLI that mapped -v to horizontal, or silently dropped -b, would pass identically. The wire test proved placement but bypassed the CLI; the CLI test drove the CLI but could not see placement. Closed by having the CLI test read the daemon's own arrangement back over a socket, which is what the two revert-proofs above then measured as load-bearing.

THE PLACEMENT IS ASSERTED THROUGH THE TREE'S RECIPROCAL READER, NOT A SHAPE THE TEST DREW. leaf_home reports where a leaf sits; a home that reads back equal to the one the split authored is the daemon agreeing with the request in the tree's own vocabulary. The discriminator against the append it replaces is the TARGET CHOSEN: three panes with the FIRST divided, because against two panes, or against the last one, beside-the-target and at-the-end are the same position and no assertion could tell the new op from the old.

LIVE, over a real socket against a real sprag-term: a split lands the pane inside the row rather than at its end, on the axis and side named, and an unreachable target is refused with nothing spawned. From the shell, all four forms of the verb reach the daemon and each one's arrangement is read back.
Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, the rustdoc gate, workspace 1192 -> 1202 tests passed / 0 failed, live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed on three consecutive runs.
carry_forward_bullets: H1 SLICE 4 IS UNBLOCKED but not started, and what it still needs is its own: the layouter that says which pane a character cell belongs to. That is the same missing piece that leaves the mouse path unwired, and it is a bigger piece than this action was.

NO HostClient OR WireHost METHOD WAS ADDED, DELIBERATELY. The shared client's split belongs to the slice that has a caller for it; a trait method nothing calls is exactly the shape that let last round's resize defect sit unnoticed in the one client no test exercised end to end. The CLI reaches the action directly, as every other pane verb does.

THE PRE-FLIGHT AND THE PLACEMENT CANNOT BE ONE STEP, so a target that exits between them leaves the pane APPENDED and the id still returned. Killing a shell the user just asked for is the worse answer and the arrangement is readable, so the outcome is reported rather than guessed at -- the same degradation an unhonorable home already takes. It is documented at the handler, not hidden.
SPLIT IS NOT AN MCP TOOL. A sibling agent can read a pane and type into one but still cannot arrange them, which is the same surface gap the debt register records for waiting.

tmux's relative resize forms are STILL unbuilt and this round did not change that: -U/-D/-L/-R move a DIVIDER, which is a different op from dividing a cell, and select-pane remains unbuilt for the current-pane reason restated above.
Still open, unchanged: PINION-PR79, the unattributed dispatch envelope, the unpriced socket, the version handshake, and the two operator-visible environment variable names that still say GUI.

From the shell, all four forms of the verb reach the daemon and each one's arrangement is read back.

R228.decision_summary: R228: H1 slice 4 -- every pane of a session reaches a real terminal, tiled. The design named ROUNDING as the one genuinely new problem in projecting a logical tree onto character cells, and rounding turned out to be the easy half: one function, one clamp, a divider cell taken off the top. WHAT ACTUALLY COST THE CARE IS THAT A PANE'S CELLS AND ITS RECTANGLE ARE TWO AUTHORITIES THAT DISAGREE BY CONSTRUCTION, in both directions, all the time -- the layouter moves a boundary the instant a split lands, and the pane's grid only catches up one poll-wake later, so every frame in between has a buffer that is either smaller than its rectangle or larger. The GUI never had to face this because pixels clip for free and whatever a widget does not cover is painted by the surface beneath it; in character cells there is no beneath, and a cell nobody writes still shows the previous arrangement's content. So the paint half needed three rules the design named none of: blank what the buffer does not reach, clip what runs past the rectangle, and refuse a wide cluster whose second column belongs to the divider. The layouter's exact PARTITION is what makes those rules sufficient rather than approximate -- every cell has exactly one author, so a repaint needs no clear at all. The cursor forced the same lesson from the other side: a terminal has ONE, and Change::Text moves it, so multi-pane turns cursor emission from a detail into a composition rule (last, and by the focused pane only) that a single-pane client could not have distinguished from any other order.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-tui/src/layout.rs (NEW): tile() lays the host's logical tree over a rectangle of character cells. A split reserves ONE cell for its divider and gives the first child floor(remaining * ratio) with the odd cell always on the far side, so the same tree at the same size always yields the same boundary -- a boundary that moved between two identical frames would redraw the whole screen. The panes and the dividers PARTITION the terminal exactly, which is the property the paint half then rests on. A region that cannot give both children a cell and a divider one goes to the first child whole and the second is OMITTED: it has no rectangle, so it is neither painted nor resized, and the pane stays alive.

crates/sprag-tui/src/paint.rs: grid_changes becomes pane_changes(grid, rect) plus a separate cursor_changes(grid, rect), and gains a divider_changes. The rectangle is now the AUTHORITY over the buffer in both directions -- cells the buffer does not reach are blanked, cells past the rectangle are clipped, and a wide cluster that would straddle the right edge is blanked rather than half-drawn because its second column belongs to the divider.

crates/sprag-host + crates/sprag-client: HostClient::split(target, dir, before) with a None default, overridden by WireHost onto R227's SPLIT_ACTION. This is the caller R227 declined to invent one for, and it refreshes BOTH mirrors because a split moves the pane set and the arrangement together.

crates/sprag-tui/src/bin/sprag-tui.rs: the client tiles every pane, sizes each pane's pty to ITS rectangle rather than to the terminal, owns a local focus (the daemon still has no active-pane concept) whose moves are reported to the host as DEC 1004 edges, and grows the prefix table with tmux's percent, quote and o.
verification_bullets: SEVEN REVERT-PROOFS, EACH MEASURED. Removing the divider's reserved cell makes an 81-column even split produce a second half 41 wide starting at column 41 -- a pane running one column past the screen's own edge (ten tests fail; one names the number). Giving the second child the divider's column makes the partition checker report cell (18,0) claimed twice. Dropping the run's origin offset paints the second pane at column 0. Skipping the out-of-buffer blank leaves a planted marker under a pane that no longer covers it. Deleting the wide-cluster edge guard writes a two-column glyph whose trailing half lands in the cell beyond the pane. Dropping the cursor's rectangle bound reports it Visible at (6,0) -- two columns into the pane next door. Resizing panes to the terminal instead of their rectangles leaves both children at 80x24 in a split window.

THE PTY GATE NOW RUNS TWO PANES, and its assertions are made where each claim can only be true one way. The sizes are read from the DAEMON, so a client that tiled its surface correctly while telling both children they still had the whole terminal fails. The divider is read from the SCREEN as a glyph, so percent drawing a horizontal line fails even though it split. Both split keys are tested because neither test alone can catch the two being swapped -- R227 recorded that same gap one layer down.

KEYS FOLLOW FOCUS, PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. After a split, what is typed must NOT reach pane 0, and after prefix o wraps focus back it must. A client that sent every key to the first pane passes the second assertion alone; one that sent them nowhere passes the first.

A SPLIT MADE BY ANOTHER CLIENT RE-TILES THIS ONE, driven over the observer's own connection with nothing typed at the terminal. Reverting the reconcile on the host's change notification leaves the outside pane at the daemon's default 40x6 forever -- the client repaints and never re-tiles.
Flake-checked rather than run once: the PTY suite is 10 green of 10 consecutive runs.
Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets, the rustdoc gate, workspace 1202 -> 1237 tests passed / 0 failed, live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed on three consecutive runs.
carry_forward_bullets: THE MOUSE IS STILL UNWIRED AND IS NOW THE ONLY MISSING WIRE. The semantic MouseInput path exists host-side and the tiling answers which pane a cell belongs to, so both halves are built and neither is connected. The client still asks termwiz NOT to capture the mouse, which is the honest state: a client that captured it and discarded every report would cost the user their own terminal's selection and scrolling for nothing.

DIVIDER JUNCTIONS ARE NOT DRAWN. Where one divider meets another at a T, both keep their straight glyph instead of becoming a box-drawing tee. tmux draws the tee; inferring one means asking what the NEIGHBOURING cells hold, which is a second pass over a partition the drawing function is handed one piece of.

NO PANE IS CLOSED AND NO DIVIDER IS DRAGGED FROM THE CLIENT. Closing is what exit already does and is the verb that would want a confirmation prompt this client has nowhere to draw; dragging needs tmux's relative resize-pane, which the daemon still does not have.

A TERMINAL TOO SMALL FOR THE ARRANGEMENT DROPS PANES rather than scrolling or cropping. The rule is deterministic and documented, the work is never lost, and the alternative -- a per-client viewport over a larger arrangement -- needs the client-size registry the window-size policy also wants.
Slice 5 is what remains of H1: sprag attach --tui chooses this client, and --remote shells out to ssh.
Still open, unchanged: PINION-PR79, the unattributed dispatch envelope, the unpriced socket, the version handshake, and the two operator-visible environment variable names that still say GUI.

R229.decision_summary: R229: bump the pinion pin from R1470 to R1490, which closes the one upstream item sprag had open. Twenty-one commits crossed and NOT ONE BREAK SITE — unusual for a range this size, and the reason the round is worth recording is that a clean build is exactly what makes this kind of bump dangerous. THE FINDING IS THAT A CLEAN CARGO CHECK IS NOT A CLEAN BUMP. Upstream R1478 changed the Unix transport's bind from "unlink the path, then bind" to "bind; on address-in-use, connect first -- reclaim only a path nobody answers on, and refuse to displace a LIVE endpoint". No compile check can see a semantic change to a syscall sequence, and nothing in the workspace failed, so the only way to know whether it mattered was to read the range and trace the reachable paths by hand. It does not matter for sprag, and the reason is worth stating rather than assuming: the daemon takes its single-instance advisory lock and the loser returns BEFORE mount is ever reached, so the new refusal is unreachable and the stale-reclaim path sprag actually depends on is preserved -- the lock decides who serves and the bind can no longer overrule it. But the same change made one of SPRAG'S OWN doc comments false: the endpoint owner's doc asserted that serve "removes the path before binding", a mechanism claim that was true when written and is now not, in a file no line of this bump otherwise touched. A pin bump can falsify a downstream comment without changing a line of downstream code, and the rule about never writing an unverified mechanism into a durable comment has a second half -- a verified one can be invalidated from outside. THE SECOND FINDING IS THAT THE BUMP RITUAL IS ALREADY MACHINE-CHECKED and I re-did it by hand out of habit: a test in sprag-rpc asserts, off the RESOLVED lockfile rather than the manifest, that the whole workspace resolves exactly one pinion revision and exactly one SCE revision, both at full-length hex. One resolved SCE revision IS the shared-instance property observed rather than restated, so the two silent failure modes the ritual exists to prevent are verified, not remembered.
changes_bullets: Cargo.toml: the nine pinion-* workspace dependencies move from 89f39fbd to 38c29df2 (upstream R1470 to R1490). The full SHA was resolved with git rev-parse rather than completed from the short form -- the one place where pattern-completion has already produced a fabricated SHA once in this project's history.

SCE was checked and NOT moved. pinion at the target revision pins scxml-core-engine 201783c4, which sprag already carried, so step three of the bump ritual was a genuine no-op this time. It is checked on every bump regardless, because it is one command and the failure it prevents -- two SCE packages type-clashing through pinion-core's generic widget facade -- is silent.
Cargo.lock: seventeen pinion package revisions, and nothing else. No package added, none removed, no version duplicated, which is the evidence that the range introduced no new transitive dependency.

crates/sprag-rpc/src/lib.rs: the ENDPOINT doc corrected for upstream R1478. The reclaim half of the old claim stayed true and the parenthesised MECHANISM did not, so the doc now states the conditional form, why the refusal is unreachable for the daemon, and where the lock that makes it unreachable is taken -- the two guards named together, at the place where someone reading about one would want the other.
verification_bullets: THE UPSTREAM ITEM IS CLOSED BY DELIVERY, NOT BY ASSERTION. pinion R1480 added IntrospectValue::Raw carrying a RawJson over serde_json's RawValue, plus a raw constructor and an as_raw borrow -- which is PINION-PR79's preferred option almost verbatim, additive, with every existing variant untouched. Read at the target revision's source, in the range's own commit, rather than inferred from the release note. sprag therefore has NO open upstream item again; the previous three rounds each carried PINION-PR79 forward as still open.

THE RANGE WAS READ FOR BEHAVIOUR CHANGES, NOT ONLY FOR BREAK SITES, and two candidates were run down to a negative. The answer-origin work of R1482, R1485 and R1487 puts a surface name beside an answer or a refusal, which would have changed the wire shape every sprag test parses -- it is opt-in, gated on a with_origin request parameter that defaults to false, confirmed by reading the dispatch branch that returns the plain body when it is absent. R1479's self-hosted text arm now declines a family that does not resolve to the one face it holds, which would bite a font-configuring application -- sprag-gui configures no font at all, so it stays on the platform stack. Both checked at the source; a green test run is not evidence about a path the tests do not take.

Gates green: cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean with zero break sites, fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets, the rustdoc gate, workspace 1237 tests passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored across 39 suites, live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed on three consecutive runs.

THE PTY GATE WAS RE-RUN TEN TIMES SPECIFICALLY BECAUSE OF R1478. It is the one suite that binds real sockets against real daemons repeatedly, so it is where a bind-semantics regression would surface if the hand-traced argument above were wrong; ten green of ten runs. A behaviour change that no compile check can see deserves the test that exercises the behaviour, not the test count that happens to be green.

A METHOD ERROR CAUGHT AND CORRECTED MID-ROUND. The first test run was piped through tail, which swallowed twenty-nine of the thirty-nine suites AND owned the pipeline's exit status -- so it reported 294 passed and exit 0, both meaningless, and both looked like a pass. Re-run with the full stream redirected to a file under pipefail to get the real tally and the real exit code. A test count read off a truncated stream, or an exit code read off a pipe's last stage, is not a measurement.
carry_forward_bullets: PINION-PR79 IS DELIVERED BUT NOT CONSUMED, and the distinction is the whole remaining value. sprag's frame encoder still materialises a serde_json Value DOM before the dispatch re-encodes it; the sites the request names are the cells answer and the find and regex arms beside it in the same file. The measured prize is what R222 already priced -- the DOM path was 6.3 to 7.5 times direct encoding -- so the consumption round has its number before it starts.

THE UPSTREAM REGISTER IS NOW EMPTY AND THAT IS A STATE TO NOTICE, not a permanent condition. Every round since R222 carried PINION-PR79 forward; the next round that finds a pinion gap should file it the same way rather than working around it.

A PIN BUMP CAN FALSIFY A DOWNSTREAM COMMENT WITHOUT TOUCHING DOWNSTREAM CODE. One was found this time by reading the range; there is no gate that would have caught it, and a doc comment asserting an upstream mechanism is the shape at risk. Worth a habit rather than a tool: when a bump changes a mechanism, grep the downstream prose that names it.

THE BUMP RITUAL'S HAND-CHECK IS REDUNDANT with crates/sprag-rpc/tests/pins.rs and should stop being re-done. The test is the better witness because it reads the resolved graph rather than the manifest, which is what decides how many copies get linked.
H1 SLICE 5 IS UNCHANGED AND IS WHAT REMAINS OF THE FRONT: sprag attach --tui chooses the terminal client, and --remote shells out to ssh. The mouse wire and H2 keybindings follow it.

Still open, unchanged: the unattributed dispatch envelope, the unpriced socket, the version handshake, and the two operator-visible environment variable names that still say GUI while a terminal client reads them.

R230.decision_summary: R230: consume PINION-PR79. The pin bump one round earlier delivered `IntrospectValue::Raw`, an answer variant carrying JSON TEXT the producer already holds, which `scene/query` splices into the reply instead of walking a tree — so a structural answer is serialized exactly ONCE, where it is produced, rather than built as a `serde_json::Value` for the dispatch to encode a second time. Nine sites, and the request the front exists for went 223.82 us to 79.56 us in a paired before/after on one box, with a reply of IDENTICALLY 9,381 bytes both times. THE ROUND'S FINDING IS THAT ITS OWN INVARIANT MADE IT INVISIBLE TO EVERY TEST THAT EXISTED. The wire bytes do not change — that is the whole safety argument for the change — and the exact consequence is that reverting the entire consumption leaves all 1,237 prior tests green. R231.decision_summary: R231: H1 slice 5, the last of the terminal-client front. `sprag attach --tui` runs sprag-tui in THIS terminal and `sprag attach --remote HOST` runs it on HOST over ssh, so the client built across slices 1-4 is finally reachable the way a user reaches it. THE ROUND'S FINDING IS THAT THE DESIGN NAMED A GATE THAT COULD NOT SEE THE CHANGE. DESIGN-H1 verified this slice with the CLI's own harness and a stand-in ssh, which pins the flag parse and the exported environment and is blind to the LAUNCH MECHANISM — a stand-in that prints and exits is equally happy in any process group, any session, with or without a controlling terminal. The claim that actually needed proving is that `own_session`, correct for the window client and the only launch this CLI had, makes a terminal client IMPOSSIBLE: setsid leaves the child with no controlling terminal, and a terminal client acquires its terminal by opening /dev/tty, which is precisely the name for the one it no longer has. Measured in a single real pty, both arms: direct, the client takes the terminal; through setsid, `No such device or address (os error 6)` on its very first line. So the terminal client is EXEC'd where the window client is spawned, and the gate for it had to be the PTY harness of another package. THE SECOND FINDING IS THAT THE MECHANISM WRITTEN DOWN FIRST WAS THE WRONG ONE. The doc claimed SIGWINCH — true, and never reached, because the client dies before it can care — and what exposed it was the revert-proof failing EARLIER than predicted, at the attach rather than at the resize.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-host/src/bin/sprag.rs: `attach` gains `--tui` and `--remote HOST`, and the parse gains one refusal. `--tui` resolves `SPRAG_TUI_BIN` (a new override beside the GUI's, through a shared `client_bin` the two now split) and EXECS `sprag-tui` with the same `SPRAG_GUI_SESSION` + `SPRAG_GUI_HOST_SOCK` the window client is handed. `--remote` builds `ssh -t DEST sprag attach --tui NAME` through `SshTarget::ssh_argv` — the same author `sprag ssh` uses, so the `-t` and the `user@` split are not re-spelled — and execs it BEFORE any local connection is opened. `--no-wait` is refused by name with either.

The new `exec_client` returns `io::Error` rather than `io::Result`, because `CommandExt::exec` comes back only on failure: on success there is no process left to return into. `attach_remote` is a sibling function so the remote argv has one author and one doc.

crates/sprag-host/tests/cli.rs: four tests over the real socket. `--tui` pre-flights and launches the terminal client with the session env (a `/usr/bin/env` stand-in prints it), with `SPRAG_GUI_BIN` pointed at `/bin/false` so a pass cannot be produced by launching the wrong client; `--no-wait` refused; `--remote` recording an EXACT argv sequence with no daemon spawned at all; `--remote` with no host.

crates/sprag-tui/tests/pty_round_trip.rs: the launcher is split (`Tui::attach` / `Tui::attach_via_cli` over a shared `start`) and `attached_client` parameterised by it, so one new test drives a client the CLI launched, on a real pseudoterminal, and resizes its window.
verification_bullets: THE MECHANISM CLAIM WAS MEASURED IN ONE REAL PTY, BOTH ARMS, AND IT CORRECTED THE DOC THAT HAD ALREADY BEEN WRITTEN. Run directly, the client takes the terminal (it emits its cursor sequences); run through `setsid`, it prints `No such device or address (os error 6)` on its FIRST line, having connected to nothing. ENXIO, from `open("/dev/tty")` inside termwiz's `SystemTerminal::new`.

FIVE REVERT-PROOFS, EACH MEASURED. Giving the terminal client the window client's `own_session` spawn: the PTY test fails at its FIRST wait — `0 attached clients` for the whole 15s deadline — not at the resize, because the client dies before it can connect. Moving the `--remote` dispatch below the pre-flight: `sprag: no server running at /tmp/sprag-cli-it-...`, a remote attach refused for the state of a machine it has nothing to do with. Resolving the launch through `SPRAG_GUI_BIN` whatever the flag says: exit 1 with NOTHING on either stream, because after `exec` there is no CLI left to say what it launched. Dropping `--tui` from the remote argv: the recorded sequence is `-t me@server sprag attach ghost`. Removing the `--no-wait` refusal: the flag is silently accepted and the client exec'd anyway.

THE `--remote` TEST SPAWNS NO DAEMON AT ALL and names a session that exists nowhere, so reaching the recorded argv IS the proof that nothing local was consulted; it also asserts the socket file was never created. The argv is compared as an exact SEQUENCE, because `sprag attach --tui ghost` and `sprag --tui attach ghost` carry the same tokens and only one is a command.
Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets, the rustdoc gate, workspace 1241 -> 1246 tests passed / 0 failed. The PTY suite ran 10 consecutive green runs.

The live GUI pixel smoke ran TEN times: nine at 88 passed / 0 failed, and ONE at 81 / 1. Reported as measured rather than retried away. It is not reachable from this change (the smoke spawns the GUI directly and uses exactly one CLI verb, `rename-window`), and the failing check is diagnosed below.
carry_forward_bullets: THE DESIGN NAMED THE WRONG GATE FOR THIS SLICE, AND THE PATTERN IS THE ROUND'S FINDING. DESIGN-H1 §7 verified slice 5 with "the existing cli.rs harness, with a stand-in ssh" — which can see the flag parse and the exported env and CANNOT see the launch MECHANISM, because a stand-in that prints and exits is happy in any process group, any session, with or without a controlling terminal. The claim that needed proving is that `own_session` — correct for the window client, and the only launch this CLI had — makes the terminal client IMPOSSIBLE. Only a real terminal can witness that, so the gate had to be the PTY harness of another package. WHEN A CHANGE IS ABOUT THE ENVIRONMENT A PROCESS IS LAUNCHED INTO, A STAND-IN PROCESS IS THE ONE THING THAT CANNOT TEST IT.

THE MECHANISM I WROTE DOWN FIRST WAS THE WRONG ONE, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAID SO. The doc claimed SIGWINCH: the kernel delivers it to the foreground process group of the tty, so a `setsid` client would never hear a resize. True, and NOT what happens — the client never reaches the point of caring, because it acquires its terminal by opening `/dev/tty`, the name for the controlling terminal it no longer has. The revert-proof failed at the FIRST wait rather than the resize, which is what exposed it. A prediction that fails EARLIER than expected is evidence about the mechanism, not noise to route around.

THE GUI PIXEL SMOKE HAS A ONE-IN-TEN FAILURE THAT MISNAMES ITSELF, AND IT IS NOT THIS CHANGE'S. `Smoke::tags` swallows a failed `scene/snapshot` into an EMPTY map with `if let Ok(..)`, so "the RPC did not answer" and "the client painted nothing" are the same value downstream. The check that consumed it then reported `daemon [5], painted []` as a pane-correspondence disagreement. It is also a single sample where every other wait in that file polls the condition it reads. Two defects, one line apart, in the project's own gate.

Still open, unchanged by this round: the version handshake (a stale remote `sprag-tui` against an updated daemon is exactly the skew nothing negotiates, and `--remote` now makes that arrangement one flag away), the unpriced socket, and the two operator-visible environment variables that still say GUI while two clients read them.

H1 IS CLOSED. What remains of the terminal client is the MOUSE wire — `MouseInput` exists host-side and `Tiling` answers which pane a cell is, and neither is connected to the other — and then H2, keybindings, which owns the prefix table this client currently hardcodes.

Two defects, one line apart, in the project's own gate.

Still open, unchanged by this round: the version handshake (a stale remote `sprag-tui` against an updated daemon is exactly the skew nothing negotiates, and `--remote` now makes that arrangement one flag away), the unpriced socket, and the two operator-visible environment variables that still say GUI while two clients read them.

H1 IS CLOSED. What remains of the terminal client is the MOUSE wire — `MouseInput` exists host-side and `Tiling` answers which pane a cell is, and neither is connected to the other — and then H2, keybindings, which owns the prefix table this client currently hardcodes.

R232.decision_summary: R232: the project's own pixel gate could not tell a transport failure from an empty screen. `Smoke::tags` wrapped its `scene/snapshot` in `if let Ok(..) { walk } out`, so an unanswered call and a client painting nothing were the SAME VALUE for every reader downstream — and the two are opposite diagnoses. It produced both of the failure modes a swallowed error can produce. The visible one was a false FAILURE, about one run in ten, where a check reported `painted []` as a pane-correspondence disagreement; the hidden one was a false PASS, because `the palette starts unpainted` is spelled `!contains_key` and an empty map satisfies it whatever the reason for the emptiness. The fix is to make the five painted-tree readers return `Result` and to let the TYPE force each of twenty-three call sites to say which meaning it wants: inside a wait an unreadable tree is honestly not-yet and the next poll re-asks; in an assertion it is a failure that names itself. The one check that sampled a settling pane set once now waits for it. Measured as a PAIRED plant, both arms of a post-boot transport failure: with the swallow the palette assertion PASSES and the pane check says `Ok([])`; with the propagation it FAILS and the pane check says `Err("scene/snapshot: planted transport failure")`. Found while gating R231, whose change could not reach it.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-gui/src/bin/sprag-smoke.rs: the five painted-tree readers — `tags`, `docked_panes`, `pane_count`, `tabs`, `pane_rows` — return `Result` instead of defaulting. `tags` was the source: it wrapped `scene/snapshot` in `if let Ok(..) { walk } out`, so a failed call and an empty tree were the same value everywhere downstream, and the four derived readers inherited it.

All twenty-three call sites now STATE which meaning they want, and the type is what forces the statement. Inside a `wait_for` closure an unreadable tree is honestly not-yet (`.ok()?`, and the next poll re-asks); in a one-shot assertion it is `is_ok_and`, which fails rather than defaults; where a value is a baseline for later deltas it is `let Ok(..) else` with a check of its own.

`check_terminal_output_never_reaches_the_shaper` WAITS for the daemon and the client to agree on one pane instead of sampling the painted set once. Its failure message re-reads the tree so the diagnostic carries what was finally there, error included, rather than a bare empty list.
verification_bullets: THE PAIRED MEASUREMENT, ONE PLANT AND TWO ARMS. A planted post-boot `scene/snapshot` failure (a flag flipped the instant boot returns, so the transport dies exactly where a real one would and boot's own guard cannot absorb it). With the swallow restored — literally `Ok(HashMap::new())`, what the old code did — "the palette starts unpainted" **PASSES** and the pane check reports `painted Ok([])`. With the propagation, the same plant makes that check **FAIL** and the pane check reports `painted Err("scene/snapshot: planted transport failure")`. The false pass is the finding: an assertion spelled `!contains_key` is satisfied by a map that is empty because nothing answered.

THE FLAKE IS GONE BY COUNT, AND THE COUNT IS STATED WITH ITS STRENGTH. Before: one failure in ten runs (`daemon [5], painted []`). After: TWENTY consecutive clean runs at 88 passed / 0 failed. Against a one-in-ten prior that is meaningful and not conclusive — about a one-in-eight chance of twenty clean runs if nothing had changed — so the paired plant above, not the streak, is what carries the claim.

A REGRESSION THE SMOKE CAUGHT ON ITS FIRST RUN, WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT COMPILES. `Result` has an `iter` of zero-or-one, so changing a `Vec<String>` accessor to `Result<Vec<String>, _>` silently retargets `pane_rows(i).iter().any(|row| row.contains(&line))` from "any ROW contains the line" (a substring test on `str`) to "the row LIST equals the line" (an element test on `Vec`). It type-checks, and the grid check failed with `Ok(Null)` on the first run. Fixed to `is_ok_and(|rows| rows.iter()..)` and commented where it sits.
Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets, the rustdoc gate, workspace 1246 tests passed / 0 failed.
carry_forward_bullets: A SWALLOWED ERROR PRODUCES BOTH FAILURE MODES, AND THE FALSE PASS IS THE ONE THAT HIDES. The same single line gave a false FAILURE about one run in ten, which is what got it noticed, and a false PASS on an assertion that had been reporting green over a dead socket for as long as it existed. The visible symptom was the cheaper of the two, and chasing only it would have left the other in place.

THE TYPE IS WHAT KEEPS THIS FIXED. Nothing stops a future reader from writing `.unwrap_or_default()`, but it cannot be written by ACCIDENT, and every one of the twenty-three sites now records at the call whether an unreadable tree means retry or means failure. That distinction is invisible when the reader defaults for you.

CHANGING A COLLECTION RETURN INTO A `Result` CAN CHANGE THE MEANING OF A CHAIN THAT STILL COMPILES. `Result::iter` yields the Ok value, so `.iter().any(..)` keeps type-checking and starts asking a different question one level up. Audit `.iter()`, `.len()`, `.contains()` and `.first()` at every site of such a conversion; the compiler will not.
Still open, unchanged: the version handshake, the unpriced socket, and the two operator-visible environment variables that still say GUI while two clients read them.

R233.decision_summary: R233: the mouse wire, the last unconnected half of the terminal client. A semantic `MouseInput` and a tiling that could name the pane under a cell had both existed since R228 with nothing joining them; this joins them. THE ROUND'S FINDING IS THAT TWO OF ITS FIVE REVERT-PROOFS PASSED, and each pass named a gate that could not see the thing it was written for. Forwarding the SCREEN cell instead of the pane-local one left every test green, because a single-pane client's only pane starts at the origin — where the two coordinate spaces are the same numbers — so the translation is invisible until a second pane exists. And handing a divider cell to a pane passed because the natural wrong target is the pane on the divider's LEFT, which was not tracking, so the HOST's own mode gate discarded the misdirected report before any assertion could reach it: two correct filters in series make the first unobservable. Both gaps were closed by building the arrangement that can see them — a two-pane gate, and a fixture in which both panes track — and only then did the reverts measure red. The design's own half is that the local terminal's tracking level is a MIRROR of what the panes' children have asked for rather than a preference of the client's: tmux needs a `mouse` option because it cannot know, and sprag's host already carries each pane's level on the wire, so the client reproduces exactly what would have happened had the child been running in this terminal directly.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-tui/src/mouse.rs (NEW): `MouseEdges`, the one input path in this client that is not a pure function of its argument. termwiz reports a STATE (where the pointer is, which buttons are down) because that is what an SGR report says without memory; the wire carries an EDGE, which only a decoder remembering the previous state can produce. Coordinates arrive 1-based by protocol and leave 0-based, once. Seven unit tests.

crates/sprag-tui/src/layout.rs: `Tiling::pane_at(col, row)` — the inverse of the module, answering which pane owns a screen cell AND where that cell is inside it. Unambiguous because the tiling is an exact partition, the same property that lets a repaint skip clearing.

crates/sprag-tui/src/bin/sprag-tui.rs: `MouseMirror` — the local terminal's tracking level is kept a MIRROR of the maximum any pane's child has asked for, so a user in a plain shell keeps their emulator's own selection and wheel, and an editor that asks for tracking gets exactly what it asked for. The client opens `/dev/tty` ITSELF and keeps the handle, because `Terminal` has no way to change mouse reporting after construction and `Change::Text` renders control characters inert by contract; `new_with` is the documented seam for it. The event loop forwards each edge to the pane under the pointer in that pane's own coordinates, and a PRESS also moves the keyboard focus there.

crates/sprag-tui/Cargo.toml: sprag-vt promoted out of [dev-dependencies]. `MouseProtocol` is already a public type of the HostClient protocol (`pane_mouse_protocol` answers with it), so this is a direct use of something already in the tree, and a production `use` from a dev-only dependency does not build.
crates/sprag-tui/tests/pty_round_trip.rs: four new gates over a real pseudoterminal, plus `MOUSE_CHILD`, a fixture whose child asks for tracking and renders what it receives.
verification_bullets: THE CHAIN IS PROVEN END TO END, EVERY LINK REAL: an SGR report written to the pty master, termwiz's parser, the edge decoder, the pane under the cell, the wire's `mouse` action, the host's mode gate, `encode_mouse`, the pane's PTY, the child. What comes back is read off the pane's text as the DAEMON holds it, so nothing about the client's painting can make it pass. The coordinates ROUND TRIP — in 1-based, carried 0-based, encoded 1-based — so the numbers that come back must be the numbers that went in.

FIVE REVERT-PROOFS, AND TWO OF THEM PASSED, WHICH IS WHAT THE ROUND IS ABOUT. Forwarding the SCREEN cell instead of the pane-local one PASSED the single-pane gate and every other test in the file, because the only pane a single-pane client has starts at the origin where the two coordinate spaces are the same numbers; a two-pane gate was written for it and then measured the child receiving column 45 instead of its own column 5. Handing a divider cell to the first pane PASSED too, because the natural wrong target is the pane on the divider's LEFT and that pane was not tracking, so the host's gate discarded the misdirected report before any test could see it — the fixture was changed to make BOTH panes track, and then measured `^[[<0;40;3M` arriving at a pane 40 columns wide.

THE OTHER THREE MEASURED RED FIRST TIME. Never mirroring: all four mouse tests fail at `mouse_protocol: None` — the terminal never reports, so nothing is ever sent. Dropping the 1-based to 0-based conversion: the unit test reads `(1, 1)` for the terminal's first cell, and the child receives `^[[<0;5;4M` for a click sent at `4;3`. Letting the wheel bits take part in the state diff: PASSED, and the doc claiming that mask was what prevented a phantom wheel release is corrected below.

THE FIXTURE ITSELF TAUGHT TWO THINGS, BOTH MEASURED. A pane's PTY starts CANONICAL, so the line discipline holds a mouse report — which has no newline — until one arrives: the first click test only passed with a `\r` typed after it, and that is what proved the rest of the chain was already working before the fixture was right. And sending two presses with movement between them and no release made the child receive button 32, a DRAG, which is exactly what that sequence means: the decoder was right and the test was sending something no terminal sends.

Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets, the rustdoc gate, workspace 1246 -> 1259 tests passed / 0 failed, the GPU-free gate, the PTY suite 10 consecutive green runs, live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed on three consecutive runs.
carry_forward_bullets: A COORDINATE TRANSLATION IS UNTESTABLE IN THE ARRANGEMENT THAT MOTIVATES THE FEATURE. The pane a single-pane client shows begins at the origin, so screen and pane coordinates are the same numbers there and the subtraction is invisible; the first arrangement that can see it is the second pane. The unit test on the mapping function did not help either, because the defect was in the CALLER's use of it. Generalises: when a change introduces a coordinate space, the gate has to be an arrangement where the two spaces disagree, and that arrangement is usually not the simplest one.

A DOWNSTREAM GATE HIDES AN UPSTREAM DEFECT WHEN IT DISCARDS THE SAME THING. The divider guard was unprovable while the pane beside it was not tracking, because the host's own mode gate dropped the misdirected report first. Two correct filters in series make the first one unobservable — the test had to remove the second (both panes tracking) before the first could be measured at all.

THE MECHANISM I WROTE DOWN WAS AGAIN NOT THE ONE HOLDING THE PROPERTY UP. The wheel mask was documented as what prevents a phantom `WheelUp` release; removing it leaves every test green, because what actually prevents it is the three-entry button table — a bit with no entry cannot produce an edge in either direction. The mask is kept for the narrower reason that it makes the remembered held-set mean what its name says, and the doc now says that instead. Same shape as R231's `/dev/tty` correction, one round later.

THE LOCAL TERMINAL'S MOUSE MODE IS A MIRROR, NOT A PREFERENCE, AND THAT IS WHY IT NEEDED NO OPTION. tmux has a `mouse on/off` option because tmux cannot know whether the program in a pane wants the pointer; sprag's host already carries each pane's tracking level on the wire, so the client can reproduce exactly what would have happened had the child been running in this terminal directly. The level is mirrored too, not just the on-off: capturing at any-event for a pane that asked for button-event would put a wire message on every pointer movement for the host to discard, which over ssh is the whole cost of the feature for none of its value.

Deliberately not built: the HORIZONTAL wheel (xterm's buttons 6/7) has no `MouseButton` to become, and inventing one here would mean encoding a report the host cannot describe — the honest fix is a variant in sprag-input with an encoder arm beside it. No divider drag, which needs a relative `resize-pane` the daemon does not have. Still open and unchanged: the version handshake, the unpriced socket, and the two operator-visible environment variables that still say GUI while two clients read them.

R234.decision_summary: R234: the two things R233 listed as deliberately not done, built. Neither reason survived being checked. The HORIZONTAL WHEEL needed a `MouseButton` variant in sprag's own input crate and an encoder arm beside the vertical pair — a change to sprag's shared vocabulary, not an upstream gap. The DIVIDER DRAG needed nothing new at all: `SplitId` has been on the layout wire since it was written, and that module's own docs say a client 'keys its live drag ratio on them', so the mechanism was waiting for the client that needed it. The note claiming otherwise came from R228 and was repeated by R233 without being re-read. THE ROUND'S FINDING IS ABOUT WHERE A GESTURE'S END IS ASSERTED. Claiming the divider on every event rather than on the press passes every assertion about the drag — the boundary moves, both children resize, the line repaints — because what it breaks happens afterwards: by the time the release arrives the divider has moved under the pointer, so the release re-claims the drag instead of ending it and every later click is swallowed. Only doing the next thing the gesture was blocking can see that, which is what the test now does.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-input/src/lib.rs: `MouseButton::WheelLeft` / `WheelRight`, xterm's pseudo-buttons 66 and 67, with encoder arms beside the vertical pair. The doc states plainly that the NAMES are a reading and the report is not: a client observes its own terminal's direction flag and the encoder reproduces the same button number, so a swapped name would be a wrong label in that file and never a wrong report at a child.
crates/sprag-host/src/pane.rs + crates/sprag-client/src/wire.rs: `wheelleft` / `wheelright` on the wire, both directions of the same vocabulary.
crates/sprag-tui/src/mouse.rs: the horizontal axis read from the SAME direction flag as the vertical one, so neither this module nor the encoder decides what "left" means.

crates/sprag-tui/src/layout.rs: `Divider` gains the split's `SplitId` and the `region` it divides — identity, because the tree is re-read every frame and an index into it means a different node the moment anything splits. `Divider::ratio_at` is the INVERSE of the layouter's division rather than a fraction of the region, which is what makes a drag track the pointer instead of drifting a cell at a time; `with_ratio` edits one split by identity and answers `None` when the tree does not carry it.

crates/sprag-tui/src/bin/sprag-tui.rs: a press on a divider CLAIMS a drag, the moves that follow rewrite that split's ratio through `set_layout`, and the release ends it. The write is guarded by the host's revision and the client re-tiles from what the host ANSWERS, so a refused write and an accepted one are handled by the same line.
verification_bullets: FOUR REVERT-PROOFS, AND ONE OF THEM PASSED TWICE BEFORE THE GATE COULD SEE IT. Recognising the divider on every event instead of claiming it on the press passed the whole drag test: the boundary moved, both children were resized, the line was repainted. What it broke is invisible from there — by the time the RELEASE arrives the divider has moved under the pointer, so the release re-claims the drag instead of ending it and the client swallows every click afterwards. The test was extended with a click AFTER the drag, and only then did the revert measure `pane 0 holds ""`.

The other three measured red first time. Encoding a horizontal notch as a vertical one: the unit test reads `WheelUp` for `WheelLeft`, and the child receives `^[[<64;7;5M` twice — the second notch indistinguishable from the first. (The remaining two are R233's, re-run green.)

THE RATIO IS ASSERTED BY ROUND TRIP, NOT AGAINST A NUMBER. Every reachable column of a 21-cell region is dragged to and re-tiled, and the divider must land on the column asked for; a ratio is "correct" until you ask where it puts the line, so the number alone would assert nothing. The clamp is asserted at both ends: a drag off either edge stops at the last arrangement that is still two panes.

THE DRAG REACHES THE CHILDREN'S PTYs, asked of the DAEMON rather than read off the screen — the same distinction the window-change test exists for, one gesture down. A client that redrew the line in a new column while leaving both children on their old winsize fails there.

Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets, the rustdoc gate, workspace 1259 -> 1265 tests passed / 0 failed, the GPU-free gate, the PTY suite 10 consecutive green runs, live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed on three consecutive runs.
carry_forward_bullets: A GESTURE'S END IS A SEPARATE CLAIM FROM ITS EFFECT, AND ONLY THE NEXT ACTION CAN ASSERT IT. Every assertion about the drag itself — the boundary, the children's sizes, the repainted line — passed with a client that never let go. The defect lives entirely in what happens AFTERWARDS, so the test had to keep going: do the thing the gesture was blocking, and see it work. Generalises to any modal state a client enters on one input and leaves on another.

A CLAIM COPIED FROM A MEMORY IS NOT A VERIFIED CLAIM. R228 recorded "no divider drag — it needs tmux's relative `resize-pane`, which is unbuilt", and R233 repeated it. It was never true: `SplitId` has been on the wire the whole time and the layout module's own docs say a client "keys its live drag ratio on them", so the path existed before the client that needed it. The cost of the wrong note was one round of the feature not being built. Re-read the seam before recording that something is blocked.

SCOPE CUT FOR SIZE IS STILL A SCOPE CUT. Both of these were listed as "deliberately not done" with reasons that read as principled and were not: the horizontal wheel needed a variant in sprag's OWN crate, and the divider drag needed nothing at all. Neither was an upstream gap and neither was hard. The project's own rule is to default a cost-versus-correctness fork to the long-term-correct target and phase it, never to recommend the truncated one — and a "deliberately not done" list is exactly where that rule gets quietly broken.

Still open and unchanged: the version handshake, the unpriced socket, and the two operator-visible environment variables that still say GUI while two clients read them. Nothing about the mouse remains unbuilt in this client.

R235.decision_summary: R235: H2 slice 1 — the prefix table stops being a `match` in a binary and becomes the user's keymap. `config.toml` grows `[keys]` / `[[bind]]` / `[[unbind]]`, a binding names a TYPED action parsed from the same string the shell takes (`split-window -h`, `detach-client`), and `sprag-tui` spells none of its own bindings any more. THE ROUND'S FINDING IS THAT A COMPLETE, SELF-CONSISTENT DESIGN STILL SHIPPED A HOLE THAT ONE LINE OF LIVE OUTPUT EXPOSED. Every unit test passed, every revert-proof measured red, and the first `sprag list-keys` against a real config printed `prefix C-a` above `bind-key -T prefix C-b send-prefix` — the self-send stranded on the abandoned key, so `prefix prefix` did nothing and the one way to type the prefix into a pane was gone. No test could have caught it, because the tests asserted the table the design described and the table was the thing that was wrong: `send-prefix` on the prefix key is not an independent choice of key, it is a statement about WHICHEVER key the prefix is, so it has to follow. tmux has exactly this hole and papers over it with a convention (`bind C-a send-prefix` as a remembered second step); sprag models the prefix as a field rather than a server option, so it can simply be right. The second finding is a method one and worse: `.githooks/doc-gate.sh` defines a shell FUNCTION and is meant to be sourced, so running it directly does nothing and prints nothing — I read that silence as a passing gate, and the commit hook then failed on a doc link to a private item that had been there the whole time.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-host/src/keymap.rs (NEW): `KeySpec` (tmux's `C-` / `^` / `S-` / `M-` modifier prefixes, verified against `man tmux` on this box, plus sprag's own `Super-`), `BoundAction` (`detach-client`, `send-prefix`, `split-window -h|-v [-b]`, `select-pane -t :.+`), and `Keymap` — whose `default()` IS tmux 3.2a's table as `tmux list-keys -T prefix` prints it. Modifiers match EXACTLY, which turns the old hardcoded rule "a command key with a modifier on it is a slip" into a consequence and makes `C-o` bindable, which that rule could not express at all. `set_prefix` moves a `send-prefix` sitting on the old prefix onto the new one; nothing else follows.

crates/sprag-input/src/lib.rs: `NAMED_KEYS` + `is_key_name` — the wire's key-name vocabulary as one public list. It had been split between a producer (`sprag-tui`'s decoder) and a consumer (`encode`) with nothing shared, and a config that binds by NAME is a third reader that must refuse a name nothing can produce. Deliberately WIDER than what `encode` accepts: `F13` upward name a key a client can bind and no PTY can receive.

crates/sprag-host/src/config.rs: `[keys]` / `[[bind]]` / `[[unbind]]` and a `keymap()` reader beside `load()`. TWO readers over ONE file shape, because `UserConfig` is a wire DTO that crosses to the palette and a keybinding must not: a keymap is what one client does with one keyboard. A key both bound and unbound in one file is REFUSED rather than resolved by precedence.

crates/sprag-tui/src/bin/sprag-tui.rs: `command()` routes through the keymap, `PREFIX_KEY` and `is_prefix` are gone, and the config is read FIRST — before the daemon is reached and long before the terminal is taken, so a typo is a message on a screen that still works. `send-prefix` sends the PREFIX read off the keymap, not the key that triggered it.

crates/sprag-host/src/bin/sprag.rs: `sprag list-keys`, printing tmux's own `bind-key -T prefix KEY COMMAND` shape. The one verb here that needs NO daemon, which is the point rather than a convenience: tmux must start a server to answer the same question, and a user editing their config has none running.
verification_bullets: THE GATE IS A PTY TEST WITH A REAL `config.toml`, because every other test hands `command()` a keymap and therefore proves the routing while saying nothing about whether `run()` ever reads a file — the seam where the whole feature can be absent with every unit test green. Its discriminating assertion is the FIRST one, not the last: with `prefix = "C-a"` declared, typing `C-b` then `d` must reach the pane and paint. REVERT MEASURED: replace the config read with `Keymap::default()` and the observation is `client: EXITED ExitStatus { code: 0 }` over a blank screen — the binary took `C-b` as its prefix and detached.

THE DEFECT THIS ROUND IS ABOUT WAS FOUND BY RUNNING THE TOOL, NOT BY A TEST. `sprag list-keys` against a hand-written config printed the self-send still bound to `C-b` after the prefix moved to `C-a`. Now covered three ways — the self-send follows, a USER's own binding on the old prefix key does NOT follow, and moving onto an occupied key replaces it — and the revert (assign the prefix alone) fails two of the three.

FOUR MORE REVERT-PROOFS, ALL MEASURED RED. Dropping the "a prefix is only a prefix when a key follows it" guard makes `"^"` parse as Ctrl-nothing, so the caret key becomes a config error. Comparing names without modifiers makes `Ctrl-D` detach — the case the hardcoded table needed a special rule for. Removing `keys`/`bind`/`unbind` from the file shape makes `deny_unknown_fields` reject the WHOLE file, i.e. rebinding one key silently empties the user's command palette. Deleting one name from `NAMED_KEYS` fails the cross-crate drift guard with `PageDown decodes to "PageDown", which no config could bind`.

A DRIFT GUARD IN EACH DIRECTION, because the two tables sit on either side of a crate boundary where neither crate's own tests can see the other. In `sprag-input`: the vocabulary exceeds the encoder by EXACTLY F13-F24, asserted as an equality so it fails from either side. In `sprag-tui`: every name the decoder can produce is accepted by the vocabulary, enumerated over KeyCodes rather than over names so a new decoder arm is covered as soon as its code is listed.

Gates green: fmt, clippy --workspace --all-targets, the rustdoc gate (RUN PROPERLY THIS TIME — see the carry-forward), workspace 1265 -> 1299 tests passed / 0 failed, the GPU-free gate, the PTY suite 10 consecutive green runs, live GUI pixel smoke 88 passed / 0 failed on three consecutive runs.
carry_forward_bullets: A DESIGN CAN BE COMPLETE, CONSISTENT, AND FULLY TESTED AND STILL BE WRONG ABOUT WHAT IT MODELS. Nothing was missing from the keymap design; the defect was that it treated `send-prefix`'s KEY as an independent choice when it is a function of the prefix. Tests written from a design cannot find that, because they assert the design. What found it was printing the artefact and reading it — one line of `list-keys` output. Generalises: after building a thing that has a rendering, RENDER IT AND READ IT, before believing the tests.

A GATE THAT PRINTS NOTHING ON SUCCESS IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A GATE THAT DID NOT RUN. `.githooks/doc-gate.sh` defines a function for pre-commit to source; `bash .githooks/doc-gate.sh` executes zero commands and exits 0. I recorded it as clean and it had never looked at anything — the commit hook then failed on a private-item doc link that had been in the file for an hour. The lesson is not about that script: any gate invoked in an unfamiliar way must be made to FAIL once before its silence is read as a pass.

THE SPECIAL CASE DISSOLVED INTO THE DATA STRUCTURE. The hardcoded table needed a written rule — "a command key with a modifier on it is a slip" — to keep `Ctrl-D` from detaching. A table matched on exact modifiers gets that as a consequence, and gains what the rule forbade: `C-o` becomes bindable. When a mechanism needs a guard clause to stay correct, the guard is often a hint that the representation is wrong.

A VOCABULARY WITH TWO ENDS AND NO MIDDLE ONLY SHOWS ITS SEAM WHEN A THIRD READER ARRIVES. The wire's key names had a producer and a consumer that happened to agree; nothing held them to it, and nothing needed to until a config file started naming keys. The list now lives in `sprag-input` with a guard in each direction. Look for this shape wherever two crates agree on strings.

NOT BUILT, AND EACH REASON IS A MECHANISM RATHER THAN A SIZE. `bind-key`/`unbind-key` at RUNTIME needs a decision this slice does not force: where the live table lives while a client is already running. tmux's `-n` root table (bindings with no prefix) needs arbitration against the pane for every keystroke, which does not exist. `-r` repeat needs a timer in an event loop that is a pure select today. The GUI still has an empty `WidgetCore::keybinding` and now has a keymap to read. H2's OTHER half — `set-option` / `show-options`, and with it `window-size` — is untouched: sprag has no options table for an option to live in.
