10 new proofs, and all 9 revert-proofs RUN red: re-emitting TOML instead of editing in place kills the comment; a non-implicit table breaks the pin; joining a foreign group; comparing entries WITH their decor (which made every re-install rewrite the file -- the test caught this as a real bug, not a hypothetical); a status that stops reading the switch; treating a null `agent_id` as a subagent; ignoring the config-dir variable; overwriting rather than refusing; giving codex Claude's word for blocked.

Suite exit 0 / 44 targets / 1690 passed (1680 -> 1690 = exactly this slice's 10). fmt clean, clippy 0 all targets, doc gate 0 (it caught two public items linking to private ones). Live: install preserves a comment and two user tables, uninstall restores the file byte-identically, `features.hooks = false` reads BROKEN with the control reading `installed`, and a relative `CODEX_HOME` is refused by name.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: A reverse edit is only exact if its OWN anchor is unique. The last revert-proof restored `("Notification", ...)` into the FIRST table that matched -- Claude's -- silently swapping both targets' blocked events. The script had checked the forward anchor's uniqueness and not the reverse one, and only re-running the suite caught it. Extends R271's byte-restore lesson: check uniqueness in BOTH directions.

The trust gate is REPORTED, not read. codex records approvals at `hooks.state."<identity>".trusted_hash`, whose key is a normalised internal identity with no stability promise; a status derived from misreading it would be exactly the confident wrong answer R273 was about. If codex ever documents that key, reading it would let `list-hooks` distinguish `installed` from `installed, awaiting review`.

Whether the `agent_id` filter is right for codex is read off its SCHEMA (optional exactly on the events a main agent can raise, required on the subagent pair) and not observed from a running codex, which needs an authenticated session. If it is wrong the pane reports nothing and falls back to screen inference -- a degradation, not a break.

Slice 3c is now the real test of the abstraction: a THIRD target must be a `const` and nothing else. Neither remaining candidate has been read at its own HEAD, and the two properties this slice added (a disable switch, a follow-up step) were both discovered from the target rather than predicted.

R275.decision_summary: The bound on an agent report's authority was measured rather than inherited, and R271's "the daemon can see exactly when the reporter expires" turned out true only for the rarer of two shapes: an agent typed at the pane's shell prompt is a grandchild, so killing it leaves the child alive, is_eof never fires, and a crashed agent parked `working` on a pane sitting at a prompt forever.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-terminal/src/pane_pty.rs: `PanePty::foreground_pgid()` reads `/proc/<child>/stat` field 8 (`tpgid`) — a sibling of `read_cwd`, under the same `pid()` guard that exists because a reaped pid may be recycled. Read from `/proc` rather than `tcgetpgrp` because the PTY master is owned by the resize coalescer thread, and the two were measured EQUAL at a prompt, under a foreground job, and after that job was killed.

crates/sprag-detect/src/track.rs: `Reported` gains an opaque `owner`, and the five fields that travelled together from wire to tracker became one `Report` value. The owner lives INSIDE the report rather than in a map beside the tracker, because a second place answering "is there a report on this pane" is exactly the silent drift R271 found; and it belongs to ONE report, so the next speaker brings its own or none.

crates/sprag-host/src/agent.rs: `AgentRegistry::orphaned` asks the OS whether a report's owning process group still exists, through `process_group_exists` — one `kill(-pgid, 0)`, with `EPERM` answering TRUE (the group exists and belongs to another user, which is what `sudo`-run agents leave) and pgids below 2 refused, since `kill`'s negation reads those as commands rather than questions.
crates/sprag-host/src/sweep.rs: the release rule gains its second half, keeping the loop's cost shape — the cheap side first and the agent lock only when it holds.

crates/sprag-host/src/workspace.rs + wire.rs + bin/sprag.rs: `report_agent` takes `bind`, which asks for the report to last only as long as whatever runs in the pane and does NOT say what that is — the daemon samples the group itself, so no caller can name somebody else's. `sprag hook` sets it; `sprag report-agent` does not, because a person's report is theirs to withdraw. `with_pane` replaces a second traversal that duplicated `holds_pane`'s definition of holding a pane.
verification_bullets: The defect was MEASURED before anything was designed, on a real pty with a control: the foreground pgid moved when a grandchild agent started (2746154 -> 2746237), returned to the shell's when it was killed, and the killed group was gone — all while the shell stayed alive, so is_eof was false throughout.

Suite exit 0 / 44 targets / 1690 -> 1697 passed (+7 = exactly this round). fmt clean, clippy 0 all targets with NO suppression (the argument-count warning was answered by grouping the five fields into `Report`, not by an allow), doc gate 0, pre-commit green.

The live proof runs a real daemon whose pane's child is an interactive shell, starts a job at its prompt, fires `sprag hook claude` with a real payload, kills the job with Ctrl-C, and watches the pane recover — with the report read back WHILE the job ran as one control and the shell answering afterwards as the other, so neither "retires everything" nor "the pane died" can pass.

Nine revert-proofs RUN red: the sweep's new half; the daemon ignoring `bind`; the hook not asking for it; an unbound report becoming expirable; kill's wildcards unrefused; an owner inherited by the next report; the wrong /proc/stat field; the comm field anchored on the FIRST paren; and the line split from the start ignoring comm entirely.
carry_forward_bullets: A revert-proof that reports GREEN may never have RUN. `cargo test -p X --lib <filter>` exits 0 when the filter matches NOTHING, and one proof was filtered on `agent::tests::...` while the test had landed in `agent::clock_tests::...` — 0 passed, 455 filtered out, exit 0, reported as "the test proves nothing" when in fact it had not been asked. Every revert-proof harness must assert the test COUNT it ran, not just the exit code. This is silence-is-not-a-passing-gate inside the very mechanism built to catch it.

A fixture must carry every hazard the claim names. The /proc/stat parse claim was "comm may contain spaces AND parens", and the first fixture had only a space — so the rfind-to-find mutation stayed GREEN, because that mutation is only wrong for a paren. One name (`sl) eep`) now falsifies both, and the general form is: a claim with two hazards needs a fixture with two hazards, or half of it is untested.

EPERM from kill — a process group that exists but belongs to another user, which `sudo claude` leaves in a pane — is handled and NOT exercised: an unprivileged test cannot make a process it may not signal. Named in the test's own doc rather than left to be assumed.

Residue, bounded: a pgid could in principle be recycled between the agent's death and the next sweep, holding a stale report one round longer. It needs a full pid wraparound inside one sweep interval, and its consequence is exactly the behaviour this replaces — so the fix is never worse than what it replaced, which is what makes the residue acceptable rather than merely small.

R276.decision_summary: The daemon gained the fact it already held the other half of: which WINDOW is current was session state every client follows, while which PANE is current was each client's private guess — so an agent, a shell and a second display client had no way to say "here", and "what is left of pane 3" had no answer that did not go through somebody's rectangles.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-terminal/src/layout.rs: `PaneDir` (a direction IS an axis plus a side — the two facts this tree already speaks) and `LayoutTree::neighbor`, a STRUCTURAL walk: whether a neighbour exists is decided by the tree's shape alone, and the ratios are consulted only to RANK several candidates, in unit space. So the answer is the same for every client, at every size, and with no client attached. The rival computes it from the last COMPOSED FRAME's u16 rectangles, which move with a sidebar, a tab bar and cell rounding — read at their own HEAD 26a7bc86, not from a README.

crates/sprag-terminal/src/registry.rs: `Window::active` beside `layout`/`floating`/`manual_size`, healed in `reconcile_layout` where the float set is already pruned, and handing off to the ADJACENT leaf in the arrangement as it stands — never to "the first pane", which would throw a user from pane 7 of 8 back to the top for closing one. Durable (`WindowSnapshot::active`, additive) on `manual_size`'s argument: it is a DECISION, and a reboot is exactly when there is no client to ask.

crates/sprag-host/src/wire.rs + workspace.rs + host.rs: `select_pane {pane} XOR {dir}` (the shape `resize_window` established for its four spellings), where a direction with NO neighbour answers `changed: false` rather than refusing — a keybinding at the edge of a layout is a normal keypress, not a caller's mistake. `neighbors.<pane>` answers herdr's `pane.neighbor` AND `pane.edges` with ONE derivation, so `null` IS the edge and the two halves cannot disagree; theirs are two routes to one fact, and their `edges` booleans come from unchromed rects while the `layout` beside them is chromed. `Event::PaneSelected` is DERIVED at H6's one site, and the establishment case is deliberately silent.

crates/sprag-host/src/workspace.rs: `pane_target` — the exact mirror of `window_target` — so `split`, `close` and `resize` with no target act on the active pane, and the wire doc that recorded the impossibility ("`pane` is REQUIRED, because the daemon has no active-pane concept to mean here") is retired along with the CLI's and the TUI's copies of the same sentence. Deliberately NOT applied to `report_agent`/`release_agent`: those are driven by a PROCESS that reads its own pane from `SPRAG_PANE`, and a default there would let a hook whose environment was lost report on somebody else's pane.

A split now makes its new pane ACTIVE in the DAEMON (tmux's rule). The first shape had the display client publish that after its own split answered, and a live test caught the race: the client's write said "the user is here" about a decision taken 30 ms earlier and landed AFTER another client's select. One authority, one write — and `sprag split-window` and an agent get the behaviour for free instead of being the callers that end up somewhere else.

crates/sprag-tui + sprag-client + sprag-gui: both display clients now PROJECT the active pane and PUBLISH the user's own moves, following on the EDGE of the daemon's answer rather than its level — a mirror lags a wake behind a write, and a level-triggered follow yanks the cursor back to where the user was before their own keypress. The GUI's decision is a pure function (`active_pane::decide`) so the rule is tested without a host. `sprag select-pane [-t S] <PANE|-L|-R|-U|-D>`, `sprag panes` marks the active row, and `select_pane` joins the MCP surface with `list_panes` marking where the human is.
verification_bullets: Suite exit 0 / 44 targets / 1697 -> 1721 passed (+24 = exactly this round). fmt clean, clippy 0 across the workspace with no suppression, doc gate 0, pre-commit green on all five commits.

The neighbour walk's ranking test carries its own CONTROL: the same arrangement with the divider's share moved from 0.25 to 0.75 must answer a DIFFERENT pane, so an implementation that ignored the ratios would answer the same one twice and fail. A separate case pins the property the structural walk exists for — a 0.001 share, which rounds under one cell in any real window, still has its neighbours.

The TUI's follow is proven LIVE, over a real socket against a real daemon: a `select_pane` sent on the observer's connection moves where the terminal's next keystrokes land, with the negative half (what was typed before the select stayed in the pane it was typed into) making "types into pane 0 regardless" fail. Repeated 10x, 10/10.

The live PTY suite is what found the yank: `keys_follow_the_focus_the_prefix_moves` went red with "beforeb" — one character reached the right pane and then a lagging mirror pulled the cursor away. It is the revert-proof for the edge-triggered rule: red before the fix, green after.

The ring-capacity derivation MOVED and was re-derived rather than papered over: a split is now THREE records (pane, arrangement, active pane) where it was two, so the 64-pane burst is 188 records rather than 126 and JOURNAL_CAPACITY's stated reach is 85 worst-case operations rather than 128. The FIRST split of a window is still two, because the active pane it sets is that window's first — which the ratio test now states as a row rather than leaving to be discovered.

The MCP tool has a live gate of its own (R258's rule): the server is driven against a real daemon and the move is read back through `list_panes`, because the tool and the listing are wired by different code and a plausible answer that sent nothing would satisfy every wording test.
carry_forward_bullets: THE GUI PIXEL SMOKE IS 123/1, and the failure is diagnosed and is NOT in this round's code. Measured both ways: without the follow the run builds `(narrow|narrow)|wide` and every grid matches; with it, the palette's split targets the now-focused pane and builds `wide|(narrow|narrow)` — where the daemon hands the wide pane 37 columns while the client's widget measures 38. The daemon tiles in CELLS (`tile`/`divide`) and the client lays out in PIXELS through flex, so their rounding can differ by a cell; the shape had simply never been reachable under Xvfb because no pane was ever focused there. A user with a focused pane reaches it today, with or without this round. Next round's first item, and the smoke now prints the numbers.

The active pane's ESTABLISHMENT (a window's first) is deliberately not an event. It was one in the first draft, and the timing was an artifact: a `split` in one window recorded a select in ANOTHER, because that was simply when the daemon happened to reconcile it. The rule is the one a new window's panes already follow — the container is the change, and a reader re-reading it gets the contents.

`sprag ls` still reports the current window's FIRST pane's cwd and branch rather than the active pane's, and that is now a decision rather than an inherited limitation: a listing describes sessions the reader is mostly NOT in, so a stable representative keeps it from flickering as somebody walks around inside one. Recorded because it is the obvious thing to change next and the reason not to is not obvious.

A terminal client cannot show a FLOATING pane, so when the session is on one the TUI keeps its own cursor and publishes NOTHING — "I cannot display that" is not the user choosing something else, and correcting the daemon would fight the client that can show it. The divergence is bounded to that case and is stated in the client's docs.

`git stash` on a CLEAN tree saves nothing, so a later `git stash pop` applies whatever was already on the stack — here an unrelated entry from R156, which spread conflict markers across nine files. Everything was committed, so `git reset --hard HEAD` recovered it and the old entry was left intact. A control run must be taken with a worktree or an explicit checkout, never with a stash whose contents were not verified.

R277.decision_summary: The one-cell divergence R276 left as next round's first item was not a cosmetic rounding note: it was corrupting the pointer, because two separate pixel-to-cell converters were INFERRING how many cells a pane has from the rectangle the widget was drawn in, and a pane's cells are the session's.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-gui/src/terminal.rs: the rule stated ONCE, beside the cell<->pixel round-trip that already lives there. `cell_index(offset_cells, count)` takes an offset ALREADY in cells — not a fraction and a count — so the shape that produced the defect is no longer expressible at the signature, and `rect_cells(rect_px, metric)` names the other quantity honestly: a widget's extent in cells is FRACTIONAL, because pinion's TextGrid fills the sub-cell remainder with the terminal background (R1028) so the remainder is invisible but real.

crates/sprag-gui/src/hyperlink.rs: the OSC-8 hover oracle — which is also the pane's mouse-report layer under DECSET 1000/1002/1003 — scaled pinion's [0,1] pane-rect fraction by the pane's own column COUNT. That spreads `cols` columns across a widget spanning more than `cols` of them. It now scales by the widget's extent and clamps to the pane's grid, and `reconcile_pane_hyperlinks` is fed BOTH halves from the same frame because a stale half is a mis-aimed pointer.

crates/sprag-gui/src/selection.rs: `cell_at` derived its extent from the rect (`floor(rect.w / cell_w)`), so a press in the strip the widget has and the pane does not named a column outside the buffer — which a tracking child receives as a mouse report past its own width. The extent is now `SlotView::pane_grid_size`, the host's answer for that pane.

crates/sprag-gui/src/bin/sprag-smoke.rs: the check that failed at 123/1 asserted `painted == buffer`, which `fit_window` never promised and cannot deliver — it folds each pane's MEASURED cells into one window and the daemon re-divides that window in cells, so two quantisations of one boundary leave some pane a cell of slack and the SHAPE decides which. Replaced by the two claims that are true by construction: no pane is painted smaller than the session gave it, and the surplus is under one cell per axis. The grids print on EVERY run, because a bound that only speaks when it breaks cannot show itself drifting.

crates/sprag-gui/src/main.rs: the module's own Winsize section still said a pane's `(cols, rows)` derive from its sub-rect, which stopped being true when the daemon became the arbiter. Corrected to say what the sub-rect IS — this client's input to the decision — and where the sub-rect still decides (`owns_its_own_size`: a floating pane, or a host with no arbitrated window).

claudedocs/PINION-PR80 (filed, NOT worked around): a `TextGridNode`'s one `rect` means both the paint extent (R1028 fills it whole so no parent surface leaks) and the winsize derivation (R974.1: `cols()` is what the producer is TOLD to size to). A producer sized by another authority cannot satisfy both with any rect, so sprag's snapshot reports cols=38 / buffer_cols=37 forever — the signal pinion's own doc defines as an in-flight resize or a producer bug. Asked for `with_winsize`, default None, rect untouched; consumption is one line.
verification_bullets: Suite exit 0 / 44 targets / 1721 -> 1724 passed (+3 = exactly this round's tests). fmt clean, clippy 0 workspace-wide with no suppression, doc gate 0 over 16 crates, pre-commit green on both commits.

THE ROUND'S OWN METHOD FAILURE, caught by running the revert-proof: the first hover test PASSED on the implementation it was written to exclude. The two forms differ by `frac * (span - count)`, which is below one cell everywhere and so crosses a cell boundary only for some fractions — and the probe had been placed at the widget's mid-point, where both answer 40. Re-aimed at column 60 and row 20, the retired form answers (59, 19) for a pointer over (60, 20): off by one on BOTH axes, measured.

The selection revert-proof is the sharper one because its failure is not an approximation: with the rect-derived extent restored, a press in the surplus strip of a 10x4 pane answers Some((10, 4)) — a cell the grid does not contain. It boots the real in-process terminal rather than stubbing a size, because the claim is that the converter reads the HOST's answer.

Live headless pixel smoke (Xvfb + lavapipe, real daemon, real window): 123 passed / 1 failed -> 125 passed / 0 failed. The check count rose by two because the one unachievable equality became two achievable claims, and the surplus claim is TIGHT rather than vacuous — the measured grids are ((38,17),(37,17)) and two exact panes, so the bound it asserts is the value it observes.

The pinion gap was verified at the pin sprag builds against (38c29df2) by reading BOTH sides of the collision — `TextGridNode::cols()` deriving from the rect, and R1028's own test name asserting the whole-rect background fill — rather than assuming the obvious fix (shrink the rect) was available. It is not: shrinking the rect shrinks the gutter fill and leaks the theme surface into the pane, which is the leak R1028 exists to prevent.
carry_forward_bullets: PINION-PR80 is OPEN and is the only thing standing between the snapshot and the truth. Until it lands, every introspecting client — sprag's own MCP surface included — reads a permanent cols != buffer_cols on any tiled pane whose widget carries slack, and pinion's documented reading of that is 'an in-flight resize or a producer bug'. The pointer no longer believes it; a reader still would.

`max_size` is absent from pinion's LayoutStyle while `min_size` is present (R1086, added for the symmetric reason). It was the first fix considered and is recorded here as REJECTED for this defect rather than merely unused: sizing the grid node to its buffer would need it, and would also move R1028's gutter fill into sprag. Worth filing on its own merits if a second consumer appears; it is not what PR-80 asks for.

The surplus bound of one cell per axis is now ASSERTED and is not PROVEN. `fit_window` walks down from the fold and returns the largest window satisfying every pane, which bounds the slack from above but not obviously by one — the number is measured, not derived. If that check ever fails it is a finding about the fold, not a flake, and the grids beside it will say which pane.

herdr was NOT re-read for this round: there is no local clone (the 2026-08-01 audit was taken at 26a7bc86 from a full clone since removed), so no superiority claim is made on the pointer axis. herdr vendors ghostty and therefore has a pixel surface over a cell grid, which means it has the same class of converter — that is a hypothesis, not a reading, and it should be checked at source before it is written anywhere durable.

The next capability gap is unchanged and untouched by this round: pane zoom / swap / move (7 items, gap 7 of the herdr re-audit), which is cheaper now that an active pane exists. Pane plugins (11) and git worktree (4) rank above it by item count and below it by cost.

R278.decision_summary: A head-to-head against herdr's shipped binary found sprag's server answers a request 4.4x FASTER while its CLI is 23x SLOWER, because a 50 ms accept poll sits on every new connection - and the session that measured it exposed how quietly this client fails, by silently attaching to a stranger's daemon nine times and leaving nine sessions behind.
changes_bullets: sprag-rpc client.rs: HostConn::call wrote its request with writeln! at a RAW UnixStream, so serde_json's token-by-token Display made every brace its own sendto - 84 sendto for one 105-byte line. The line is now built WHOLE and put out with one write_all, which retires the flush too: no buffered state is left to forget. Measured live: sendto 84 to 2, syscalls per call 202 to 120.

sprag-rpc client.rs: every failure out of call now NAMES its request (the method plus the path its params address), with the ErrorKind PRESERVED because callers exit on UnexpectedEof rather than retry. Done at the funnel: there is one call and dozens of call sites, and the site that gets forgotten is the one that fires.

sprag-client wire.rs: four hand-rolled from_value().map_err() copies became one read_slot that names the slot when the DECODE fails. That is the opposite fact from a refused request and the two used to read identically - a decode failure is a version skew between a client and a daemon.

PINION-PR81 filed (MAJOR): pinion-rpc-transport keeps its listener non-blocking and sleeps ACCEPT_POLL = 50 ms between WouldBlock accepts. Its own docstring calls that negligible for an out-of-band endpoint, but in sprag this socket is the PRIMARY agent path with a fresh connection per CLI invocation. ACCEPT_POLL predates sprag having a CLI at all: nobody wrote anything false, and the consumer's architecture turned a true sentence false.

The benchmark is recorded as METHOD, not only as numbers: herdr was measured as the artifact it SHIPS rather than a local build, both sides got one session and one pane at the same 120x39 = 4680 cells, conditions were interleaved per repetition because the box carries other work, and the request bytes were captured with strace so each server is driven exactly as its own client drives it.
verification_bullets: Suite exit 0 / 44 targets / 1724 to 1726 (+2 = exactly this round's two tests). fmt clean, clippy 0 workspace-wide with no suppression, doc gate 0 over 16 crates, pre-commit green on both commits.

THE MEASUREMENT, with the CLI removed so the servers are compared and not the binaries (N=200, load 4.2 recorded): sprag warm 0.025 ms on a held connection against herdr cold 0.110 ms, and sprag cold 50.188 ms (p10 50.021 / p90 50.332). A p10/p90 band that tight around a round number is the signature of a TIMER rather than of work, and it matches ACCEPT_POLL exactly. At the CLI: sprag 47.8 ms against herdr 2.08 ms, with --version as the process-start control at 0.67 / 0.61 ms.

The control that isolates the accept delay MOVES THE STATE rather than merely passing: on one connection the FIRST request costs 19.65 ms and the next fifty cost a median of 0.020 ms. Same socket, same request bytes, same process.

The one-write claim is pinned by a test whose CONTROL is the whole point: a counting writer shows writes == 1, and the RETIRED form through the same instrument must count more than ten, or writes == 1 would also pass on a counter that never increments. It also asserts the bytes round-trip back to the identical request.

The naming is proven LIVE by rebuilding the original symptom with a stub daemon that answers the layout slot with a bare integer: the message went from invalid type integer 0 expected string or map, to one that names the slot and the struct it could not read.

TWO of the round's own hypotheses were REFUTED by their controls. The write fix did NOT fix the client boot failure - a binary built without it boots fine 3/3. And herdr has no pixel-to-cell converter at all - ratatui plus crossterm, no winit or wgpu, and their vendored libghostty-vt is a PARSER, so mouse events reach them already in cells.
carry_forward_bullets: THE INCIDENT, recorded because the mechanism is reusable and the cost was real: sprag-tui resolves its daemon from SPRAG_GUI_HOST_SOCK and falls back SILENTLY to the well-known socket, so a probe that set only SPRAG_HOST_RPC_SOCK attached to the machine's live daemon. A boot begins with new_session and failed afterwards, so each of nine runs left a session behind. They were identified by fingerprint and killed on the owner's instruction; the daemon then ended itself, having nothing left to serve.

THE FAIL-LOUD ITEM STILL OPEN, and the one that actually bit: a boot that CREATED a session and then fails leaves it behind. The shape wanted is a rollback through a NEW connection, because the failure being guarded is usually the boot connection being unusable, and when even that fails the error must NAME the orphan. Deliberately not done here - it wraps about 75 lines of spawn_or_attach's tail.
The silent socket FALLBACK is also still silent. Naming the request fixed WHICH STEP failed; it did not make a client say WHICH DAEMON it chose when nothing named one.

sprag-tui's original boot failure is UNDIAGNOSED and its reproduction is LOST. Ruled out with controls: the user config, a project .sprag.toml, TERM and terminfo across six values, the layout reply through both from_str and from_value, and this round's write fix. One clue survives: expected string or map is what a serde ENUM says when handed an integer, while LayoutSnapshot names its struct - so the failing slot decodes into an ENUM, and this round's naming will say which one next time.

RE-MEASURE after PR-81 lands, with the SAME harness rather than a new one. The projection is sprag CLI about 0.72 ms against herdr's 2.08 ms - roughly 3x ahead where it is 23x behind today - and that number is a PROJECTION, not a measurement. The herdr release binary is kept at /tmp/hb/herdr; the durable clone is /home/coin/herdr.

R279.decision_summary: The two fail-loud items R278 left were ONE defect - a fact the client acts on but cannot state - so both were fixed by making the fact a type that carries its own obligation: the endpoint now names what pointed this process at it, and a boot that creates a session owns undoing it.
changes_bullets: sprag-rpc endpoint.rs (new): HostEndpoint carries the socket path AND its provenance (Named by an env var / Given by a flag or harness / the well-known Default, with the vars it consulted). A message that names the endpoint therefore names its origin STRUCTURALLY - a call site cannot forget to, having never held a bare path to print. mount() and socket_path() now resolve through it, so the end that BINDS and the end that CONNECTS are read the same way in one log.

The client precedence gained a level, and that level is the correction: SPRAG_GUI_HOST_SOCK, then SPRAG_HOST_RPC_SOCK, then the well-known socket. The daemon exports its own path env into every pane it births, so a client started INSIDE a pane now belongs to the daemon that owns that pane - $TMUX semantics, already how sprag-mcp resolves. The display clients were the one surface ignoring the fact, which is exactly how R278's probe put its client and its daemon on different sockets. An EMPTY value counts as unset.

sprag-client wire.rs: the boot is a TRANSACTION. Everything after the session is created runs as ONE fallible expression (boot_into_session), so no later edit can add an early return that skips the undo, and its failure is handed to BornSession::roll_back - which kills the session over a FRESH connection, because the failure being guarded is usually the boot connection being unusable (a tripped read deadline retires a HostConn by design). An ATTACHED session is never rolled back: the guard only exists on the create path, so that is structural rather than remembered.

The failure is a TYPE, not prose: BootError carries the endpoint, the cause, and a BootResidue of None / Removed(name) / Orphan{name, why} - an orphan cannot be constructed without both the name and the reason the removal failed, which is what makes the operator line actionable (remove it with sprag kill-session -t NAME). It travels inside io::Error so every caller keeps its io::Result, and downcast_ref answers did this boot leave a session behind without parsing a sentence.

WireHost::boot over an explicit BootSpec is now the seam and spawn_or_attach is the thin env-reading wrapper over it, which is what let the end-to-end proof drive a private daemon without touching process globals. The sprag CLI's own connect() was the same defect at another surface and was fixed with it: no server running at PATH became no server running at PATH (named by SPRAG_HOST_RPC_SOCK) / (the well-known default; SPRAG_HOST_RPC_SOCK is unset).
verification_bullets: Suite exit 0 / 45 targets / 1740 passed (was 44 / 1726: +1 target and +14 tests, exactly this round's). fmt clean, clippy 0 workspace-wide with no suppression, doc gate 0 over 16 crates, pre-commit green on both commits.

The end-to-end proof runs against a real sprag-term and its injection is the PRODUCT's own behaviour, not a test hook: argv names a binary that does not exist, so new_session validates the spec, creates the session, tolerates the fork/exec failure by design and answers with the name - then boot_panes has to reach the pane count and its spawn is refused. A failure strictly AFTER the creation, with no test-only code in the client.

It probes BY NAME rather than counting sessions, and that choice is load-bearing: the sessions slot drops paneless unattached sessions (SessionInfo::is_listable), so this orphan is invisible to a count. A request scoped to a session that does not exist is refused whole, so scoping a read to the reported name asks about that one session.

REVERT-PROOF at both layers, run: with BornSession::kill neutered to Ok(()), the end-to-end fails with the session 1 the failed boot created must not survive it, and the unit test fails with exactly one request - the kill - was sent: left 0, right 1. The end-to-end CONTROL (the probe sees a session that exists) passed in BOTH runs, so the probe discriminates rather than always answering gone.

The unit test's recording server had to be given a BOUNDED accept first: with the kill neutered it parked on accept forever and the revert-proof HUNG instead of asserting. A test that hangs when the code is wrong is a test whose failure nobody can read.

The operator-facing strings were RENDERED and read, not assumed. The CLI's two arms were run live against an empty runtime dir so nothing could reach the machine's daemon, and the orphan report is pinned as a whole SENTENCE (which daemon, what failed, what is still there, what to type) with only the OS's errno text left unpinned, being the one part this code does not author.
carry_forward_bullets: HostEndpoint::context was DEAD ON ARRIVAL - written as the ONE way a wire failure is told while BootError did its own formatting, i.e. a doc comment making a claim no caller backed. Caught during self-review and given the caller its doc named: the poll-connection reconnect in attach_in_place, which is the one failure a user meets AFTER the boot and which said Connection refused while naming no daemon. The class is worth hunting: an abstraction justified by a sentence about how it will be used.

The rollback's connect takes NO retry window, unlike the boot's. Written first with CONNECT_TIMEOUT (5 s), it delayed the orphan report by five seconds and bought nothing: that window exists for the SPAWN race, and a daemon that answered moments ago either accepts instantly (a listening socket's backlog does not wait on the accept loop - the very thing PINION-PR81 is about), refuses instantly, or is wedged and caught by the read deadline.

herdr comparison, at 9a4ce5e1 and at source: their create is atomic BY CONSTRUCTION (create_workspace_with_launch_env builds the workspace before pushing it into state) and their client's connect-or-spawn creates nothing server-side - it runs a THIN CLIENT against workspaces the server owns. R280.decision_summary: The boot failure five rounds could not reproduce was a VERSION SKEW, diagnosed from source rather than reproduced - and the fix is not that one slot but the missing agreement underneath it: every request now declares the wire shape it speaks, the DAEMON refuses one it does not, and a shape pin keeps the number from going stale.
changes_bullets: THE DIAGNOSIS, from source and with no reproduction. `expected string or map` is not an enum's message, it is serde_json's `deserialize_enum` refusing a value that is neither. Walking the boot's decodes, exactly ONE fatal one holds such an enum and the request count lands on it: request 9 is the layout, request 10 is the one never sent. Before e2f2376 (R264) `LayoutWire.root` was an externally tagged `LayoutNodeWire`; today it is an arena INDEX, and a one-pane window's index is 0 - which is why the sentence said `integer 0`, a fresh client boot being exactly that window. Pinned as a running test in sprag-terminal's layout module, beside the migration it is the underside of.

Why five rounds missed it: R278 captured the layout reply and checked that it decoded - with the NEW client. A skew is invisible from either end alone, and testing the end you have is the one-sided comparison this arc keeps re-learning about rivals.

sprag-rpc: WIRE_PROTOCOL, PROTOCOL_PARAM and PROTOCOL_FIELD, with the param merged into EVERY request by `HostConn::call`'s existing seam - the one place a request is built, so no client can omit it, including clients that do not exist yet. Zero extra round trips; the declaration rides traffic that was already there.

sprag-host: the DAEMON refuses a request written against a shape it does not speak, at `dispatch_one` - the single door every socket and stdin client passes - BEFORE scope resolution and before any handler. This is the half a client cannot perform: an old client contains no check to run, so the only end that can catch it is the new one. herdr has a protocol version (checked at attach and before every CLI request) but BOTH its checks live in the client, so an old herdr client against a new server performs none - exactly the direction that bit sprag.

sprag-client and the CLI take the other direction, which only a REPLY can carry: the daemon answers `client/hello` with its own protocol, and a hello that names none is a daemon from before the check. The boot shakes hands BEFORE it creates anything, so a skewed pair now costs a connection rather than an abandoned session. The CLI gained a hello for the same reason; herdr pays a whole extra status round trip per request to ask the same question.
verification_bullets: Suite exit 0 / 45 targets / 1746 passed (was 1740: +6, exactly this round's). fmt clean, clippy 0 workspace-wide with no suppression, doc gate 0 over 16 crates, pre-commit green on all three commits.

BOTH directions proven against a real sprag-term: a request put on the wire BY HAND without the protocol key - a request this build can no longer produce, since HostConn adds it - is refused with a message naming both numbers and the remedy; and the hello reply carries the daemon's own number, which `HostConn::handshake` reads. The client-side refusal of a daemon that names no shape is proven against a stub that answers a hello the old way.

REVERT-PROOF, run: with the `protocol_refused` call deleted, the hand-written old-style request is SERVED - the pre-fix behaviour verbatim, a daemon answering a client that will then misread it - while the CONTROL (the same request carrying this build's protocol) passed in both runs, so the test discriminates rather than refusing everything.

THE SHAPE PIN catches a change that still COMPILES, which is the case a hand-maintained constant misses. Adding a field to a pinned DTO is a compile error at the pin itself (it constructs the struct literally); a `#[serde(rename)]` on `WindowInfo::name` compiles clean, and the pin failed at runtime with both strings and the instruction to bump WIRE_PROTOCOL. Nothing in herdr's tree fails when a shape moves under their number.

THE HANDSHAKE RE-OPENED R273's HOLE AND R273's OWN TEST CAUGHT IT. The CLI's `connect` now performs I/O, so `deliver_hook`'s read deadline - set after the connection existed - no longer covered the first wait, and against a wedged daemon the agent's hook stalled 20 s instead of 2. Fixed structurally: `connect(deadline)` takes the bound as a parameter, so a caller cannot obtain a connection without stating how long it will wait. 18 management sites pass None (a person's command, interruptible); the hook passes its own.

Nine `rpc.rs` unit tests fed raw requests to `dispatch_one` and were refused by the new door - correctly. They now declare the protocol at their single funnel, so the door is exercised by every one of them rather than bypassed. Two sprag-rpc assertions became FALSE ("an unscoped connection adds nothing") and were RE-STATED rather than patched: it adds no session and always declares its shape, which is a different fact.
carry_forward_bullets: Negotiation is deliberately NOT built - a daemon serving two shapes at once would have to keep every retired shape alive forever, and the daemon is restartable with its sessions restored from the durability snapshot, so "restart the daemon" is a complete remedy and both messages say exactly that. Recorded so a later round does not read the omission as an oversight.

WIRE_PROTOCOL is 1 and the pin covers WindowInfo, SessionInfo and LayoutSnapshot - what a client decodes WHOLE through serde. The hand-parsed slots (panes, revision) are deliberately outside it: a client reads those key by key with explicit fallbacks, so adding a key cannot break one. If that ever stops being true, the pin's coverage is what has to move first.

The debt register's item 5 is CLOSED, and closed by DIAGNOSIS rather than by reproduction. Its surviving clue - that the failing slot decodes into an enum - was correct and sufficient; what was missing was reading the OTHER end's decoder. The general form is worth keeping: when a symptom cannot be reproduced, find the pair of versions that produce it and read both.

R281.decision_summary: The pin bump delivered both owed upstream items, and the re-measurement it owed then found the real reason sprag's CLI was slow - a yes/no question answered by scanning a list that is filtered for humans and costs a whole /proc walk - so the round ends with sprag measurably faster than herdr on every axis it was behind on.
changes_bullets: THE PIN: 38c29df2 -> 49cd8477, 73 commits, and a TENTH pinion crate. sprag's Cargo.toml gained pinion-gpu because the vello_renderer_impl! expansion now names ::pinion_gpu::{GpuError, GpuContext, FrameTimer, GpuFrameClock} in the consumer's crate root (pinion R1537 took the wgpu device out of vello's RenderContext so it can request TIMESTAMP_QUERY). SCE unchanged at 201783c4 on both sides - step 3 checked by opening pinion@49cd8477's own Cargo.toml, not assumed.

THE BUMP MOVED SPRAG'S WIRE WITH NO SPRAG SOURCE LINE CHANGED. pinion R1540 put rename_all = "lowercase" on UnderlineStyle, so a cell frame's "underline" crosses as "none" where it crossed as "None". sprag_grid::wire's interned CellStyle carries pinion's cell vocabulary VERBATIM, deliberately, so that an upstream ADDITION is a compile error rather than silent data loss - and a respelling is neither. WIRE_PROTOCOL 1 -> 2, and the shape pin extended to the cell frame with every style field carrying a non-default value, because a default-everywhere buffer would pin only the unit variants.

PINION-PR80 CONSUMED, unconditionally rather than per call site: grid_node - the node-shape SSOT both the headless and GUI paths build through - declares with_winsize from the cells it is handed. In sprag the layout has never been the sizing authority (the daemon tiles the arbitrated window in CELLS and that division is both the TIOCSWINSZ and the buffer), so this is a fact about sprag, not about a binding. Every sprag grid now answers winsize_source "producer" with cols == buffer_cols; the headless snapshot used to answer cols 0 against a real buffer and tell readers to use buffer_cols instead.

PINION-PR81 CONSUMED AND RE-MEASURED with R278's own harness, then the re-measurement found the next wall. The daemon's share collapsed as promised, but the CLI was still 4.5x slower than herdr, and 87% of what was left was ONE request every scoped command sends: require_session -> session_exists scanned the `sessions` slot to answer does this name exist. That listing attributes each session's listening ports through a whole /proc walk (ProcScan::scan), and it also HIDES a resting empty anchor (SessionInfo::is_listable), so the scan was both the cost and a correctness defect - `sprag panes -t 0` answered no session named "0" while `sprag new 0` answered a session named "0" already exists, both true, about one daemon.

The fix asks the SCOPE RESOLVER instead, which is the only authority for it, and reads the answer off the JSON-RPC code rather than off a sentence: sprag-rpc gained HostConn::try_call + RpcFault + CallError so a caller can act on WHICH failure it was, and INVALID_PARAMS got one home in the transport both ends share (the daemon's two reply builders now spell it from there). sprag also gained `--version`, which contacts no daemon - the one question a misbehaving install has to answer, and the process-start control every latency comparison subtracts.
verification_bullets: Suite exit 0 / 45 targets / 1748 passed (was 1746: +2, exactly this round's two CLI tests). fmt clean, clippy 0 workspace-wide with no suppression, doc gate 0 over 16 crates, pre-commit green on all seven commits. Live headless pixel smoke 126/0 (was 125/0: +1, the PR-80 acceptance check).

THE RE-MEASUREMENT, same harness as R278 (sock.py and bench.py byte-identical apart from their output path), release binaries, interleaved, load recorded. Socket: sprag cold 50.188 ms -> 0.044 ms and herdr 0.075 ms, so the axis sprag was 456x behind on it is now 1.7x ahead on; warm 0.021 ms. CLI: list the panes 47.79 -> 0.73 ms against herdr 1.03, read a pane's screen 47.81 -> 1.04 against 1.16. Round trip alone (op minus the version control): 0.19 vs 0.53 and 0.50 vs 0.66. R278's ~3x projection is now a measurement at the round-trip level and 1.3x end-to-end, process start being what is left.

THE ONE HARNESS CHANGE IS THE HARNESS'S OWN RULE. Its docstring says the request is whatever the tool's CLI actually sends, captured with strace - and R280 made every request declare its protocol, so the R278 bytes now measure a refusal. Re-captured with strace: the single difference is "protocol":2. herdr's request is untouched, its binary being the same shipped one.

THE /proc SCAN IS THE COST, proven by a control that MOVES the number rather than by reading the code: the same `sessions` request costs 0.010 ms on a daemon where no session holds a live pane and 4.111 ms with one - the branch ProcScan::scan sits behind. Per-request breakdown on a warm connection: client/hello 0.010, sessions 3.931, panes 0.015, cells.0 0.123 ms.

REVERT-PROOF, run: with the old listing scan restored under the new test, a_session_the_listing_hides_is_still_addressable fails with exactly the operator sentence the defect produced - a scoped command reaches the hidden anchor: sprag: no session named "0". Its CONTROLS passed in both runs: the listing still hides the anchor (this is not "show it"), and a genuinely unknown name is still refused, so addressability was not bought by accepting everything.

R280's DOOR FIRED LIVE, three times, against a real older build rather than a stub. A sprag-tui from before the WIRE_PROTOCOL bump failed four smoke checks in silence; a git worktree at 640aab2 rebuilt that exact binary as a control, and with the smoke's new diagnostic the client's own pty screen read: this daemon speaks wire protocol 2 and the client speaks 1 ... Rebuild the client, or restart this daemon. The R278 harness's own request bytes were refused the same way.
carry_forward_bullets: STILL OPEN, and now measured: the `sessions` slot pays ProcScan::scan for EVERY reader, including the GUI's sidebar poll, because ports rides the same answer as name/windows/cwd/branch. This round stopped one caller asking; it did not make the answer cheap. The structural fix is R217's rule applied here - an expensive enrichment is asked for, not attached - and it moves a wire shape, so it is a WIRE_PROTOCOL 3 slice. 4 ms per poll is what it is worth.

HostConn::call still renders a JSON-RPC fault as `host rpc error: <object>` at every other call site; try_call exists but only the pre-flight uses it. Now that RpcFault carries data, the CLI's generic error path could print the daemon's sentence instead of its JSON - a small, uniformly-better change this round did not make.

The `--version` control was rc=2 and 0 bytes for TWO rounds (R278 recorded the number; the harness printed the exit code both times). sprag had no --version at all, so the control was measuring the unknown-command path - usage to stderr, exit 2. Read the exit code, again: the harness was not silent, the reader was.

PINION-PR80 and PR-81 are both CLOSED - delivered as requested and over-delivered twice (accept_wakeups makes demand-driven waiting assertable as a COUNT; winsize_source carries the authority as a fact rather than an inference). Remaining upstream: PR-48 (socket-disabled-at-bind, MINOR) and the older unlanded reports. The ranked herdr gaps are unchanged: plugins 11 / worktree 4 / zoom-swap-move 7.

Consuming with_winsize would have made the pixel smoke's two boundary checks vacuously true (cols == buffer_cols by construction, so buffer <= painted and painted - buffer <= 1 both read 0 <= 0). The widget's span moved to rect / cell metric, where it still lives, and the grids print every run. A consumption that improves a number the gate reads is a consumption that can silently retire the gate.

That listing attributes each session's listening ports through a whole /proc walk (ProcScan::scan), and it also HIDES a resting empty anchor (SessionInfo::is_listable), so the scan was both the cost and a correctness defect - `sprag panes -t 0` answered no session named "0" while `sprag new 0` answered a session named "0" already exists, both true, about one daemon.

The fix asks the SCOPE RESOLVER instead, which is the only authority for it, and reads the answer off the JSON-RPC code rather than off a sentence: sprag-rpc gained HostConn::try_call + RpcFault + CallError so a caller can act on WHICH failure it was, and INVALID_PARAMS got one home in the transport both ends share (the daemon's two reply builders now spell it from there). sprag also gained `--version`, which contacts no daemon - the one question a misbehaving install has to answer, and the process-start control every latency comparison subtracts.

R282.decision_summary: The session list stopped answering a question it had to sample: cwd, branch and listening ports left SessionInfo for their own address, because the registry's structure and the operating system are different kinds of fact, and serving them together made the cheapest question in the mux cost a /proc walk of every process on the box on every poll wake of every attached client.
changes_bullets: THE SPLIT, by NATURE rather than by cost. SessionInfo keeps what the registry itself moves - name, windows, panes, default, attached - all of which change on an event the scene revision already announces. cwd/branch/ports moved to sprag_terminal::SessionActivity, sampled from the OS, which moves with nothing the daemon can see. Removing the fields rather than leaving them optional is what makes the confusion unrepresentable: an unfilled ports: [] would have meant both 'serves nothing' and 'you did not ask', and no reader could have told which. WIRE_PROTOCOL 2 -> 3, shape pin extended to both new shapes.

THE SAMPLE IS ASKED FOR, AND ANSWERS WITH ITS AGE. session_activity.<max_age_ms> is a parametric query family (cells.<offset>'s shape - the argument rides the path, and a query never bumps the revision, which is R152's livelock lesson). ActivitySampler holds one sample per HOST and re-takes it only when the caller's declared tolerance is not met, under a lock the other askers wait on - so N concurrent readers cost ONE /proc walk, and a daemon nobody is looking at costs nothing at all. The reply carries sampled_ms_ago, because a sampled fact read without its age is one whose freshness the reader has to assume.

THE CALLER NAMES ITS TOLERANCE, and the two callers want different ones: `sprag ls` passes 0 and waits for its own walk (it prints once and is then read for as long as somebody looks at it), the session rail passes SESSION_ACTIVITY_DISPLAY_MAX_AGE = 1s. Both join the two answers by NAME, never by position - the listing is filtered for humans (is_listable hides a resting anchor) and the sample is not, so the two lists are different lengths on purpose.

A CLIENT NEEDS ITS OWN CLOCK FOR A FACT NOTHING ANNOUNCES, and this was found by the pixel smoke rather than by reasoning. The first implementation refreshed only on a poll wake; a wake means the SCENE moved, and a cd that prints a prompt RACES the sample - the daemon answers that wake from a sample taken a moment before the chdir, nothing bumps the revision again, and the rail shows the old directory until the next unrelated keystroke. ActivityThread (one thread, one connection, per attached client) refreshes at the tolerance and repaints only when the rows CHANGED, so an idle window stays idle.
verification_bullets: MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER WITH THE SAME INSTRUMENT, and the instrument gained the rows so the next round does not rebuild a harness in a scratchpad. sprag-latency, release: `request sessions slot (live panes)` 3478.178 us -> 2.247 us, and the enrichment it used to carry (the difference against the same request on a host with no live pane) 3476.92 us -> 0.84 us, from 20.86% of a 60 Hz frame to 0.005%. A poll wake now pays 2.247 + 2.372 = 4.6 us for both reads. Asking for a FRESH sample still costs 5143 us - the walk did not get cheaper, it stopped being attached to the identity question.

THE BEFORE/AFTER SPREAD IS THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN, not a claim: `request panes slot (with tokens)` - untouched by this round - moved 9.513 -> 11.138 us between the two runs, so the second run was on a busier box, which is also why the fresh sample reads higher than the enrichment it replaces. sprag-latency's own docs put across-run movement at 20-30%.

R283.decision_summary: The debt register's item 9 was an inherited sentence, and measuring it refuted it: the CLI does not print a JSON object at anybody — it prints a Rust enum variant on two paths and a client-side guess on six more, and the guesses exist because pinion's InvokeError has no room for the reason a producer already knows.
changes_bullets: THE INHERITED CLAIM WAS FALSE AND IS CORRECTED. R281 registered 'HostConn::call still renders a fault as host rpc error: <json object>' and R282 carried it forward unread. Measured instead: 15 reachable CLI failure paths against an isolated daemon, and the split is 7 exact / 6 guess / 2 leak. Nothing anywhere prints a JSON object - RpcFault::Display has preferred the `data` sentence since R281, so the only question was what the daemon puts THERE.

THE TWO LEAKS ARE FIXED SPRAG-SIDE. `report-agent` and `release-agent` were the only CLI verbs with no mapping at all: `sprag report-agent --pane 999` printed `scene/invoke /sprag_mux/external/report_agent: host rpc error: InvokeRejected` - a scene path and a Rust variant name, neither of which an operator can act on. Both now go through `try_call` and a shared `agent_refusal`, which names the pane, names the TWO causes the daemon's one variant covers (no such pane daemon-wide, or no agent detector on this host), and quotes what the wire actually carried. No request is added to the happy path; a transport failure passes through untouched, because it is not about panes.

THE COMMENT WAS THE OWED ITEM, AGAIN. `require_pane`'s doc asserted that a wrong id is 'an unknown ADDRESS, whose raw refusal says nothing about panes, unlike the mux actions' pane-level Rejected'. That last clause is exactly backwards - a mux action's Rejected carries no payload at all, so it is not pane-level, it is not any level - and it is why nobody had looked at these two verbs. The false half is replaced by what was measured, with a pointer to where the remainder lives.

PINION-PR82 FILED (MEDIUM, unlanded): `InvokeError::Rejected` is a payload-free variant, in both pinion-core's trait enum and pinion-rpc's, so a producer that knows exactly why it refused can only answer the variant name - which arrives in JSON-RPC `data` as the string "InvokeRejected". That is why six sprag messages are disjunctions of 2-4 causes rather than facts (`split-window` lists four). Asked for `Rejected(String)`, that reason carried through to `data`, and (recommended) a JSON-RPC code distinct from Invalid params. Indexed in PINION-REQUIREMENTS.md 상태 갱신 55.

THE MEASUREMENT IS THE FINDING, and it was taken before anything was designed: 15 CLI commands run against a daemon on its own socket, each failure's exact stderr and exit code recorded. The 2 leaks and the 6 disjunctions are quoted verbatim in PINION-PR82; the disjunctions are what makes the upstream gap concrete rather than a preference.

REVERT-PROOF, run: with the two call sites returned to `call`'s flat rendering, the new test fails with `left: "sprag: host rpc error: InvokeRejected"` against the sentence it expects. The whole sentence is pinned rather than three fragments of it (R279), and BOTH verbs are asserted - they share one helper, so a test of one would pass while the other still leaked.

THE TEST CARRIES ITS OWN CONTROL: the same two verbs against the pane that IS there, in the same test, both exit 0. Without it every assertion above would also pass against a build where both commands were simply broken.

THE TWO CAUSES WERE READ OFF THE DAEMON'S SOURCE, not guessed: `workspace::report_agent` returns Rejected at exactly two sites (no AgentClock on this host; `with_pane` found no such id) and `release_agent` likewise (no clock; `holds_pane` false). `holds_pane` is DAEMON-WIDE, which is why a `require_pane` pre-flight would have been a REGRESSION - it checks the scoped session's current window, so it would refuse panes the daemon accepts.

THE PROBE DAEMON WAS FINGERPRINTED BEFORE IT WAS KILLED: its pid was found by reading /proc/<pid>/environ for its OWN socket path, never by matching a command-line pattern, and the two unrelated daemons on this box were left running. R278's incident rule, applied.
carry_forward_bullets: THE SIX DISJUNCTIONS ARE STILL DISJUNCTIONS and will stay so until PR-82 lands: split-window (4 causes), resize-window (3), break-pane (3), join-pane (3), rename-window (2), resize-pane (2). Consuming the fix is one line each - the reason goes where the `or` list is. They were deliberately NOT rewritten this round: a better-worded guess is still a guess.

A REFUSED ACTION MAPS TO -32602 Invalid params, which is the same code sprag's `session_exists` reads as 'no such session'. No collision today - that probe sends a scene/query, which cannot be action-rejected - so it is safe by accident rather than by design. Raised as PR-82's recommended half; if it is declined, sprag should stop keying on the code alone.

`agent_refusal`'s sentence contains a clause that exists only because of the upstream gap ('All it could say was ...'). When PR-82 lands, that clause and the two-cause disjunction both go, and the test pinning the whole sentence is what will force the update rather than leave a stale message behind.

R284.decision_summary: The arrangement gained the two verbs a caller that draws nothing could not say — move-pane and swap-pane — and the design came from sprag's own join-pane doc rather than from the rival list: a move that cannot state a PLACE is to join-pane what a spawn is to a split, and closing it with ONE verb that derives both windows from the two pane ids covers a table herdr needs two methods for and still leaves a hole in.
changes_bullets: THE GAP WAS WRITTEN IN SPRAG'S OWN DOC, NOT IN THE RIVAL AUDIT. JOIN_PANE_ACTION already said 'a client that wants it at a specific split drops it there and writes the tree' - which is verbatim the argument SPLIT_ACTION makes for why it had to exist over spawn + set_layout, and which an author with pixels can act on while a shell script or an agent cannot. So the table is: a NEW pane states where with `split` and does not with `spawn`; an EXISTING pane now states where with `move_pane` and does not with `join_pane`. Both verbs stay - they cover the two things a caller can actually know (what is in the destination, or only its name), with nothing in between.

NEITHER WINDOW IS NAMED, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. A PaneId is registry-unique, so `pane` implies its source window (break_pane's existing rule) and `target` implies its destination. One request therefore covers a re-placement inside one window and a move into another, with no mode flag: whether the two windows differ is an OBSERVATION about the two ids. Read at herdr 9a4ce5e1, at source: `pane.swap` refuses to cross a tab (PaneSwapReason::CrossTab, api/panes.rs:533) and `pane.move` refuses to STAY in one (PaneMoveReason::SameTab, api/panes.rs:685-707), so moving a pane within its own tab is expressible in NEITHER and falls back to a whole-tree layout.apply.

A SWAP IS NOT TWO PLACEMENTS, and the tree says so. LayoutTree::swap_panes exchanges the two leaf ids where they sit, so every divider keeps its id, direction and ratio BY CONSTRUCTION - nothing is removed, so no split can collapse and nothing has to be restored. Cross-window is allowed (tmux allows it; herdr refuses it) and is built from the float path's own capture: each pane's LeafHome is read while its leaf still exists, and the other pane is inserted at it. The two homes name siblings in different trees, so neither capture disturbs the other.

THE ACTIVE PANE FOLLOWS THE PANE AT HOME AND THE CELL ABROAD. Within one window nothing has to happen - `active` is a PaneId and the pane the user was on is still there, merely elsewhere (tmux and herdr both do this). Across two, the window whose active pane just LEFT cannot follow it, so it lands on the ARRIVING pane: a strictly better answer than reconcile_layout's closed-pane successor (a neighbour), and available only here, because only a swap knows what took the place.

TWO RENAMES, because a second caller made the first caller's name a lie: LayoutTree::split_beside -> place_beside and Window::split_pane -> place_pane. Both already MOVED an arranged pane rather than duplicating it - the property the move rests on entirely - so the operation was always a placement and the split was one caller of it. R227's shape: a mechanism hidden under the name of whoever asked first.

AN EDGE IS NOT AN ERROR AND A TYPO IS. swap_pane's naming shape is SELECT_PANE_ACTION's ({pane?, with} XOR {pane?, dir}, both or neither is TypeMismatch), and so is the split between a quiet answer and a refusal: a direction with no neighbour, and a pane swapped with itself, answer {changed: false} because a key bound to `swap-pane -L` pressed at the left edge is well-formed; a pane id naming nothing is Rejected. move_pane's pane == target IS refused, because unlike a swap that request has no reading at all.

A STALENESS BUG THE DESIGN DID NOT PREDICT, found by a test rather than by reading. The first cut asked the destination window's TREE whether the target was tiled; the tree reconciles LAZILY, so a pane spawned since the last read holds no leaf and a plainly-present target would have been REFUSED. Fixed by asking the POOL minus the float set - exactly the set a reconcile arranges - so the answer no longer depends on when anybody last read. THE ROUND'S OWN DESIGN HAD AN INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY, caught by re-reading it: the direction form resolved adjacency in the SCOPED window while both move verbs derive windows from pane ids, so `swap-pane -t 0 5 -L` for a pane 5 in a non-current window answered 'nothing to trade with' - not conservative but FALSE. SessionRegistry::neighbor_of derives the window from the pane; host::neighbor was deleted with its only caller rather than left as dead surface (R279's context()).

The slot split is right (panes answers WHO, layout answers WHERE) but the CLI exposes only the first - a gap for exactly the audience these verbs exist for. Registered, not fixed: it is a presentation decision about an existing verb.

PANE ZOOM IS THE NEXT HEAD and is deliberately NOT this round's shape. It is not a tree operation: zoom is a filter on sprag_terminal::tile, the CELL authority every client and every PTY winsize follows, plus a durable per-window field and a change in every renderer. Note for it, read at herdr 9a4ce5e1: their zoom target is DERIVED from focus (ui/panes.rs:180 renders tab.layout.focused(), and focus_pane_action_keeps_zoomed_when_changing_focus asserts the retarget is deliberate), so a sprag `zoomed: Option<PaneId>` is a different design needing its own argument, not this one's.

NO HostClient TRAIT PAIR AND NO MCP TOOL was added. break_pane/join_pane have trait methods because the GUI's command palette calls them; no GUI gesture asks for a move or a swap, so a trait pair would be an abstraction justified by its FUTURE use. Same for MCP: the agent surface reads and types, and rearranging a user's panes is not an agent's job today. Both are one thin method away the moment a caller wants them.

NO KEY BINDING. BoundAction has four variants and tmux binds { and } to swap-pane; adding it is the H2 keymap surface's slice, and choosing a default key inside the mux crate would be a decision made in the wrong place. The wire verb is what a binding would call.

A CROSS-WINDOW MOVE STILL READS AS PaneClosed IN THE SOURCE PLUS PaneCreated IN THE DESTINATION on the event stream, because SessionShape's fingerprint is per-window. That is exactly what join-pane already produces and is a property of the funnel rather than of this round; not re-litigated here.

R285.decision_summary: The window gained a zoom, and it names a PANE rather than carrying a flag — because sprag PUBLISHES the arrangement in slots while the rival reads its own struct under one lock, so a boolean here would have to be joined against the active pane fetched at another instant; the filter then lives in tile(), the one cell authority, behind a Projection type a caller cannot obtain without stating whether anything is zoomed.
changes_bullets: THE REPRESENTATION IS THE ARGUMENT, and R284 registered that it needed one. herdr 9a4ce5e1 stores `Tab.zoomed: bool` (workspace/tab.rs:48) and DERIVES the target at paint time from whichever pane is focused (ui/panes.rs:179-180). That is sound for herdr: renderer and state are one process under one lock, so the two facts cannot be read a moment apart. sprag publishes them - which pane is active is a DIFFERENT slot (R276) - so a boolean would force a join across two reads, and a client that woke between the two writes would fill its window with the wrong pane (R265's torn read). Window.zoomed: Option<PaneId> travels in LayoutSnapshot beside the tree it filters, so one read decides what to draw.

ONE INVARIANT, KEPT AT TWO AUTHORITIES THAT ALREADY EXISTED: a zoom names the pane its window is ON and TILES, or there is no zoom - so the pane a user types into is always one they can see. Every way active moves goes through the new private Window::set_active, every way the tiled set moves goes through reconcile_layout, and both call heal_zoom. NOTHING ELSE in the crate or the host mentions the zoom: a split ends it because a split selects its new pane, a close ends it because active hands off to a successor, a float ends it because the pane stops being tiled. herdr writes self.zoomed = false at FOUR hand-placed call sites (workspace/tab.rs:414, :483, :505, :527) - four chances for a fifth verb to leave a zoom on a pane that is gone.

THE FILTER IS A TYPE, NOT A PARAMETER. Projection::{Whole(&LayoutWire), Zoomed(PaneId)} is what tile() and fit_window() now take, so a caller cannot reach either without answering 'is anything zoomed?' - R270/R279's unrepresentable-not-forbidden, applied to a QUESTION rather than to a value. It allocates nothing (a zoom is not an edit; the arrangement is untouched underneath), and of falls back to Whole for a pane the tree does not hold because the constructor is public and must be total. Consequence: sprag_host::window::retile reflows the ZOOMED pane's PTY to the whole window, once, for every attached client - herdr does that in its renderer, in a branch it already carries TWICE (ui/panes.rs:179 and :235 via Workspace's Deref to Tab).

THE ARRANGEMENT STAYS READABLE WHILE ZOOMED, on purpose. tree remains what set_layout writes back and what move_pane/swap_pane act on; LayoutSnapshot::projection() is the one place the two are combined into what to DRAW. Serving only the filtered tree would be tidier for a renderer and would blind exactly the audience R284's verbs exist for. The GUI adopts the projection into its dock and its EXISTING pending_write refusal (a surface whose pane set differs from the host's is never written back) covers the zoomed case with no rule of its own.

A STRUCTURAL VERB DOES NOT END A ZOOM, which is where herdr has a hole in the same shape R284 found in its neighbour: herdr REFUSES pane.move outright when either tab is zoomed (PaneMoveReason::ZoomedTab, api/panes.rs:656 and :708), so a zoomed tab cannot be re-arranged at all. Here the arrangement moves and the filter does not, and because the zoom names a PANE rather than a position it rides a swap to the pane's new place.

NO SinglePane REFUSAL. herdr fails the request when the tab holds one pane (actions.rs:1925); sprag accepts it. A zoom is a stored state, not a repaint, and whether it changes what is on screen depends on a pane count that can move a moment later - failing on it would make one caller's result depend on another caller's timing. One fewer reason code, one fewer branch, and zoom then split behaves because the split selects.

WIRE_PROTOCOL 3 -> 4, and the SHAPE PIN is what demanded it: adding zoomed to LayoutSnapshot failed the_wire_shape_is_what_this_protocol_number_stands_for at the commit that wrote it. A pre-R285 client would decode the new snapshot cleanly, ignore the key, and paint the whole arrangement while the daemon had already reflowed the zoomed pane's PTY to the full window - the wrong-answer-that-parses this number exists for. herdr's PROTOCOL_VERSION has no such check.

It allocates nothing (a zoom is not an edit; the arrangement is untouched underneath), and of falls back to Whole for a pane the tree does not hold because the constructor is public and must be total. Consequence: sprag_host::window::retile reflows the ZOOMED pane's PTY to the whole window, once, for every attached client - herdr does that in its renderer, in a branch it already carries TWICE (ui/panes.rs:179 and :235 via Workspace's Deref to Tab).

THE ARRANGEMENT STAYS READABLE WHILE ZOOMED, on purpose. tree remains what set_layout writes back and what move_pane/swap_pane act on; LayoutSnapshot::projection() is the one place the two are combined into what to DRAW. Serving only the filtered tree would be tidier for a renderer and would blind exactly the audience R284's verbs exist for. The GUI adopts the projection into its dock and its EXISTING pending_write refusal (a surface whose pane set differs from the host's is never written back) covers the zoomed case with no rule of its own.

A STRUCTURAL VERB DOES NOT END A ZOOM, which is where herdr has a hole in the same shape R284 found in its neighbour: herdr REFUSES pane.move outright when either tab is zoomed (PaneMoveReason::ZoomedTab, api/panes.rs:656 and :708), so a zoomed tab cannot be re-arranged at all. Here the arrangement moves and the filter does not, and because the zoom names a PANE rather than a position it rides a swap to the pane's new place.

NO SinglePane REFUSAL. herdr fails the request when the tab holds one pane (actions.rs:1925); sprag accepts it. A zoom is a stored state, not a repaint, and whether it changes what is on screen depends on a pane count that can move a moment later - failing on it would make one caller's result depend on another caller's timing. One fewer reason code, one fewer branch, and zoom then split behaves because the split selects.

WIRE_PROTOCOL 3 -> 4, and the SHAPE PIN is what demanded it: adding zoomed to LayoutSnapshot failed the_wire_shape_is_what_this_protocol_number_stands_for at the commit that wrote it. A pre-R285 client would decode the new snapshot cleanly, ignore the key, and paint the whole arrangement while the daemon had already reflowed the zoomed pane's PTY to the full window - the wrong-answer-that-parses this number exists for. herdr's PROTOCOL_VERSION has no such check.

R286.decision_summary: The two things R285 recorded rather than fixed were fixed: the zoom's residual ambiguity turned out to be an inconsistency with its own sibling verbs (a floated target is SPLIT_ACTION's refusal, not swap-pane's edge), and the pixel smoke's 1-in-8 flake was root-caused by MEASUREMENT to an unsound check — the driven line scrolled out of a 152-cell pane before any client could paint it, which is why a parent-commit control reproduced it exactly.
changes_bullets: THE AMBIGUITY WAS A SYMPTOM OF AN INCONSISTENCY, not a corner to document. R285 made a FLOATING zoom target an edge (answered zoomed:false / changed:false) on swap_pane's rule that an edge is not an error. Wrong analogy, and the codebase already said so: an edge is a boundary a MOVEMENT ran into, while a floated pane is a target that cannot be zoomed at all - and SPLIT_ACTION (workspace.rs:357) and move_pane both REFUSE a target the tiling does not hold. A zoom acts on the tiling, so it belongs with them. Window::zoom_pane now checks the POOL MINUS THE FLOAT SET and answers None.

THE PAYOFF IS THAT THE FOUR ANSWERS BECOME DISTINCT. Accepted, a toggle aimed at a floated pane while another was zoomed answered zoomed:false / changed:true - byte for byte what toggling a zoom OFF answers - so the CLI had to consult what IT had asked for to guess between them. Refused, the pair is total over four cases with one meaning each, and the CLI's match dropped its `on` arm entirely: now filling / already filling / arrangement back / arrangement already showing. A verb whose success is ambiguous forces its caller to print the causes it is consistent with, which is R283's shape. Also removed a half-effect: an accepted-but-did-nothing request used to MOVE the active pane as a side effect of declining to do the thing it was for.

THE SMOKE'S FLAKE WAS ROOT-CAUSED BY BUILDING THE DISCRIMINATOR IT LACKED, in three steps, each answering the fork the last one left. (1) `0 projections, 0 cells` said nothing, so the failure learned to ask the DAEMON whether its pane held the line - it did, so the shell was fine and the client had not fetched. (2) That left 'never woke' vs 'woke and skipped', so the failure learned to drive a SECOND line - it painted, so the poll thread was alive. (3) That left 'lost one notification' vs 'nothing to show', so the daemon was asked about its live SCREEN as well as its scrollback-inclusive text - and the screen did NOT hold it. The line had scrolled out of a 152-cell pane before any client could paint it. Not a lost frame: nothing left to show.

SO THE CHECK WAS UNSOUND, and that is why a parent-commit control reproduced it exactly - it was never about the code under test. It now waits on a condition that cannot expire: the client shows the line, OR the pane has already scrolled it away; both mean 'not behind', and an unreadable daemon counts as still-showable so it can never be the reason the check passes. The claim the check is really about - driving ONE pane costs that pane's area and nothing else - is priced below and untouched.

A SEPARATE, REAL FREEZE WAS FOUND ON THE WAY AND FIXED ON ITS OWN MERITS. When a wake's pane re-query fails, sprag-client's poll thread rebuilds its seeds from the cache - and carried projection: pane.projection.clone(), the token the held frame was taken under. stale_panes then compares held == held, fetches nothing, and the pane FREEZES: not until a later wake, but until something else in the session moves, because the wake that change had was already spent. Its own gate forbids exactly this - 'I cannot tell must never resolve to assume unchanged' - so the seed now carries None. This did NOT fix the flake above, checked by re-running, and is recorded as what it is.

changes_bullets: THE GAP WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. `sprag panes` reads the panes slot and prints one line per pane; that listing is INVARIANT under all three placement verbs. A swap exchanges two positions and the ids come back in the same pool order; a zoom changes nothing in it at all. Both are asserted in the new integration test as the FIRST half of every step, so the reading that could not observe the verbs is pinned beside the one that can. Until now the remedy in the register was literally 'read the layout slot over raw JSON-RPC'.

IT IS A SECOND VERB, AND THE REASON IS R285's OWN ARGUMENT TURNED ON ITS CALLER. Marking the zoom on the pane listing would make one command join TWO slot reads taken at two instants - which is the torn read Window.zoomed: Option<PaneId> exists to remove. A CLI that joined them would print the same lie more slowly. One verb, one slot, one revision; scoped like `panes` (optional -t, same subject) rather than like the window verbs.

THE RENDERING IS A TREE, AND ITS RULE IS ONE SENTENCE: a divider line reads `RATIO SIDE|SIDE` where the ratio is the FIRST side's share and the two branches below are in that order, so the box glyph says which child and the words say which side. SplitDir::Horizontal draws `left|right` and Vertical `top|bottom`, taken from the type's own documented convention rather than re-decided here. A zoomed leaf is marked `(fills the window)` - the exact words zoom-pane prints when it SETS one, so the verb and the reading cannot drift into two vocabularies - and the float line is additive (absent, not empty) on `sprag agent`'s rule.

IT DESERIALISES THROUGH THE SSOT TYPE. sprag_terminal::LayoutSnapshot, the same one tests/cli.rs already uses off this slot, never a hand-walk of the arena JSON - a second reader of that flat encoding (R264) is a second thing that can come to disagree with the daemon about it. The rendering itself is a pure fn in the binary with one caller; not lifted into a library, because R279's context() is what an abstraction justified by its future use costs.

ONE DEFENSIVE ARM, AND IT IS NOT SPECULATIVE. The daemon's heal_zoom invariant means a zoom always names a tiled leaf, so the marker always lands. The CLI checks whether it did and prints `zoomed: pane N (not in this arrangement)` when it did not - because that invariant is held on the OTHER side of a socket whose whole reason for carrying a WIRE_PROTOCOL number is that the process there can be a different build (R280). Swallowing the field would let this verb draw a tidy arrangement while silently dropping the fact that one pane covers all of it.

THE HERDR COMPARISON IS THE REVERSE OF R284/R285's: HERE THE RIVAL WAS AHEAD AND NOW IS NOT. `herdr pane layout` exists (cli/pane.rs:21, :141). Three findings from opening their functions at 9a4ce5e1: (a) PaneLayoutSnapshot.zoomed is a BOOL (api/schema/panes.rs:543) and the rects in panes[] come from tab.layout.panes(area) (app/api/panes.rs:1689), which never consults tab.zoomed - the zoom is applied only in the paint path (ui/panes.rs:179) - so a caller reading their API while a tab is zoomed gets `zoomed: true` beside every pane's UNZOOMED rect and can only reconstruct the screen by knowing herdr's paint rule; (b) their geometry is ONE ATTACHED TUI's, area = self.state.view.terminal_area (app/api/panes.rs:1686), a field written during render; (c) their CLI prints the raw JSON response, not even pretty-printed (cli.rs:720).

A FALSE SENTENCE IN THE VERB THIS ROUND WAS WRITTEN AGAINST, fixed in its own commit: `panes`'s doc ended 'there is no active pane to mark' - five lines above the code that marks it, which R276 gave the daemon. An inherited claim, false at HEAD. The owed item is often the comment.
