THE RENDERING IS A TREE, AND ITS RULE IS ONE SENTENCE: a divider line reads `RATIO SIDE|SIDE` where the ratio is the FIRST side's share and the two branches below are in that order, so the box glyph says which child and the words say which side. SplitDir::Horizontal draws `left|right` and Vertical `top|bottom`, taken from the type's own documented convention rather than re-decided here. A zoomed leaf is marked `(fills the window)` - the exact words zoom-pane prints when it SETS one, so the verb and the reading cannot drift into two vocabularies - and the float line is additive (absent, not empty) on `sprag agent`'s rule.

IT DESERIALISES THROUGH THE SSOT TYPE. sprag_terminal::LayoutSnapshot, the same one tests/cli.rs already uses off this slot, never a hand-walk of the arena JSON - a second reader of that flat encoding (R264) is a second thing that can come to disagree with the daemon about it. The rendering itself is a pure fn in the binary with one caller; not lifted into a library, because R279's context() is what an abstraction justified by its future use costs.

ONE DEFENSIVE ARM, AND IT IS NOT SPECULATIVE. The daemon's heal_zoom invariant means a zoom always names a tiled leaf, so the marker always lands. Swallowing the field would let this verb draw a tidy arrangement while silently dropping the fact that one pane covers all of it.

changes_bullets: THE GAP WAS MEASURED AT THE TOOL TABLE, NOT INHERITED. sprag-mcp advertised thirteen tools and none read the arrangement, so an agent could make a pane active, read it and type into it while having no way to learn where any of them WERE - it could not resolve 'the pane to the right of mine', which is how a person names a pane. R285 had declined an MCP tool for the zoom on the argument that 'an agent reads and types; a zoom is a thing you do FOR a human to look at'. That argument does not extend to a layout READ, it INVERTS: an inherited justification is dated by the verb it was written about.

THE ADJACENCY MOVED TO THE SHAPE SO THE PUBLISHED FORM CAN BE ASKED. leaf_path / facing_leaves / neighbor walked LayoutNode, the host's own type; LayoutNodeWire is the same shape and is what every client is HANDED, so a reader of a LayoutSnapshot could not ask the question the daemon can answer. A private Arranged trait exposing exactly what the walk needs (a pane, or a division of two sub-trees at a ratio) is implemented for both, the walk is generic over it, and LayoutTree::neighbor and the new LayoutWire::neighbor are two callers of ONE derivation. Split identity is deliberately absent from the trait - it is the one field the two forms differ on, and adjacency does not depend on it. No wire change and no WIRE_PROTOCOL bump: adjacency is a function of an arrangement already published, not a new fact.

THE DRAWING BECAME A LIBRARY FUNCTION WITH A NAMING HOOK. R287's render_layout lived in the sprag bin, so a second surface showing the same arrangement would have been a second writer of one convention - and a human comparing their own `sprag layout` against what their agent reported would have been reading two pictures. It is now sprag_terminal::arrangement::render(&snapshot, &label), in the crate whose conventions it states (SplitDir's first/second order, LayoutSnapshot::zoomed, ::floating), so a change to any of them changes the drawing in the same commit. The LABEL is the reason this is not a copy with a hook: the CLI names a pane by the host id an operator passes to select-pane, the MCP surface by the 1-based number ITS tools take, and rendering both as a bare `pane N` would print the same words for different panes. The float line now uses that naming too, instead of the bare ids it printed beside leaves that said `pane 1`.

THE JOIN IS A TRANSLATION, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE `sprag panes` REFUSES. The numbering is the pane pool's order and the arrangement is a different slot, so the tool reads two. R287 refused to mark the zoom on the pane listing because that join states a FACT assembled from two instants, which can print a state that never existed; this one translates an IDENTITY - a pane's id and its number name the same pane - and its only failure mode is a pane missing from one of the two sets. The pane list is read FIRST so that case is visible: a leaf with no number prints `pane ? (id N, gone since the pane list was read)` rather than being numbered (handing back a number that now belongs to somebody else) or dropped (a pane the daemon is still tiling, vanishing in silence). The moving fact - which pane the user is typing into - is NOT here, and the tool's description says where it is.

'YOU ARE HERE' IS THE ANCHOR, AND IT IS THE ID PUBLISHED WITH THE SOCKET WE ASKED. Without it a direction has nothing to be relative to. It is not a slot read - it is this PROCESS's identity, from SPRAG_PANE in our own environment or the first /proc ancestor carrying one, the resolver host_sock already uses. But a candidate is accepted only when its ADDRESS half is the socket this process actually used: pane ids are per-daemon and start at zero, so a box running two sprag terminals has two pane 1s, and taking the first id in reach would mark a real, plausible pane of the terminal being asked about. The two lookups became one ancestor walk with two readers rather than two walks.

R289.decision_summary: A HUMAN can now fill the window with one pane - zoom-pane joins the binding vocabulary with tmux's own prefix z, both frontends carry it out, and the palette offers a row so it is findable - closing the gap R285 left when it gave the daemon a zoom whose only human caller was a shell command; herdr has shipped prefix+z all along, which makes this the second round in three where the rival was ahead.
changes_bullets: THE GAP WAS MEASURED AT THE VOCABULARY. BoundAction had four variants and none was a zoom, so no key could be bound to one in either frontend by any user. Every zoom string in sprag-gui / sprag-client / sprag-tui was about HONOURING one (the adopted surface is the PROJECTION), never setting one, and HostClient carried split / select_pane / set_layout / set_floating and no zoom. The daemon has had the feature since R285 and its only human caller was a shell command, for a feature whose entire subject is what the window looks like.

R285's OWN REASONS FOR DEFERRING EACH PIECE ARE WHAT ADMITTED IT HERE, neither inherited unread. It declined a key binding because choosing a default key inside the mux crate is a decision made in the wrong place and belongs to the H2 keymap surface: this IS that surface. It declined a HostClient pair because no GUI gesture asked for one yet, and R279's context() is what an abstraction justified by its future use costs: a gesture asks now, so the abstraction is built BY its caller rather than ahead of it.

THE VOCABULARY IS TAKEN WHOLE: zoom-pane, zoom-pane -Z, zoom-pane -u, the CLI verb's own flags, round-tripping through Display. Accepting the verb while refusing its flags would be the fragment-of-a-grammar the select-pane arm warns about. A pane id is refused with split-window's own words, a keystroke acts where the user is; the BARE form is the toggle rather than a refusal, because the CLI reads it the same way and one key has to be a switch. The default table gains z: tmux's key, sprag's verb spelling.

THE CLIENT NAMES THE PANE, though the wire action would default an absent one to the session's active pane. A gesture happened ON a pane and the active pane can move between the gesture and the call, the tear select_pane already sends an id to avoid. ZoomOutcome carries zoomed AND changed rather than flattening to a bool, because R285 made those four cases distinct and a caller handed one flag would guess between two of them.

THE PALETTE ROW IS WHAT MAKES IT FINDABLE. Its title carries BOTH vocabularies on NewPane's recorded rule, the word a tmux or herdr user types and the phrase every other sprag surface prints for the state. It advertises no chord, like NewPane, which also has a keymap binding and lists none. No context-menu row: ToggleFloat, the closest analogue, is palette-only, and a second rule for the second toggle would leave two surfaces disagreeing.

TWO EXISTING TESTS USED z AS THEIR UNBOUND KEY and now say so out loud, moved to k with the assertion itself as the guard. Three prose counts of the action vocabulary were stale the moment the fifth landed and are now written without a number.

THE ONE CLAIM NO TEST PINS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN CLAIMED. THE SMOKE'S FIRST FAILURE WAS THE CHECK, NOT THE PRODUCT, diagnosed by building the discriminator the timeout lacked in three steps: ask the DAEMON's own layout verb (no zoom in force, so the client never asked), ask the client where its FOCUS was (on the pane), and drive the same command from the PALETTE (which worked). What remained was the key path: the keymap gate above deliberately ENDS on a config the client cannot use, so the table in force had the prefix at C-a and C-b armed nothing.

THE RIVAL IS AHEAD ON THIS AXIS AND WAS BEFORE THIS ROUND: herdr 9a4ce5e1 ships a zoom keybind defaulting to prefix+z (src/config/model.rs:989). Where sprag is ahead once reachable: their zoom is a per-TAB bool resolved inside the active tab, so it cannot express zooming a pane of a window nobody is looking at, while sprag DERIVES the window from the pane; they refuse a single-pane tab (app/actions.rs:1925) where sprag accepts it; and they refuse a pane MOVE into or out of a zoomed tab.

publishable_changes_bullets: THE GAP WAS MEASURED AT THE VOCABULARY. BoundAction had four variants and none was a zoom, so no key could be bound to one in either frontend by any user. Every zoom string in sprag-gui / sprag-client / sprag-tui was about HONOURING one (the adopted surface is the PROJECTION), never setting one, and HostClient carried split / select_pane / set_layout / set_floating and no zoom. The daemon has had the feature since R285 and its only human caller was a shell command, for a feature whose entire subject is what the window looks like.

R285's OWN REASONS FOR DEFERRING EACH PIECE ARE WHAT ADMITTED IT HERE, neither inherited unread. It declined a key binding because choosing a default key inside the mux crate is a decision made in the wrong place and belongs to the H2 keymap surface: this IS that surface. It declined a HostClient pair because no GUI gesture asked for one yet, and R279's context() is what an abstraction justified by its future use costs: a gesture asks now, so the abstraction is built BY its caller rather than ahead of it.

THE VOCABULARY IS TAKEN WHOLE: zoom-pane, zoom-pane -Z, zoom-pane -u, the CLI verb's own flags, round-tripping through Display. Accepting the verb while refusing its flags would be the fragment-of-a-grammar the select-pane arm warns about. A pane id is refused with split-window's own words, a keystroke acts where the user is; the BARE form is the toggle rather than a refusal, because the CLI reads it the same way and one key has to be a switch. The default table gains z: tmux's key, sprag's verb spelling.

THE CLIENT NAMES THE PANE, though the wire action would default an absent one to the session's active pane. A gesture happened ON a pane and the active pane can move between the gesture and the call, the tear select_pane already sends an id to avoid. ZoomOutcome carries zoomed AND changed rather than flattening to a bool, because R285 made those four cases distinct and a caller handed one flag would guess between two of them.

THE PALETTE ROW IS WHAT MAKES IT FINDABLE. Its title carries BOTH vocabularies on NewPane's recorded rule, the word a tmux or herdr user types and the phrase every other sprag surface prints for the state. It advertises no chord, like NewPane, which also has a keymap binding and lists none. No context-menu row: ToggleFloat, the closest analogue, is palette-only, and a second rule for the second toggle would leave two surfaces disagreeing.

TWO EXISTING TESTS USED z AS THEIR UNBOUND KEY and now say so out loud, moved to k with the assertion itself as the guard. Three prose counts of the action vocabulary were stale the moment the fifth landed and are now written without a number.

The target is the LAST painted tile, never the first, so a zoom that filled with whichever pane came first cannot pass, and its rect is asserted to GROW, measured 184x510 to 772x510.

FOUR REVERT-PROOFS, EACH KILLING EXACTLY ONE TEST: refusing the zoom's flags fails the round-trip test (1 of 476); dropping z from the default table fails the tmux-table test (1 of 476); zooming a pane the row was not given fails the no-captured-pane test (1 of 294); making the in-process trait answer None fails the trait test (1 of 476).

THE ONE CLAIM NO TEST PINS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN CLAIMED. The wire client re-reads the arrangement when a zoom moved something; REMOVING that block left the smoke GREEN at 136/0, because both frontends converge through the wake the daemon sends. It is kept for sprag-tui, whose key arm reconciles and paints in the same breath off this mirror. Both facts are in the method's own docs.

THE SMOKE'S FIRST FAILURE WAS THE CHECK, NOT THE PRODUCT, diagnosed by building the discriminator the timeout lacked in three steps: ask the DAEMON's own layout verb (no zoom in force, so the client never asked), ask the client where its FOCUS was (on the pane), and drive the same command from the PALETTE (which worked). What remained was the key path: the keymap gate above deliberately ENDS on a config the client cannot use, so the table in force had the prefix at C-a and C-b armed nothing.

THE RIVAL IS AHEAD ON THIS AXIS AND WAS BEFORE THIS ROUND: herdr 9a4ce5e1 ships a zoom keybind defaulting to prefix+z (src/config/model.rs:989). R290.decision_summary: A pane can say WHAT IT IS RUNNING: the foreground job that owns its terminal, sampled through R282's machinery rather than published, indexed by process group so a reparented member is not lost, and served to the CLI and to an agent.
changes_bullets: procfs::Stat is the crate's one parse of a /proc/<pid>/stat line; ports and pane_pty had two, and the second read the file as a String, so a child whose comm the kernel truncated mid-codepoint reported no foreground group at all.
PanePty::tty captures ttyname_r on the slave at openpty and keeps it, so the daemon states a pane's terminal device instead of a caller inferring it from the child's fd 0, which a child may redirect.

Sampled<T> holds the cache and the coalescing that R282 built for sessions; ActivitySampler and the new PaneProcessSampler are its two users, and what stays with each fact is its own sampling function.

PaneProcessSampler answers what every pane is running: its device, its child, and the foreground job that owns its terminal, indexed by process GROUP from one /proc pass, so a job member reparented away from the pane's child is still in the job.

JobProcess carries the kernel comm and the argument VECTOR, never a pre-joined line: joining argv with spaces makes an argument containing a space indistinguishable from two, and publishing both forms would let one fact be read two ways.

pane_processes.<max_age_ms> is a sampled address beside session_activity, registry-wide because /proc has no index by process group, so enumerating one pane's job is the same full pass that answers every other pane.

Samplers bundles the host's sampled facts, one set per host, so an arm cannot mint a sampler where a scene is assembled and silently lose the coalescing while every individual answer still looks right.

sprag processes [PANE] is the third pane verb: panes says WHO, layout says WHERE, this says what is running, and it quotes argv per argument so the one place that flattens the vector cannot claim a lie.

The MCP surface gained pane_processes, re-derived rather than inherited: an agent cannot get this fact another way, because list_panes carries the spawn label, read_pane carries text a build may have scrolled away, and a silent build looks like an idle prompt.
verification_bullets: Suite exit 0 over 45 targets, 1825 passing (1805 before), clippy 0 with no suppression, doc gate 0/16, rustfmt clean.
Headless GUI pixel smoke 136 passed / 0 failed, unchanged from the baseline this round started at.

Each of the eight commits was checked out into its own git worktree and cargo check --workspace --all-targets passed there, because the pre-commit hook checks the working tree and not the staged snapshot.

Discriminating revert-proof for the group index: a job whose member was reparented away (sh -c "sleep 300 &" inside a job that execs into sleep 400) has two members; the descendant walk herdr uses finds one, computed in the same test from the same /proc, and the reparented member's parent was measured as 2258 rather than the pane's shell.
Discriminating revert-proof for the tty: replacing the captured device with a plausible /dev/pts/0 fails the assertion against the child's own /proc/<pid>/fd/0, which read /dev/pts/13.
Discriminating revert-proof for the coalescing: releasing the sampler lock before sampling turns eight concurrent readers from one walk into eight.
Measured on the sprag-latency battery: a fresh pane_processes request is 2751.41 us for every pane at once, a re-read inside the tolerance is 2.66 us.
Every rendered answer was forced to fail and read: the CLI block, the MCP text byte for byte, the live MCP answer over stdio, and the sampled row itself.

The rival was read at 9a4ce5e1 rather than recalled: tty is assigned None at app/api/panes.rs:234 and nowhere else, argv0 is None at platform/linux.rs:151 and :318, cmdline is argv joined by spaces at :152, and members are enumerated through the CONFIG_PROC_CHILDREN-gated /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/children at :281.
carry_forward_bullets: No HostClient method and no GUI consumer were built for this fact, on R285's own argument: nothing draws it yet, and an abstraction justified by its future use is what R279's context() cost. The wire slot and two surfaces are what has callers.

The pane row's provenance is PanePty::pid's gate, and that gate has a narrow residue the crate already lives with: the reader thread publishes the exit after waiting, so a pid read a moment before that publication could in principle be recycled before the walk reaches it. Re-checking after the walk would narrow the window without closing it, so it is stated in the sample's own docs rather than papered over with a check that cannot make the claim it looks like it makes.

sprag pays a full /proc pass where herdr pays a walk of the pane child's subtree, so for ONE pane herdr's is cheaper; sprag buys completeness, kernel-config independence, an age on the answer and one pass for every pane and every concurrent reader. That is a trade and it is recorded as one, not as a win on cost.

Nothing in either frontend renders what a pane is running, and nothing polls the address, so the 2751 us pass is paid only when somebody asks. A status-bar or pane-header consumer is the additive follow-up, and it would be the first caller with a display tolerance rather than zero.
Item 6's remaining herdr cells after this round are pane.rename, tab.move and workspace.move; pane.process_info is closed.

Three controls in the unit test: another refusal keeps its own words, a fault that merely mentions the variant name is left alone, and a fault with no data says nothing about the daemon's age.

R291.decision_summary: A pane's foreground JOB CHANGE becomes an event, because its IDENTITY is 236x-292x cheaper to watch than the answer it names
changes_bullets: Event::PaneJobChanged + JobWatch: the settle sweep samples each pane's foreground process group and announces a move, so a job change is an event rather than something every reader polls for.
A first reading ESTABLISHES and is not news; the census prunes with the agent tracker's, both asserted on one pane close.
One pass now makes ONE announce per session carrying every event it found, so a session with both an agent transition and a job change is woken once.

wait_for_change reports pane_job_changed and names pane_processes as the follow-up read; its subject now travels as the 1-based NUMBER its own tools take, which a comment had claimed and the code did not do.
sprag_terminal::foreground_pgid_of names the read a pid alone can make, so the pass performs no I/O under a workspace lock.

R292.decision_summary: A wait is for the change a caller NAMED, parked on the journal instead of on a revision that pane output bumps 22431 times a second
changes_bullets: MEASURED FIRST, and the register's statement of the gap was too kind: the scene/waitFor + events.<since> pair returned 67293 times in 3 seconds against a build-rate pane (22431/s), every batch EMPTY, where a quiet pane returned 0 — the cursor cannot advance past the journal's head while output runs the revision away from it, so the tool did not block at all.

EventKind + Subject are DERIVED from Event by exhaustive match, and EventKind::wire_str is the one place an event's wire name is spelled — the eleven-arm JSON literal in the serializer is gone, so a filter cannot parse a second word.

EventFilter is any-of clauses over an optional kind and an optional subject: 'pane 3's job changed OR pane 3 closed' is ONE wait, 'any pane closed' is expressible, and every ACCEPTED filter is satisfiable because an unsatisfiable one is a wait that never returns.
JournalChannel holds the journal and its parked replies under ONE lock, so the park decision cannot race an append and no append site can forget the wake; replies are always sent outside it.

events/waitFor is intercepted in dispatch_one beside pinion's try_async_wait_for, parks its reply (the daemon dispatch is one thread for every client), and is released by RpcIngress::on_disconnect — the client's own socket deadline is the only timeout.
wait_for_change takes pane and kinds and makes ONE host call; sprag events -f parks on the journal, so following no longer spins; EventFilter::narrowing_wire is the single builder both surfaces send.
verification_bullets: Suite exit 0 / 45 targets / 1861 tests (+24 on 1837); clippy 0 with no suppression; doc gate 0/16; pixel smoke 136/0 unchanged.

WIRE_PROTOCOL stays 4 and it was RUN this time, both directions against a parent-commit (5eab1f5) worktree: an old client reads and follows the new daemon unchanged, and a new client meets a LOUD refusal from the old one naming the method and its whole supported set.

⚠ A REVERT-PROOF PASSED GREEN AGAIN, one round after R291's: deleting the on_disconnect release left all 507 unit and 40 wire tests passing, because notify's own test calls release DIRECTLY. the_dispatch_loop_releases_a_closed_connections_waits now drives dispatch_frames itself, and the proof then fails on exactly it.

Four other revert-proofs each discriminated first time: the lost term, the unfiltered park decision, the establish-the-shape observe, and the typing-rate gate (whose control is the instrument, not a test).

MEASURED with a control that moves it: with 8 waits parked and a full ring the derive site costs 0.163-0.221 us gated against 1.707-3.024 un-gated, three runs, minima — about 10x the site's own cost, at typing rate.

Live at every surface: a wire test where a filtered wait trips its deadline while scene/waitFor is released by the same daemon's output; a CLI test where -f prints nothing for 2 s then exactly the named change; and the MCP job wait collapsed from R291's re-call loop to ONE call.
Every rendered answer forced to fail and read, including the refusal an operator sees, which was reaching them behind 'host rpc error:' and now reads as the sentence itself.
carry_forward_bullets: A FAILING TEST found the real hole: a park had to ESTABLISH the session's shape, or a client whose first host call is a wait sleeps through the very next change — and the live wire test passed either way because read_revision had already established it.

The MCP description was missing pane_selected while the daemon reported it: R291 registered that prose list as undrifted and it had drifted. It is derived from EventKind::ALL by a test now, which also holds the '5 seconds' sentence against SWEEP_INTERVAL.

I inherited R291's claim that herdr's events.wait does server-side matching and never opened the handler: 18 of its 19 declared EventMatch shapes are refused at runtime, and the mechanism is a 100 ms poll. Seven kinds their daemon emits cannot be named to that verb at all.

JournalChannel holds the journal and its parked replies under ONE lock, so the park decision cannot race an append and no append site can forget the wake; replies are always sent outside it.

R294.decision_summary: An agent may open a pane to work in and is ANSWERABLE for it: the daemon records WHO ASKED for each pane, so the agent surface can refuse to close a pane its caller did not open. Re-derives debt item 14's question and answers it with a different verb than the register assumed — no move/swap/zoom for an agent (those decide what a HUMAN looks at), but yes to opening and closing its own workbench, which is the first step the four rounds of read/wait tooling before it all presupposed. herdr at 9a4ce5e1 closes ANY pane by id with only a worktree-group confirmation, and records nothing about what created a pane, so it has nothing to gate on; honest trades stated: their split takes ratio and env, and their agent surface is their whole 76-method API.
changes_bullets: A pane records the pane whose occupant asked for it: `Pane::opened_by`, published additively on the panes slot, durable across a reboot, and refused at birth when it names a pane the daemon does not hold.

The `spawn` and `split` actions take `opened_by` and `cwd`; the directory is validated as a directory before anything is built, because a spawn into a missing one produces a pane whose child died and reads on screen as a shell that exited for no reason.

`sprag panes` names the opener, so an operator can see which agent's pane opened the one that appeared; `sprag kill-pane` stays ungated, because the daemon publishes a FACT and the agent surface applies a POLICY.
MCP `open_pane` appends a work pane stamped with the asking pane's id, and `close_pane` refuses every pane its caller did not open, naming who did.
The `initialize` primer now names every advertised tool, derived from the roster by a test: it had silently dropped `pane_processes` and `wait_for_change` across two earlier rounds.
verification_bullets: Suite exit 0, 45 targets, 1877 passed (1862 before); clippy 0 with no suppression; doc gate 0/16; headless pixel smoke 136 passed / 0 failed.

Seven revert-proofs, each shown to discriminate: the restore stamping, the snapshot capture, the opener existence check, the panes-slot key, the split path's own argument (which the spawn test does NOT cover), the MCP close gate driven through the real process, and the primer derivation against the exact drift that shipped twice.

WIRE_PROTOCOL stays 4 and it was RUN, not asserted: a parent-commit (5a5d584) release binary in both directions, with the new pair as the control. NEW daemon + OLD cli and OLD daemon + NEW cli both exit 0 and list both panes; only the new pair prints "opened by pane 0". The panes-slot answer is 1072 bytes in every case, which is the additive claim measured rather than argued.

That run FOUND A DEFECT: a same-protocol daemon that predates the field accepts `opened_by` and records nothing, so the open answer's promise of a later close would have been false. The answer now reads the fact BACK off the pane.

NO TIMING CLAIM IS MADE for the pane-list read. `sprag-latency`'s `request panes slot` row spans 11.1-24.2 us run to run at the PARENT commit alone, and a deliberately injected per-pane String allocation moved the byte count (1072 to 1138, so the probe was really in the path) without moving the time. The instrument cannot resolve a change of this size on this box.
carry_forward_bullets: No display client shows the provenance: the GUI pane header and the TUI status line do not, so its only readers are `sprag panes` and `list_panes`.
`sprag split-window` cannot stamp an opener, so the CLI rendering has no CLI-reachable producer and its test puts the fact on the wire the way the agent surface does.
The "opened by: pane id N, not in this window" rendering is unit-reachable only; the live tests cover "you" and "pane N".
`parse_cwd`'s directory check narrows the window it cannot close: a directory removed between the check and the exec still produces a pane whose child died.
The open answer's degraded branch (an older daemon dropped the fact) is pinned pure and unreachable live, because the suite can only build one daemon.
Nothing caps how many panes one opener may hold, on the same trust model already recorded for parked waits.

R295.decision_summary: A pane has a NAME, and the name is how you address it — the stable handle an agent holds where a pane NUMBER silently comes to mean a different pane.
changes_bullets: PaneName parses a pane's operator-given name: trimmed, at most 80 bytes, no control character, never all ASCII digits — the last two are load-bearing, since the listing is a machine-readable contract and a name shares one argument with a pane NUMBER.
Pane::name is durable and registry-unique: on the snapshot, re-stamped by Host::restore, and a snapshot claiming one name twice is malformed exactly as a duplicate id is.

rename_pane {pane, name?} acts DAEMON-WIDE and answers with the name it RECORDED, so no caller re-implements the trimming rule; the two PANE births take a name and the window/session births do not, because their own `name` argument is the container's.
Event::PaneRenamed is DERIVED from the shape diff — a pane's public shape is its ID, which survives a rename, so the argument that struck WindowRenamed admits this one.

The MCP `pane` argument takes a NUMBER or a NAME, told apart by JSON's own types; open_pane names its work pane at birth, rename_pane is close_pane's authorship gate, and pane_layout draws the name beside the number it stands in for.
sprag rename-pane names a pane and sprag panes quotes it; pane_display_title prefers a name a person chose over the title the child rewrites on every prompt.

The panes-slot answer is 611 bytes in BOTH skew rows and 626 once a pane is named — the additive claim MEASURED, with a control that moves the number.

THE ASYMMETRIC HALF DRIVEN LIVE: a NEW sprag-mcp sending `name` to an OLD daemon gets the argument silently dropped, and open_pane reads the fact BACK and WARNS instead of promising a handle that would never resolve — the branch R294's equivalent could only unit-test.

R296.decision_summary: A wait is for the OUTPUT you named: pane/waitForOutput parks until a pane prints what a caller asked for, woken by that output itself rather than by a poll — and it searches what the pane KEPT, so a line that scrolled away while nobody was looking still answers.
changes_bullets: pane/waitForOutput parks a caller until the pane it names has retained output matching a literal `needle` or a regular-expression `pattern` — the blocking tense of the `find.<needle>` / `regex.<pattern>` slots, answering the very same PaneFind so "does it say X" and "wait until it says X" cannot drift into two shapes.

It is a THIRD park, beside pinion's revision waiters and the journal's filtered waits, because output wakes a display client and must not wake a named-change wait: it hangs off the revision (the only token output moves) carrying a PREDICATE, which is what turns a wake into an answer.

The evaluation runs on the DISPATCH OWNER and never on the PTY reader thread the revision observer fires from — a search over a pane's retained output there would back-pressure the terminal itself, which is spawn_reaper's own recorded argument. The observer does two lock-free atomic reads and, on the false-to-true edge only, one non-blocking send.

Park and pass on one thread make the lost wakeup UNREPRESENTABLE rather than avoided: JournalChannel needs a lock spanning decide-and-park because a park races an append on another thread; here there is no separate initial check at all, since a park signals and the ordinary pass answers it.

The armed flag is cleared BEFORE the pass searches, so output landing during a pass queues exactly one more and never zero — and it bounds the cost: a flooding pane puts at most ONE evaluation in flight per session, where the rival pays a full pane read per waiter every 100 ms whatever the pane does.

`sprag wait-for-output --pane N NEEDLE [--regex]` shares find's parser and its PANE:LINE: format; the MCP `wait_for_output` takes a pane NUMBER or NAME, and its refusals reach the agent as the daemon's own sentence rather than behind `host rpc error:`.
verification_bullets: Suite exit 0 / 45 targets / 1923 passed (from 1909), clippy 0 with no suppression, doc gate 0/16, pre-commit green on all 5 commits.

SKEW RUN in BOTH directions against parent-commit (0a0c986) RELEASE binaries, and on BOTH surfaces: OLD cli + NEW daemon refuses `unknown command "wait-for-output"` with usage, exit 1; NEW cli + OLD daemon refuses `'pane/waitForOutput' is unsupported; use one of: ...` naming every method it does serve, exit 1 read from a REDIRECT and never a pipeline; NEW sprag-mcp + OLD daemon answers isError with that same sentence. A new METHOD is LOUD where R294's new ARGUMENT was silently dropped.

Six revert-proofs each shown to DISCRIMINATE: the loop's OutputMoved arm (timed out), the park's own first evaluation (no reply), the disconnect release of an output wait (1 left parked), a refused pattern treated as keep-waiting (no reply), the pane-existence gate (no refusal), and the parked_any gate (20 bumps signalled 20 times).

THE ORDERING CLAIM NEEDED A TEST BUILT FOR IT AND SIXTEEN OTHERS WERE BLIND TO IT: clearing the armed flag before or after the search is indistinguishable to every test that does not overlap a pass with output. `output_that_lands_during_a_pass_queues_the_next_pass` makes the search itself bump the revision, and it is the ONLY test that fails when the clear is moved after.

The pass is PRICED with a control that MOVES it: 34.441 us searching a pane with nothing kept against 338.227 us at the DEFAULT_SCROLLBACK_LINES cap — 9.82x — and a pattern is 0.96x a literal, so the walk is the term that counts and not the engine. The control's own assertion caught the first version of it, which expected 2000 lines kept where the cap makes only 1000 possible.

End-to-end latency is BOUNDED, NOT RESOLVED, and that is reported rather than a null result: a live wait answered 3.3-4.1 ms after the write, including two `sprag send-keys` process spawns, and the same two spawns alone measured 3.9-8.0 ms — spanning the figure. The bound is what the claim rests on: under ~4 ms against a rival whose sleep alone is 100 ms.

Every rendered answer forced to fail and READ, on both surfaces, which caught a defect: the MCP timeout leaked `Transport(Custom { kind: WouldBlock, ... })` to an agent beside a sentence saying nothing had failed, AND reported every transport error as "not yet" — so a dead daemon would have told an agent its build was still running. Now the deadline is matched on ErrorKind and anything else is an error.

A live MCP integration test drives all four properties against a real daemon and a real PTY, including the scrolled-off discriminator with its own control (the marker is absent from the recent window a polling reader would look at, and is still matched).
carry_forward_bullets: NEW debt item 22 (R296): a flooding pane with a parked wait on a full scrollback occupies 338 us of the DISPATCH OWNER per burst, which is the one thread every client's requests pass through — priced, bounded by the armed flag, and the first number to look at if a workspace ever parks many waits.

A DELTA search would be cheaper and would be WRONG, recorded so it is not "optimised" in later: a terminal line can change without being appended (a progress bar rewrites in place), so "what is new since the last pass" is not a well-defined question about a screen. Searching everything is what makes the answer correct.

The wait carries NO deadline and NO `revision` in its answer. The deadline is the caller's socket read deadline, on notify.rs's existing argument (the daemon holds no clock); herdr's server-side `timeout_ms` is a real ergonomic advantage and is conceded. R298.decision_summary: PINION-PR83 is CONSUMED: events/subscribe answers once and the daemon then speaks unprompted, so a follower pays one request for a whole session instead of one per change — measured 9 requests down to 3 against a parent-commit control, and the rival's counterpart is a 100 ms poll that loses what lands while a client is away.
changes_bullets: **PINION-PR83 IS CONSUMED.** pinion R1552 (`8be57209`) delivered `RpcEgress` — a per-connection writer, the PR's shape (B) rather than the preferred (A) — and `events/subscribe {since, match?}` is sprag's consumer of it: one request answered once, and thereafter one `events/changed` NOTIFICATION per batch, unprompted, until `events/unsubscribe` or the connection ends it. Plus the pin bump itself (`49cd8477` -> `9673cafe`, 10 crates, SCE unchanged at `201783c4` and checked).

The surface was already three-quarters built and this completes it: the `events.<since>` SLOT is the read, `events/waitFor` is the one-shot, and this is the FOLLOW — one cursor vocabulary, one batch shape, one filter grammar across all three, so a caller moves between them without rewriting its reader. The wait STAYS: an agent asking "tell me when the build finishes" wants one answer, and a tool call cannot hold a stream.

A subscription is a park that ADVANCES where a wait FIRES ONCE, which is the whole of what the upstream change bought — so it is a second vector rather than a flag, because the two differ in whether the entry survives its own delivery.

The cursor advances UNDER THE APPEND'S OWN LOCK, which is the delivery-exactly-once guarantee: a second append cannot observe the old cursor because it cannot take the lock until the pass has written the new one back. Advancing BEFORE the write is the safer order, and the docs say why (a peer that cannot be written to has no reader to re-offer a record to; the other order re-sends every batch to a client whose socket buffer was merely full).

Registered DISARMED and armed after the opening response — pinion's own shape for the same sub-microsecond hazard: a change landing in between would name a subscription id the client has not read, which it can only discard, with the cursor already past it. Arming then delivers through the ordinary pass, so there is no catch-up fork.

`HostConn`'s reader had to learn to DISCRIMINATE, and this is the sharpest correctness in the round: it read the next line as its answer, which was exactly right for as long as a daemon could only answer. A notification arriving first would have been read as a `result` and then lost for good. It now matches on `id` (JSON-RPC 2.0, section 4.1) and SETS ASIDE what is not its own, delivered by `next_notification` rather than dropped.

`sprag events -f` opens ONE subscription instead of re-issuing a wait per batch. FIXED while reading the skew output: its first rendering carried `host rpc error:` before the daemon's own sentence — item 20's class, and R296's fix shape on the verb beside it, so every fault this call can raise is now rendered as the daemon wrote it.
verification_bullets: Suite EXIT 0, 45 targets, 1937 passed (R297 left 1929; +8 is exactly the eight new tests). clippy 0 no suppression, doc gate 0/16, fmt clean, pixel smoke 136/0. The pin bump was verified on its own first, with the SAME numbers R297 ended on (1929) — so the bump and the feature are separable claims.

MEASURED, with a PARENT-COMMIT CONTROL, and the instrument is `strace` counting the follower's socket sends against a change count that MOVES: the parent (`events/waitFor`) sends 4 requests for 1 change and 9 for 6 — one per batch, exactly as designed; R298 sends 3 for either, flat, while the lines it prints grow 110 -> 128. That is the round's whole claim and it is a number rather than an argument.

⚠ AND THE FIRST INSTRUMENT MEASURED NOTHING — `--since 999` is past the journal's end, so both arms printed zero lines and both showed 3 sends. `lines=0` is what said the probe never entered the path. *Read what a number sits next to before believing it*, and this one nearly reported a null result as a win.

⚠ A REVERT-PROOF PASSED, AND IT FOUND A VACUOUS HALF. Deleting the streaming call from `announce` left the round's own subscription test GREEN, because a spawn reaches a follower through `observe` (the shape diff) and never through `announce` — the SWEEPER's path, where a job change is recorded when nobody performed anything. A subscription following `pane_job_changed` would have been silent for ever with nothing failing. `the_announce_site_writes_to_a_subscription_too` now covers it, and the two tests fail on opposite edits. **SIXTH round running that the largest gap in a round's tests came from breaking the code rather than reading it.**

SEVEN revert-proofs, each shown to DISCRIMINATE: no push at either derive site (two, each failing only its own test), a cursor that does not advance (the second delivery repeats pane 1), registered ARMED, an arm that delivers nothing, a reader that takes the next line (the call answers Null), and a reader that DROPS the set-aside frame (the follow blocks to its deadline).

SKEW RUN, both surfaces of it: a NEW `sprag events -f` against a PARENT-COMMIT daemon in a worktree (own socket, own XDG config/data/state, `/proc/<pid>/exe` read back as the control) is refused BY NAME — `'events/subscribe' is unsupported; use one of: …`, exit 1, read from a redirect. So a new METHOD is additive and LOUD, and `WIRE_PROTOCOL` STAYS 4 for R296's already-measured reason. Reading that output is what found the `host rpc error:` leak.
carry_forward_bullets: Against herdr at `9a4ce5e1`, and the comparison is now the other way round on this axis: their `events.subscribe` is a per-connection thread doing `subscription.poll(...)` then `sleep(CONNECTION_POLL_INTERVAL)` — 100 ms (`src/api/server.rs:29`) — over an `EventHub` that is a 512-cap `Vec` scanned linearly and cloned. sprag's is released by the APPEND, under the append's own lock, so a change reaches a follower as fast as the daemon can write a frame.

And the CONTRACT is stronger, not just the mechanism: `since` is the cursor the caller has already accounted for, so a reconnecting client resumes EXACTLY where it left off. herdr's subscribe starts at `events_after(current_sequence())`, which silently loses whatever landed while the client was away. That difference was predicted in the PR83 doc before the transport existed; it is now built.

HONEST TRADES: herdr's subscription surface is richer (typed `EventMatch` shapes sprag's filter does not have every case of), and their `events.wait` / `pane.wait_for_output` sugar remains. sprag has no MCP tool for the subscription and cannot have one usefully — a tool call is one-shot, so `wait_for_change` stays the agent's form.

NEXT on this seam: the GUI and TUI still park on `scene/waitFor` per wake, which is the OTHER re-issue loop and the one a display client runs at typing rate. It is now expressible as a subscription; whether it SHOULD be is a separate derivation, because a display client's question really is "re-read", and a revision is a generation counter rather than a log.

The surface was already three-quarters built and this completes it: the `events.<since>` SLOT is the read, `events/waitFor` is the one-shot, and this is the FOLLOW — one cursor vocabulary, one batch shape, one filter grammar across all three, so a caller moves between them without rewriting its reader. The wait STAYS: an agent asking "tell me when the build finishes" wants one answer, and a tool call cannot hold a stream.

A subscription is a park that ADVANCES where a wait FIRES ONCE, which is the whole of what the upstream change bought — so it is a second vector rather than a flag, because the two differ in whether the entry survives its own delivery.

The cursor advances UNDER THE APPEND'S OWN LOCK, which is the delivery-exactly-once guarantee: a second append cannot observe the old cursor because it cannot take the lock until the pass has written the new one back. Advancing BEFORE the write is the safer order, and the docs say why (a peer that cannot be written to has no reader to re-offer a record to; the other order re-sends every batch to a client whose socket buffer was merely full).

Registered DISARMED and armed after the opening response — pinion's own shape for the same sub-microsecond hazard: a change landing in between would name a subscription id the client has not read, which it can only discard, with the cursor already past it. Arming then delivers through the ordinary pass, so there is no catch-up fork.

`HostConn`'s reader had to learn to DISCRIMINATE, and this is the sharpest correctness in the round: it read the next line as its answer, which was exactly right for as long as a daemon could only answer. A notification arriving first would have been read as a `result` and then lost for good. It now matches on `id` (JSON-RPC 2.0, section 4.1) and SETS ASIDE what is not its own, delivered by `next_notification` rather than dropped.

`sprag events -f` opens ONE subscription instead of re-issuing a wait per batch. FIXED while reading the skew output: its first rendering carried `host rpc error:` before the daemon's own sentence — item 20's class, and R296's fix shape on the verb beside it, so every fault this call can raise is now rendered as the daemon wrote it.
publishable_verification_bullets: Suite EXIT 0, 45 targets, 1937 passed (R297 left 1929; +8 is exactly the eight new tests). clippy 0 no suppression, doc gate 0/16, fmt clean, pixel smoke 136/0. The pin bump was verified on its own first, with the SAME numbers R297 ended on (1929) — so the bump and the feature are separable claims.

MEASURED, with a PARENT-COMMIT CONTROL, and the instrument is `strace` counting the follower's socket sends against a change count that MOVES: the parent (`events/waitFor`) sends 4 requests for 1 change and 9 for 6 — one per batch, exactly as designed; R298 sends 3 for either, flat, while the lines it prints grow 110 -> 128. That is the round's whole claim and it is a number rather than an argument.

⚠ AND THE FIRST INSTRUMENT MEASURED NOTHING — `--since 999` is past the journal's end, so both arms printed zero lines and both showed 3 sends. `lines=0` is what said the probe never entered the path. *Read what a number sits next to before believing it*, and this one nearly reported a null result as a win.

⚠ A REVERT-PROOF PASSED, AND IT FOUND A VACUOUS HALF. Deleting the streaming call from `announce` left the round's own subscription test GREEN, because a spawn reaches a follower through `observe` (the shape diff) and never through `announce` — the SWEEPER's path, where a job change is recorded when nobody performed anything. A subscription following `pane_job_changed` would have been silent for ever with nothing failing. `the_announce_site_writes_to_a_subscription_too` now covers it, and the two tests fail on opposite edits. **SIXTH round running that the largest gap in a round's tests came from breaking the code rather than reading it.**

SEVEN revert-proofs, each shown to DISCRIMINATE: no push at either derive site (two, each failing only its own test), a cursor that does not advance (the second delivery repeats pane 1), registered ARMED, an arm that delivers nothing, a reader that takes the next line (the call answers Null), and a reader that DROPS the set-aside frame (the follow blocks to its deadline).

SKEW RUN, both surfaces of it: a NEW `sprag events -f` against a PARENT-COMMIT daemon in a worktree (own socket, own XDG config/data/state, `/proc/<pid>/exe` read back as the control) is refused BY NAME — `'events/subscribe' is unsupported; use one of: …`, exit 1, read from a redirect. So a new METHOD is additive and LOUD, and `WIRE_PROTOCOL` STAYS 4 for R296's already-measured reason. Reading that output is what found the `host rpc error:` leak.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: Against herdr at `9a4ce5e1`, and the comparison is now the other way round on this axis: their `events.subscribe` is a per-connection thread doing `subscription.poll(...)` then `sleep(CONNECTION_POLL_INTERVAL)` — 100 ms (`src/api/server.rs:29`) — over an `EventHub` that is a 512-cap `Vec` scanned linearly and cloned. sprag's is released by the APPEND, under the append's own lock, so a change reaches a follower as fast as the daemon can write a frame.

And the CONTRACT is stronger, not just the mechanism: `since` is the cursor the caller has already accounted for, so a reconnecting client resumes EXACTLY where it left off. herdr's subscribe starts at `events_after(current_sequence())`, which silently loses whatever landed while the client was away. That difference was predicted in the PR83 doc before the transport existed; it is now built.

HONEST TRADES: herdr's subscription surface is richer (typed `EventMatch` shapes sprag's filter does not have every case of), and their `events.wait` / `pane.wait_for_output` sugar remains. sprag has no MCP tool for the subscription and cannot have one usefully — a tool call is one-shot, so `wait_for_change` stays the agent's form.

NEXT on this seam: the GUI and TUI still park on `scene/waitFor` per wake, which is the OTHER re-issue loop and the one a display client runs at typing rate. It is now expressible as a subscription; whether it SHOULD be is a separate derivation, because a display client's question really is "re-read", and a revision is a generation counter rather than a log.

Item 9's PINION-PR82 is STILL OPEN — verified at pinion's own `origin/main`, not inherited: `InvokeError::Rejected` is a payload-less unit variant (`pinion-core/src/external.rs:960`), so every "refused, and the CLI cannot say which" entry stands.

R299.decision_summary: An agent moves a person's focus by DIRECTION in one call, and every select says WHICH of four things happened — so "nothing that way" stops reading as "already there". Measured: 4 host round trips down to 2 for the same move, with the torn read gone; the rival spends one reason word where the daemon knows two, and derives its direction from the rects of its last composed frame.
changes_bullets: **AN AGENT CAN MOVE A PERSON'S FOCUS BY DIRECTION, IN ONE CALL.** MCP `select_pane` takes `pane` XOR `dir`, which closes debt item 23's head. The wire arm has resolved a direction against the arrangement under ONE registry lock since the placement verbs shipped (R284) and gained a keybinding at R297; the agent surface was the one caller that could not reach it, so "put them on the pane to the left" was a `pane_layout` read at one instant and a `select_pane` by number at another — the torn read a pane NAME exists to prevent, rebuilt out of two correct tools.

**`PaneStep` — `To(pane)` / `Edge` / `Untiled`, because the two ways to go nowhere are DIFFERENT FACTS.** An edge is a boundary a movement ran into; an untiled origin (a FLOATING active pane) has no adjacency to walk at all. It costs nothing to produce: the `leaf_path` walk `LayoutTree::neighbor` has always begun with already decides it, and `neighbor` is now THIS answer with the reason dropped — one walk, two forms, so no caller can reach a second definition of "the pane to the left".

**`SelectHow` — the answer's new `outcome` key: `moved` / `already_active` / `at_edge` / `untiled`.** TOTAL over the request grammar with exactly one cause per word, which is what makes a sentence exact rather than a list of possibilities (`ZoomOutcome`'s own rule, one verb over). `SelectHow::changed()` is the ONE derivation of the `changed` key beside it, so the bool and the word cannot disagree.

**THE DAEMON SAYS THE REASON BECAUSE ONE OF THE FOUR CANNOT BE DERIVED.** Three are recoverable by a caller that remembers which arm it asked, and `SelectHow::read` does exactly that against a daemon too old to answer the key. Telling "nothing that way" from "the pane you are on is floating, so there is no that-way" takes the arrangement — and a client that read the arrangement to explain its own move would join two instants to describe one action, which is this round's own defect one layer up.

**FOUR OUTCOMES, FOUR SENTENCES, at both text surfaces, from PURE renderers** (`select_sentence`, `render_selection`) so every one is pinned by a unit test rather than only the ones a live daemon is easy to drive into. `sprag select-pane -L` at the left edge now prints `nothing to the left of 0` where it printed `already on 0` — an answer to a question the caller had not asked, and one `tests/cli.rs` had asserted, so the suite agreed with it for as long as it existed.

**FIXED, and it is item 23's own sharpest second-pass finding: `flag_of` could PANIC in a `Display` impl.** The directional flags were a `[(&str, PaneDir); 4]` table with a reverse lookup that `.expect()`ed every direction to be in it, so a fifth `PaneDir` variant broke neither the array nor `PaneDir::ALL` and the first thing to notice would have been `sprag list-keys` panicking. It is an exhaustive `match` now — that variant fails to COMPILE where the vocabulary is decided — and `direction_of` is derived from it and public, which killed `sprag select-pane`'s OWN third copy of the table (a flag mapped straight to a wire word, skipping `PaneDir` altogether).

**FIXED — the `select_pane` doc block had sat above `tool_open_pane` for four rounds**, glued to the front of its doc by a missing blank line, so the select tool had no doc at all and the open tool's began by describing a different verb.
verification_bullets: Suite EXIT 0, 45 targets, 1945 passed (R298 left 1937; +8 is exactly the eight new tests — the flake fix below added a HELPER, not a test, and the count says so). clippy 0 with no new suppression, doc gate 0/16 — it CAUGHT a link the `neighbor_in` -> `step_in` rename broke — fmt clean, pixel smoke 136/0.

MEASURED, with a control that MOVES: what an agent pays to move a person's focus one pane right, same binary, same daemon, same end state. `pane_layout` + `select_pane {pane}` = **4 host round trips** across two instants; `select_pane {dir}` = **2**, one instant. `strace` counting `connect(2)` to the socket, which is exact because every host call opens its own connection. The number moved (5 -> 4 on the control arm) when the audit removed a third call, which is what says the instrument reads the code under test rather than a constant.

⚠ THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN ANSWER TEXT CAUGHT A STALE BINARY, and it looked exactly like a wire bug. The measured arm reported `nothing to the right of pane 1` while the CLI and a raw socket probe both MOVED from the same state. The traced frame said why: `{"dir":"left"}` for a request that said `right` — the `sprag-mcp` on disk was the one built during a revert-proof. **A revert-proof restores the SOURCE, not the BINARY**, and four probes went into a defect that did not exist. *Read what a number sits next to* — here it was a sentence, and it was the sentence that was wrong.

⚠ A REVERT-PROOF EXPOSED A VACUOUS ASSERTION OF MY OWN. The CLI test compared `select_sentence(...)` against `format!("nothing {} 0", dir.beyond())` — the string it formats itself — so `beyond()` could have returned anything and it would still have passed (proved by changing one phrase and watching it stay green). Now four literals. **This is the register's `list-keys` `-r` entry repeated by the round that was reading it.**

⚠ AND A REVERT-PROOF SHOWED WHAT THE LIVE TESTS CANNOT SEE: dropping the `outcome` key from the daemon's answer leaves the live MCP test GREEN, because the client's own fallback derives `at_edge` from `changed: false` plus the arm it asked. That is the skew contract working, not a hole — so the key is pinned by the unit tests and DEMONSTRATED by the raw probe below, and the one word no caller can derive (`untiled`) has NO live driver at either surface, because nothing on the CLI or the MCP surface can float a pane (item 14's gap, reaching this round).

TEN revert-proofs, each shown to discriminate: `Untiled` collapsed into `Edge` (two tests, in two crates); both nowhere arms answering `at_edge`; the answer without its `outcome` key; `changed()` widened past `Moved`; `SelectHow::read` ignoring the word it is given; the MCP tool sending a FIXED direction instead of the one asked (the live test fails); the edge arm deleted from each of the two renderers (the agent's live test fails with it); a respelled `-R` in the flag match; and `beyond()` respelled, which is the one that found the vacuous assertion.

SKEW RUN, BOTH DIRECTIONS, against a parent-commit daemon in a worktree (own socket, own XDG config/data/state, `/proc/<pid>/exe` read back as the control, and a MOVE first to prove the arm is live). NEW client -> OLD daemon: the raw answers to `{dir:left}` and `{pane:0}` are the SAME BYTES — `{"changed":false,"pane":0}` — which is the defect measured rather than argued, and the new CLI still prints `nothing to the left of 0` from its fallback. OLD client -> NEW daemon: the two answers now differ (`at_edge` / `already_active`) and the old CLI ignores the key it does not know. **`WIRE_PROTOCOL` STAYS 4**: an added ANSWER KEY is absent-not-wrong to a new client, unlike R294's added ARGUMENT, which an old daemon accepts and drops.

⚠ A FULL-SUITE RUN FAILED ONCE, ON R297's LIVE TUI TEST, AND IT WAS THE CHECK. `pane 0 holds "beforeed"`: five characters of the marker had gone to the pane the client had not left yet. The wait was on the DAEMON's `active` flag, and a client routes keystrokes through its own mirror, which follows on its next wake — the mechanism the sibling test one screen down already documents. Now `typing_follows` types one `.` at a time until one MORE of them is on the destination pane's screen (counted, not looked for: a shell prompt may already hold a dot). Passing under load is not provable by re-running, and this claim is the mechanism plus the fix, not an absence.
carry_forward_bullets: Against herdr at `9a4ce5e1`, HONEST TRADES FIRST: their `pane.focus_direction` takes an OPTIONAL ORIGIN pane (`PaneFocusDirectionParams.pane_id`), so a caller can ask "left of THAT pane" where sprag's arm always starts from the active one — and their answer carries the whole layout snapshot, so their caller re-reads nothing. Both are real, and the first is the wider gap.

THE MECHANISM WIN, at their source: `directional_pane_target` is `tab.layout.panes(self.state.view.terminal_area)` fed to `find_in_direction`, which compares RECTANGLES — and `view.terminal_area` is the last COMPOSED FRAME's area, so the answer moves with a sidebar, a tab bar and cell rounding, and needs a client attached at all. sprag's is the arrangement's split ratios as fractions: the same answer for every client, at every size, with nothing attached.

THE DISCRIMINATION WIN: `let reason = target.is_none().then_some(PaneFocusDirectionReason::NoNeighbor);` — one word for both cases, and `directional_pane_target` answers `None` at an edge AND when the source pane is absent from the rects it last drew (`panes.iter().find(|pane| pane.id == source_pane_id)?`). sprag names which, because the daemon knows which. R297 conceded this axis ("their message is better") and it is now the other way round.

THE ORIGIN ARGUMENT IS NOT BOLTED ON, and the reason is R294's: an added wire ARGUMENT is silently ACCEPTED AND DROPPED by an older daemon, so it would land the user somewhere unexpected off a request that parsed. It costs a `WIRE_PROTOCOL` bump plus a derivation against `select_toward`'s own "neither end is the client's fact" argument. Registered as item 25, not built.

`HostClient::select_toward` STILL RETURNS `Option<PaneId>` and drops the reason the wire now carries. Deliberate: no display client has anything to say with it yet, and threading a fact for a future caller is what R279's `context()` cost. The debt narrows from "nobody can know" to "the trait drops what the wire now carries".

`PaneDir::ALL` REMAINS AN ARRAY LITERAL NO COMPILER CHECKS. `flag_of`'s match now makes a new variant a compile error where the vocabulary is decided, so it can no longer be RENDERED wrongly; a variant left out of `ALL` would still fail to PARSE silently. Rust has no stable way to derive the array, so the residual is named in the function's own docs rather than hidden.

NEXT on this seam, in order: the origin argument above (item 25's head); `swap-pane -L|-R|-U|-D` as a bound action, still the cheapest thing in the herdr comparison; and a harness for the coverage residuals, now ELEVEN across items 15/16/18/19/20/22/23/24/25 and overdue by seven rounds.

R300.decision_summary: select_pane takes an ORIGIN, so an agent can ask for the pane next to a named one - or next to its own - in a single instant, and the wire protocol number moves because an added ARGUMENT is silently dropped where an added answer key is not
changes_bullets: select_pane's request grammar became a TYPE (SelectAsk: `pane` XOR `dir`+`from?`), parsed by the daemon and built by all four clients, so three wire keys are spelled once where the CLI, the MCP tool and the shared wire client each wrote their own literal.
The `dir` arm takes an ORIGIN: `from` names the pane the step is measured from, absent meaning the ACTIVE pane, which is what a keypress means and what the CLI and the keybinding still always mean.

A step that goes nowhere leaves the user on the ACTIVE pane, never on the origin, and the two nothing-happened sentences name the ORIGIN at both text surfaces because with an origin they are two different panes.

An origin the current window does not hold is REFUSED, not answered `untiled`: a pane of another window is not "in no arrangement", and `step` cannot tell those apart because a tree holds no leaf for either.

R303.decision_summary: A display client VIEWS a session; it does not re-send a name. The scope grammar gains an attachment arm, an attachment ends with its session, and the name the client paints becomes a mirror.
changes_bullets: A display client's scope is its ATTACHMENT, not a session name: ScopeAsk gains an Attached arm ({"attached": true}), defined once in sprag-rpc for both ends of the wire, and refused whole in four named ways (NotAString / AttachedNotABool / TwoScopes / NotAttached).

An attachment now ENDS when its session is killed (AttachmentRegistry::session_ended, called where handle_session_kill publishes the departure) — a shipping defect: list-clients named a dead session and the next session of that name inherited its viewer.

A new SESSION_SLOT answers the name of the session a request is scoped to, and the client MIRRORS it on each poll wake, because a client that no longer holds a name still has to PAINT one (the sidebar row, the palette mark, the next/previous walk, sprag-tui's terminal title).

WIRE_PROTOCOL 5 to 6: the second bump caused by an added ARGUMENT, and the one with the worst skipped-bump failure yet — a pre-R303 daemon reads {"attached":true} as an ABSENT scope, i.e. the default session, for every read and every keystroke.
verification_bullets: MEASURED FIRST at 2402e62: a real `sprag attach alpha --tui` EXITED on rename-session while a control renaming another session left it alive; a raw probe then showed the sharper half — after a new session took the retired name the same read SUCCEEDED, against a session the client never named, while list-clients still reported it on the renamed one.
Suite EXIT 0 / 45 targets / 1995 (R302 left 1982), clippy 0 no new suppression, fmt, doc gate 0/16, pixel smoke 136/0 on a REBUILT release set.

TEN revert-proofs each shown to DISCRIMINATE, plus one that did NOT: breaking SESSION_SLOT to answer the default left the live TUI test green because that fixture's client WAS on the default session; the claim was re-aimed at the socket test, where the viewed session is not the default.

Skew run BOTH directions against a parent-commit daemon, with a live rename as the control that moves: an unbumped client attached to `alpha` read DEFAULTWIN off the old daemon (the silent wrong target, measured), the same probe reads ALPHAWIN off this one, and both builds refuse the other by name.
The added per-wake read priced against three controls on one connection (release): session 14.97us / 43B, windows 17.14us, sessions 16.54us, panes 19.19us — the cheapest of the four.
carry_forward_bullets: sprag-gui has no live driver for a rename: the seam is shared sprag-client code driven live by the TUI test, and the pixel smoke renames nothing.

The MRU stack still holds NAMES, so `switch-client -l` to a visited session whose name was retired and re-issued lands on the impostor — the same capture one verb over, visible and recoverable rather than silent, and with no cheap fix while an identity stays off the wire by R302's own decision.
The lock order the attached arm depends on (attachments then registry, never nested) is reasoned from the code shape and driven by nothing.
An MCP agent still scopes by name and cannot ask for an attachment, because it never attaches — the attached scope serves clients that attach, by construction.

R304.decision_summary: A client REMEMBERS a session, not a name: the visit history moves to the daemon keyed by SessionId, client/attach learns to ask for it, and WIRE_PROTOCOL goes 6 to 7
changes_bullets: A client's session VISIT history moved to the daemon, keyed by SessionId: AttachmentRegistry::client_history plus last_viewed, which resolves through SessionRegistry::name_of (liveness and the current name in one lookup) and prunes ids that no longer resolve.

client/attach gained a TARGET grammar spelled once in sprag-rpc (AttachAsk): {"last": true}, narrowed by {"unattached": true} for tmux detach-on-destroy no-detached, with three refusals so an unreadable target never falls through to "the session you are already on". The reply became the session NAME the client landed on, or null when a history ask found none.

R306.decision_summary: a key can ask a question: the prompt surface both frontends lacked, and the window name grammar it needed
changes_bullets: WindowName: the third name grammar, enforced at all three doors a window name enters by (new-window, rename-window, break-pane -n), with all-digits allowed because the registry mints 0/1/2.
rename_window ANSWERS the name it recorded, as rename_pane (R295) and rename_session (R302) already did; WIRE_PROTOCOL 8 -> 9, the first bump caused by a REFUSAL rather than an argument or an answer.

sprag_host::prompt: the ASK is a value (Line{subject,seed} / Confirm{question,consequence,verb,action}), Ask::of is the ONE place deciding which actions ask, and Subject::commit is the ONE implementation of what an answer does.

Line: a cursor-aware, GRAPHEME-stepping line editor with the readline chords (C-a/C-e/C-u/C-k/C-w) for a client with no text widget; it reports a byte offset, never a column, because width belongs to the surface that paints.
BoundAction gains rename-window / rename-session / rename-pane / confirm-before <action>; the guard is recursive over the same grammar and refuses to wrap an action that already asks.

Defaults: prefix , and prefix $ (tmux's own keys), prefix & = confirm-before kill-window (tmux's key WITH tmux's guard, which R305 had to ship unbound), prefix P (herdr's key, where tmux has no pane-rename verb).
HostClient::rename_window / rename_session / rename_pane — the seam both frontends lacked, so sprag-gui has a live rename driver for the first time (item 29's remaining head).

sprag-tui paints a one-row overlay rather than reserving a row: a reserved row would resize every OTHER attached client's panes, since this client's area is what the daemon arbitrates the window size from.
sprag-gui gets a modal name prompt beside its confirmation, and confirm.rs now guards a BOUND ACTION as well as a catalog command.

FIX: SHIFT is not a modifier on a printable character. winit reports Shift+5 as "%" WITH shift set and a pty reports "%" with none, so prefix % — a tmux default shipped since the keymap existed — did nothing in the GUI on a real keyboard.

FIX: the GUI prompt seeds its field with TextEditState::seed, so the caret starts at the END as the terminal client's does; set_text alone left it at zero and the first keystroke landed in front of the name.
verification_bullets: Suite EXIT 0 / 46 targets / 2025 passed (R305 left 2014), clippy 0 with no new suppression, fmt, doc gate 0/16.

SIX revert-proofs each shown to DISCRIMINATE (the grammar at the rename door, the recorded answer, the key opening a prompt, the prompt owning the keyboard, the editor stepping by cluster, a guard refusing to guard a question), plus a CONTROL edit shown to stay green; two more proven separately (the shift fix in sprag-gui, and the caret seed, which the pixel smoke caught live).

R307.decision_summary: A boundary between panes is a thing you can say: the daemon gains its first divider op, the axis picks the boundary and the direction moves it, the distance is in cells, and five words say WHICH nothing happened.
changes_bullets: resize_pane {pane?,dir,cells?} is the daemon's FIRST op that moves a divider; before it the only gesture in the whole product that could change a split's share was a pointer drag in sprag-gui, so sprag-tui could not resize at all

the boundary is chosen by the AXIS (LayoutTree::divider_on, the nearest ancestor split, no side skip) and moved by the DIRECTION, so -R takes it right and whether the pane grows follows from which side it sits on — tmux's behaviour in one sentence with no case analysis
the distance is in CELLS and the conversion is the daemon's alone: a cell becomes a share against the split's region under the ARBITRATED window, which no client holds even in principle

Divider::stepped shares one private inverse with the pointer drag's ratio_at, so the clamp that keeps a cell on each side and the half-cell that makes the inverse exact are written once for both gestures
ResizeHow answers five words (resized / at_minimum / at_edge / untiled / zoomed), each with one cause and one remedy, where the rival's resize_pane answers a bool
a zoomed window is REPORTED and NOT moved: R285 made the zoom a projection so the arrangement is untouched by it, and acting invisibly is worse than doing nothing
the window-size precondition is checked FIRST, so one verb has one contract — a test found a one-pane window answering at_edge where a two-pane one refused

sprag resize-pane gains -L|-R|-U|-D [N] beside -x -y; resize-pane -L|-R|-U|-D [N] joins the binding vocabulary with tmux's EIGHT repeating defaults (prefix C-Arrow at one cell, M-Arrow at five), which the keymap's own comment had recorded as the family sprag had no verb for

HostClient::resize_toward is carried out by both frontends; MCP resize_pane is gated on the same provenance close/rename/swap use, on an argument that is this verb's own — a pane's WIDTH decides whether what the agent reads is wrapped

R308.decision_summary: What the keys do is a thing the keys can show: one derived view of the keymap in force, painted by both frontends and printed by the CLI, that also names every action no key reaches.
changes_bullets: what the keys do had NO answer inside sprag: neither frontend showed a binding, so a user had to leave the terminal and run sprag list-keys in a shell — the one moment they cannot — and the only place in the product that displayed a chord was the GUI palette's five hardcoded strings

sprag_host::keyhelp renders a keymap in force as ROWS, derived from the two authorities that already existed: BoundAction's Display (the canonical spelling list-keys prints and parse reads back) and BoundAction::VOCABULARY, "the ONE enumeration" — nothing in the module writes down the name of an action, a flag or a key

the view answers TWO questions: what your keys do, grouped by BoundAction::subject (an exhaustive match, so a verb added later must state its group), and what else you could bind — the whole vocabulary, each form marked when no key reaches its verb
list-keys joins the vocabulary as a bindable action on tmux's own prefix ?, so the key that opens the table appears in the table it opens and is rebindable by the same file as everything else

BoundAction::reaches sees THROUGH a guard: prefix & is confirm-before kill-window and reaches both, which a test measured before it existed — the first version reported kill-window unbound while the key that kills the window sat three lines above
both frontends paint it: sprag-tui gets a full-screen overlay and sprag-gui a modal, and sprag-tui's two overlay Options became ONE exclusive Overlay so a question and the key table cannot both be up

KeyHelp::pressed decides what each key MEANS (arrows and j/k, PageUp/PageDown with less's b/f, Home/End, q/Escape/Enter) so two clients cannot drift, and Shift is ignored on a character key — the shipped defect R306 measured on prefix %

R310.decision_summary: A WINDOW HAS A PLACE, AND A PLACE IS A THING YOU CAN SAY. Measured first: a session's window order was WALKED by prefix n/p, PAINTED by sprag-gui's tab strip and published as the windows slot's ARRAY - and changeable by nothing in the product, promised by nothing, and observable by nothing (SessionShape::diff matched windows by identity with a find, so a reorder produced zero events). The same collection is a RING to walk and a SEQUENCE to arrange: the walk wraps because attention comes back round, the move stops because the strip has a first tab and a last. move_window is the daemon's first ordering op, its anchor is a NAME and never an index, and PlaceHow answers four words where the rival answers a bool.
changes_bullets: WindowPlace (first/last/one-step/before/after) and PlaceHow (moved/already_there/alone/itself) join sprag-terminal beside WindowStep; Session::move_window computes one destination index in the frame with the moved window REMOVED, so "already there" falls out of a single comparison and the source-before-insert correction is written once.
An anchor is a NAME resolved under the registry lock, never an insertion INDEX a client computed from a list it read earlier - PaneName's argument one level up.
The current window follows its own window across a move BY IDENTITY (WindowId), because an index is where a window is and where it is, is exactly what this verb changes.

Event::WindowsReordered is DERIVED in SessionShape::diff from the COMMON-ID SUBSEQUENCES of the two shapes - the first comparison in that function that reads a sequence where every other reads a set, so a reorder produced zero events before this round.

It names no window on purpose and the claim is PROVED: `move A after B` and `move B before A` leave identical state, so no derivation from state can attribute the move, and a subject is what a filter matches on.

move_window {window?, place|before|after} answering {window, how}; the CURRENT window is resolved at the daemon under the lock that moves it, and an absent window or anchor is REFUSED rather than answered as an outcome.
sprag move-window [W] --first|--last|-n|-p|--before W|--after W, with one sentence per outcome and a daemon-too-old-for-the-verb told apart from a refusal.
prefix < / prefix > step the current window along; prefix . is tmux's OWN default for this verb and ASKS for an anchor by name, where tmux's prompt wants an index and a command template.
Subject::MoveBefore is the fourth line-ask and the first that is not a rename: its answer is an ADDRESS of a different window, its seed is EMPTY, and its commit reports the daemon's outcome word.
Both frontends carry the arms out; the GUI palette gains the four anchorless placings, PAIRED with the binding so the hint column shows the user's own chord.
The snapshot's doc called the window order "creation order", which this round made false; the arranged order is now pinned across a restart.

TEN revert-proofs, each shown to DISCRIMINATE with a control green after it: the frame correction, the current-window follow, the funnel's sequence check, the funnel's common-subset restriction, the daemon-side current-window resolution, the answer's outcome word, asks() for the prompt arm, the prompt's subject, the palette's place routing, and the restored order.

Honest trade: herdr's whole API is its agent surface, so their agent reaches tab.move by construction.
NO swap-window: for a LIST the general primitive is a move, and an exchange of two non-adjacent windows is a different result not expressible as one. tmux has both; herdr has only a move.
NO cross-session window move (tmux move-window -s a:1 -t b:) - a decision about ADDRESSING, not about ordering.
NO GUI tab DRAG, which is herdr's ONLY gesture for this. The strip that draws the order is one check away from it; the keyboard and the CLI are what had no answer at all.

sprag move-window requires -t SESSION, joining select-window and the other window verbs - the registered mandatory -t gap gains a fifth member.
The one-step keys do NOT repeat (no tmux -r), on the window keys' own argument: a held > walks a window past every other one and stops nowhere a user aimed at.
The GUI's palette offers only the four ANCHORLESS placings; the anchored forms would be one row per window per direction, and prefix . already asks for an anchor by name.
