R311.decision_summary: A READ REACHES AS FAR AS A WRITE. Measured first: sprag's WRITE verbs cross a window and its READS did not - rename_pane and swap_pane resolve a pane registry-wide, where a read is addressed at a SCENE path and the scene holds only the scoped session's CURRENT window. So an agent could RENAME and SWAP a pane it could not READ, and read_pane by name one window over answered 'no pane is called buildout; no pane in this terminal has a name yet' with both halves false. The cause is one sentence - the writes are mux actions and the reads are scene paths - and the seam already existed: Scope has always carried a window NAME and that window's POOL, so only the ASK was missing. A request can name a window now, and every subject wait_for_change tells an agent about has a tool that reads it.
changes_bullets: ScopeAsk gained WINDOW_PARAM - ORTHOGONAL to its three arms rather than a fourth, so it composes with Default, Named and Attached alike; parsed by ScopeAsk::window so the whole scope grammar keeps one home, null refused, absent means the session's CURRENT window.

Scope::narrowed is the one place the ask becomes a window, reading the name and the pool off the SAME Window as of_session always has; two refusals with their own sentences, because a window NUMBER is the likeliest mistake and is not the same error as an unknown name.

A pane NAME now resolves across the SESSION on the agent surface, which is what PaneName promised all along; a pane NUMBER stays window-local because list_panes is what defines it and widening it would silently change every existing pane: 2.
PaneRef carries the pane's window, and pane_params is the ONE place a read learns which window to look in - so a tool added later cannot forget it and quietly become window-local again.

list_windows lists the session's windows in R310's order, marking CURRENT and YOU ARE HERE separately because they are different facts, with each window's pane names so the handle an agent takes away is never a position.

list_sessions gives the third subject a reader; a READ only, because these tools act on the agent's own session and a pane name's registry-wide uniqueness is not a licence to cross a boundary the user drew.

THE COMPLETENESS RATCHET walks EventKind::ALL, takes each subject_key, and asserts the roster declares a DISTINCT tool that reads that subject - so a kind added later naming a new subject fails until its reader exists.
The refusal for an unknown name lists the session's named panes WITH their windows, where it used to say "no pane in this terminal has a name yet" about a terminal that had one.
list_panes and pane_layout name the WINDOW instead of calling it the terminal, and point at list_windows.
R310's own wait_for_change sentence said "the order list_panes's windows are listed in"; list_panes lists no windows. Corrected to list_windows.

FOUR revert-proofs, each shown to DISCRIMINATE with a control green after it: dropping the window read from Scope::resolve, resolving the window against the CURRENT one, stopping the NAME looking past the caller's window, and dropping the window from the read's params.

WIRE_PROTOCOL 10 to 11, the FIFTH bump from an added ARGUMENT, MEASURED with a discriminating control AFTER A FIRST PROBE THAT HAD NONE: the first fixture was built with the NEW client, which the old daemon refuses by number, so it had one window and "narrowed == not narrowed" was trivially true. Rebuilt with the OLD client, the old daemon answers [0] to both the narrowed and unnarrowed query - the argument accepted, DROPPED, and answered about the CURRENT window - where the new daemon answers [1] and [0].

The measurement before a line was written, against a real isolated daemon with two windows: the roster had 21 tools and readers for PANE only; read_pane by name one window over said "no pane is called buildout; no pane in this terminal has a name yet", both halves false; and rename-pane and swap-pane on the SAME pane both succeeded.

The daemon seam is there and the CLI is one flag from it; the agent surface was taken first because that is where the false sentence was.

NO WINDOW OR SESSION WRITE FOR AN AGENT (select_window, new-window, kill-session). This round's claim is about READING what an agent is TOLD; a write is R294's authorship question at a scope its per-pane gate does not cover. Honest trade, stated first: herdr's whole 76-method API IS their agent surface, so their agent reaches every one of these by construction - they are AHEAD and this round does not close it.
NO CROSS-SESSION PANE READ. The window scope rides inside a session scope.

query_session_panes costs one query per window. Fine for the handful of windows a session holds and the path only runs when a NAME missed in the caller's own window; worth revisiting if a session-wide pane slot ever exists for another reason.

sprag-mcp sends NO session scope at all, so it acts on the daemon's DEFAULT session rather than the one the agent's pane is in. Pre-existing, not this round's, and correct for the ordinary case - but it is a positional assumption of the same family as the pane number and nothing checks it.
The MCP surface still has no window or session verb in the WRITE direction and no pane_layout for another window; list_windows reports pane names and counts, not arrangements.

R312.decision_summary: A NAME IS THE ADDRESS, AT EVERY DOOR. A pane NAME is the one handle that does not move (R295) and reaches across a window (R311) - it is an ADDRESS, and an address only some doors accept is not an address but a convenience some functions happen to implement. Measured at e7be5eb: of the agent surface's eighteen pane-addressed tools SEVEN reached a pane one window over and ELEVEN refused, and of the CLI's pane verbs NONE accepted a name at all, in six different sentences. One cause - a pane address was parsed and resolved independently at every entry point, so which doors took a name was an accident of when each was written. There is one grammar now, in the library both binaries link; one resolver per surface, with the window-local helpers deleted rather than left to be reached; and two RATCHETS that derive what to check from the roster and from the usage, so a door added later cannot be narrow.
changes_bullets: sprag_host::pane_address is the ONE grammar deciding what a pane argument NAMES: PaneAddress::parse splits an all-digit token from a name exactly as PaneName::parse does, and the unknown and ambiguous refusals get one home with two callers - which is what the CLI's SIX spellings of one rule were the absence of.

The agent surface has ONE resolver. resolve_pane and resolve_pane_id are deleted; resolve_pane_ref (and its _at and _optional siblings) is the only way a pane argument becomes a pane, and pane_params the only way one is addressed.

PaneInfo has no number field any more. A number is a property of a LISTING, not of a pane - it means the Nth row of list_panes, and list_panes answers about ONE window - so a row that carried one could be read out of a listing it does not belong to and name a different pane with a straight face. It is formed only by numbered(index), from a slice the caller holds.

PaneRef carries the pane's whole row from the reading that resolved it, so a tool wanting the far pane's fields has nothing to go back for - which is the torn read R311 reintroduced, removed at its cause rather than at one call site.

require_own_pane is R294's authorship gate in ONE place: close_pane, rename_pane, swap_pane and resize_pane asked the same question of the same argument against a listing each had read, so all four refused a far pane with a sentence about NAMES instead of about ownership.
pane_layout takes the same pane argument every other tool takes - draw the window holding THIS pane - rather than a second window grammar; a far window's drawing carries no numbers and says why.

Every CLI pane verb resolves through sprag.rs's resolve_pane, which answers a PaneSite carrying the window it found. require_pane, the window-local pre-flight, is DELETED: a helper that can only see one window is the defect, and keeping it would let a verb grow back into it. A PaneSite has no other constructor.

The CLI's numeric spelling reaches any window too. A pane id is registry-unique and never reused, so it has no positional hazard and there was never a reason for a read to see fewer panes than a write.

TWO RATCHETS, both DERIVED. The agent one walks tools/list and drives every tool whose own inputSchema declares a pane property; the CLI one parses the usage text - the CLI's own published claim about which verbs take a PANE - and drives each verb it names. Neither holds a hand-written list of what to check, which is the defect R311's pin had one level up.

R313.decision_summary: AN AGENT CAN PUT A PERSON IN FRONT OF WHAT IT MADE. An agent has opened, named and driven a pane since R294 and reached one in any window since R311/R312 - it still could not make a place of its own to work in, and could not bring a person to what it made. Both halves are the WINDOW level, where the agent surface had no write at all: measured at 37d3971, the only window tools were two READS. The design question is not the tools but the DEFAULT: the daemon's new_window SELECTED, so wrapping it would take the user's screen every time an agent decided to do some work. So a window can now be born DETACHED, creating a place and SHOWING it are two acts, and only select_window is about the person. A window records WHO ASKED - R294's fact one level up - which is what makes close_window and rename_window safe to hand an agent, and close_window refuses the session's LAST window because a tidy-up must not end somebody's workspace.
changes_bullets: NEW_WINDOW_ACTION gained tmux's `detached` - a window can be CREATED without being SHOWN. The daemon always selected, so a caller that is not a person could not make itself a place to work without taking over the user's screen, which is the intrusion R294's authorship gate exists to prevent arriving one level up and with no gate at all.

Window::opened_by records who asked, exactly as Pane::opened_by has since R294: published additively on the windows slot, durable in WindowSnapshot with serde(default), and restored on manual_size's argument - a window that came back unclaimed would be one its author could no longer tidy up, so the litter the gate prevents would survive every restart.

⚠ THE BIRTH PANE IS PLACED BY NAME NOW. The host handler took the pool as "the current window's", which was correct only because new_window always selected - so the moment `detached` existed that lookup would have spawned the birth pane into the window the user was already on. A detached window would have come back EMPTY and the person's window would have grown a pane nobody asked for.

Four agent tools: open_window (always detached, always named as the agent's), select_window (UNGATED - it is select_pane's twin and moving a person is allowed), close_window and rename_window (both gated on authorship, R294's rule one level up through require_own_window).

close_window ALSO refuses the session's last window. R309 made a kill cascade, so an agent tidying its own workbench could otherwise end a person's whole session - measured: with the guard removed, the close ended the DAEMON and the test saw `host closed the connection`.

WindowBirthAsk is the REQUEST grammar as a TYPE, so the two clients and the daemon cannot spell these keys three ways - and so the wire's shape pin can hold the bytes, which is the half of R300's finding that a `json!` at a call site is invisible to.
sprag new-window -d, and `sprag windows` prints who asked for a window - the operator's half of the fact this round records.
list_windows tells an agent which windows are ITS OWN, which is the question the two gated verbs raise and the answer that was otherwise unreachable.

THE WINDOW RATCHET walks tools/list for every tool declaring a `window` argument and aims it at a PERSON's window, asserting it either succeeds harmlessly or refuses on AUTHORSHIP - and then asserts the window is STILL THERE, without which the check passes on a tool that destroyed it cheerfully.

MEASURED at `37d3971` before a line was written, through the SHIPPED sprag-mcp against a real daemon: 23 tools, of which the ONLY window-level ones were list_windows and list_sessions and both are READS; every write tool was pane-level; `new_window` SELECTED what it created (current went 0 to agentwork); `detached: true` was ACCEPTED AND DROPPED; and the windows slot published no authorship at all.

R312's OWN ANSWER named the gap, which is how this round opened: selecting a far pane told the agent "the USER is in window 0 and did not move - this surface has no verb that changes which window a person is looking at".

SIX revert-proofs, each shown to DISCRIMINATE with a control green after it: new_window selecting regardless of the flag, the snapshot dropping who asked, open_window sending detached:false, the session guard removed, the window authorship gate removed, and the protocol number put back.
⚠ THE SESSION-GUARD REVERT-PROOF SHOWED THE HARM DIRECTLY: with the guard gone the close ended the daemon, and the test's failure text is `host closed the connection`.
⚠ THE WINDOW-GATE REVERT-PROOF SHOWED IT TOO: with the gate gone, close_window destroyed the person's window and the NEXT verb in the ratchet failed to find it.

⚠ A CHECK OF MINE COULD NOT FAIL AND WAS REBUILT. The first session-guard measurement asked the agent to close its own window while the person's window still stood, which is simply a legal close. The state has to be BUILT - the person's window killed out of band - for the guard to be reachable at all.

WIRE_PROTOCOL 11 to 12, the SIXTH bump from an added ARGUMENT, measured BOTH directions with a control that isolates the one differing fact: a raw request carrying `detached` against a protocol-11 daemon returns the same answer bytes AND selects the window (current becomes quiet), where the identical request against the protocol-12 daemon leaves current on 0; a real protocol-12 client is refused BY NUMBER with the skew sentence; and the CONTROL - the old client against that same old daemon - works, so the refusal is the protocol rather than a broken daemon.

The whole claim driven end to end as standing tests: an agent opens a window, the session does NOT move, it drives a pane of that window from its own by NAME, and only select_window moves the person - with the session's current window read before and after as the discriminator.
carry_forward_bullets: ⚠ REVERTING THE PROTOCOL NUMBER IS STILL CAUGHT BY NOTHING IN-PROCESS, and this round MEASURED it rather than assuming R300 had closed it: putting WIRE_PROTOCOL back to 11 left the whole suite green. The shape pin makes a SHAPE change fail so the number gets moved; it cannot make a wrong NUMBER fail. Pinning the number as a literal WOULD catch it - and was deliberately not done, because it would make every future bump's revert-proof fail trivially and stop telling the round whether the bump MATTERED. The number's correctness rests on the skew run, both directions, every round.

NO new_session or kill_session for an agent. A session is the boundary a PERSON drew around a workspace; R311 already refused to let a pane read across one and creating or ending one is further still.
NO move_window for an agent (R310's ordering). Where a person's windows sit in the strip is their arrangement - swap_pane's argument at the window level.
NO default KEY for `new-window -d`. Choosing a default chord belongs to the keymap surface (R284's argument), not to the round that adds the flag.

THE SESSION GUARD IS CLIENT-SIDE AND RACES. close_window refuses when the session holds one window, read a moment before the kill; a person closing the other window in between would let the cascade through, and the answer REPORTS the daemon's Ended word so that case is told rather than hidden. Closing it properly needs a guarded kill at the daemon, which is R309's confirm-before one level down and a bigger decision than this round.

`sprag kill-window` IS STILL UNGATED, deliberately: it is an operator's verb and an operator means it. The daemon publishes who asked and the agent surface applies the policy - R294's split, unchanged.

THE WINDOW RATCHET'S SAMPLE TABLE IS KEYED BY ARGUMENT NAME and fails closed on an unknown one, but its `window` sample is always the PERSON's window - a tool that only misbehaves on the agent's own window would pass it. The three end-to-end tests cover that side by hand.

herdr is AHEAD on the DETACHED DEFAULT and this round only catches up: TabCreateParams carries `focus: bool` with serde(default), so a herdr tab is created without taking the screen unless the caller asks. R313.publishable_decision_summary: AN AGENT CAN PUT A PERSON IN FRONT OF WHAT IT MADE. An agent has opened, named and driven a pane since R294 and reached one in any window since R311/R312 - it still could not make a place of its own to work in, and could not bring a person to what it made. Both halves are the WINDOW level, where the agent surface had no write at all: measured at 37d3971, the only window tools were two READS. The design question is not the tools but the DEFAULT: the daemon's new_window SELECTED, so wrapping it would take the user's screen every time an agent decided to do some work. So a window can now be born DETACHED, creating a place and SHOWING it are two acts, and only select_window is about the person. A window records WHO ASKED - R294's fact one level up - which is what makes close_window and rename_window safe to hand an agent, and close_window refuses the session's LAST window because a tidy-up must not end somebody's workspace.
publishable_changes_bullets: NEW_WINDOW_ACTION gained tmux's `detached` - a window can be CREATED without being SHOWN. The daemon always selected, so a caller that is not a person could not make itself a place to work without taking over the user's screen, which is the intrusion R294's authorship gate exists to prevent arriving one level up and with no gate at all.

Window::opened_by records who asked, exactly as Pane::opened_by has since R294: published additively on the windows slot, durable in WindowSnapshot with serde(default), and restored on manual_size's argument - a window that came back unclaimed would be one its author could no longer tidy up, so the litter the gate prevents would survive every restart.

⚠ THE BIRTH PANE IS PLACED BY NAME NOW. The host handler took the pool as "the current window's", which was correct only because new_window always selected - so the moment `detached` existed that lookup would have spawned the birth pane into the window the user was already on. A detached window would have come back EMPTY and the person's window would have grown a pane nobody asked for.

Four agent tools: open_window (always detached, always named as the agent's), select_window (UNGATED - it is select_pane's twin and moving a person is allowed), close_window and rename_window (both gated on authorship, R294's rule one level up through require_own_window).

close_window ALSO refuses the session's last window. R309 made a kill cascade, so an agent tidying its own workbench could otherwise end a person's whole session - measured: with the guard removed, the close ended the DAEMON and the test saw `host closed the connection`.

WindowBirthAsk is the REQUEST grammar as a TYPE, so the two clients and the daemon cannot spell these keys three ways - and so the wire's shape pin can hold the bytes, which is the half of R300's finding that a `json!` at a call site is invisible to.
sprag new-window -d, and `sprag windows` prints who asked for a window - the operator's half of the fact this round records.
list_windows tells an agent which windows are ITS OWN, which is the question the two gated verbs raise and the answer that was otherwise unreachable.

R314.decision_summary: A session is reachable from where you already are: the keys that switch a client's session join the ONE vocabulary, and the DAEMON walks the ring. Measured first, and the first measurement was WRONG - a grep for AttachAsk::LastViewed said 'tests only', where switch_to_last_session is a production method sprag-gui drives. The real defect was sharper: sprag-gui held a PRIVATE SessionChord table of three hard-coded chords that sprag list-keys could not name, a config file could not unbind, and sprag-tui did not have at all - and its step walked this client's sessions POLL MIRROR and attached BY NAME, R304's defect one door over. R308's finding and R304's finding meeting at the same three keys.
changes_bullets: OrderStep (was WindowStep): one type names a direction along an order; the ends are the caller's, and three orders in this tree disagree about them.

AttachAsk::Step(OrderStep) on client/attach ({"step":"next"|"previous"}) - the session ring walked by the DAEMON from the client's own attachment, over sprag_host::host::listable_sessions, the one builder the `sessions` slot and `sprag ls` also paint from. WIRE_PROTOCOL 12 -> 13.

The attach grammar (AttachAsk / AttachFault / LAST_PARAM / UNATTACHED_PARAM / STEP_PARAM) MOVED from sprag-rpc to sprag_host::wire: sprag-rpc only DEFINED it (unlike ScopeAsk, which HostConn genuinely uses) and is seam-only by construction, so it could not see OrderStep and a step would have needed a second spelling of "next".

BoundAction::SwitchClient { ask: SwitchClientAsk } - switch-client -n|-p|-l|-t [<session>]; ARMS 19 -> 20, VOCABULARY 17 -> 18. Defaults: tmux's prefix ( / prefix ) / prefix L, plus C-S-PageUp / C-S-PageDown in the ROOT table, which until now shipped empty.

sprag-gui's private SessionChord table DELETED, with cycle_session and its session_neighbour mirror walk: three hard-coded chords sprag list-keys could not name, a config could not unbind, and sprag-tui did not have. The step among them read this client's sessions POLL MIRROR and attached BY NAME.
Subject::SwitchTo - switch-client -t with the name left off ASKS which session (MoveWindowBefore's rule), seeds EMPTY, checks against SessionName, commits through switch_session_named.

HostClient gains switch_session_toward / switch_session_last / switch_session_named, each answering the session it LANDED on; WireHost routes all four switches through ONE switch_to sequence, so a gesture with nowhere to go can no longer leave the client without a poll thread.
sprag-tui reaches another session for the FIRST TIME; both frontends perform the action.
The GUI palette's two session rows are PAIRED with switch-client so their hint DERIVES, and a ratchet walks the catalog: no hint may name a chord nothing acts on.
verification_bullets: Suite EXIT 0 / 46 targets / 2130 tests (baseline at 88a3939 was exit 0 / 46 / 2121, measured the same way); clippy 0 with no suppression; doc gate 0/16.

Pixel smoke 183/0 -> 191/0, RUN TWICE (the recorded -r repeat-window hazard), eight checks new, driving prefix ) and prefix L through the shipped GUI binary and judging on the daemon's per-session viewer badge rather than on pixels.

Skew BOTH DIRECTIONS against a parent-commit (88a3939, protocol 12) daemon built in a worktree, with a control isolating the one differing fact: a raw probe declaring 12 gets {"step":"next"} SILENTLY DROPPED and is answered with the session it was already on - indistinguishable from a legitimate one-session wrap - while {"last":true} on the same connection answers null, so the difference is the daemon not knowing the key; the same probe declaring 13 is refused at the handshake by number. Against the new daemon: 12 is refused by number, 13 steps (alpha -> beta), goes back (-l -> alpha) and refuses "sideways" by sentence.

A live sprag-tui on a real pseudoterminal drives prefix ) / prefix ( / prefix L across three sessions and a bound switch-client -t through a refusal and a landing; revert-proofed (replacing -l with a step FAILS it) with a control (reordering the arms stays GREEN).
The palette ratchet proved by REINSTATING the exact defect the round shipped.
carry_forward_bullets: CUT, measured not assumed: `sprag attach --last` cannot exist - new_gui_client_id mints a client id per PROCESS, so a fresh attach has no visit history and --last would always answer null. Its honest counterpart, switch-client -c <other client>, needs the daemon to re-point a client it does not drive.

CUT, stated: Ctrl+Shift+L is GONE from sprag-gui. KeySpec::matches masks Shift off a CHARACTER key (R306) and folds an ASCII letter's case under Ctrl, so a C-S-L binding also takes Ctrl-L - the shell's clear-screen - from every pane in every client. The verb keeps prefix L and stays bindable.
NOT BUILT, with a cause: no MCP tool (an MCP caller is not an attached client and has no attachment to move); prefix s stays unbound (tmux's choose-tree is a chooser and this is a name prompt).

NOT CONSOLIDATED, and it is a finding: sprag-client's list_neighbour still walks a mirror, because it steps from a session that has just been DESTROYED - only a mirror taken before the death knows where it sat, so the daemon cannot answer it.

MEASURED, so a protection is not overclaimed: a paneless session is unreachable on a live daemon (the boot session gets a pane whether or not `--` names one, and R309 ends a session whose last pane goes), so the listable order and the raw order coincide today.
OPEN: the asking arm ships bindable and UNBOUND; item 30's client id-keying question and `sprag list-clients` publishing where a client was last are untouched.

Round 10.decision_summary: Extract the plugin extension API (the README #1 concern) from two real consumers: PaneAccess (data API) + a Plugin/Driver behavior-vs-substrate split, validated by the orchestrator plus a new pipe plugin.
changes_bullets: Renamed sprag-orchestrator -> sprag-plugin; it is now the plugin substrate, split into modules: access (PaneAccess + WorkspacePaneAccess + KeyStroke/PaneRow/InjectError), plugin (Plugin::step + Step + Verdict), driver (Driver + Guardrails + Outcome/OutcomeState), and the bundled orchestrator + pipe plugins. Pinion-free.

PaneAccess is the extension API: pane_ids / pane_collapsed / pane_rows (generation+text in one locked snapshot, killing a TOCTOU race) / inject (returns bytes). WorkspacePaneAccess over Arc<Mutex<Workspace>> is the single read+inject path, so plugins stop reaching into SessionHandle directly (review finding D, read-path unification).

Split the orchestrator loop: the Driver owns the SCE statechart (flattened to idle->running->{converged,exhausted,failed}) plus the guardrails (max_iterations/max_injected_bytes moved off OrchestrationSpec onto Guardrails); Plugin::step owns perceive/act/judge. The orchestrator (fixed-stimulus drive) and a new Pipe (relay a source pane's newly-damaged rows into a destination pane; never self-converges, guardrails bind) both impl Plugin.

The Pipe is the second consumer that proves the abstraction generalizes: same damage-generation primitive as the orchestrator's observe, but a plugin-owned cursor (after-last-relay vs before-last-stimulus). act/judge were collapsed into one step (so the statechart's internal phases do not leak into the plugin contract); inject returns the byte count feeding the Driver's cost guardrail.
verification_bullets: 59 workspace tests pass. The orchestrator's four tests pass unchanged in intent via Driver::run(&mut Orchestrator, panes) -- the regression gate proving the extraction preserved behavior; plus two WorkspacePaneAccess tests and the pipe proof test (seed source, relay into destination, exhaust on the iteration budget). cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean.

The design was pressure-tested by a Plan agent that corrected five points before implementation: a single step (not act/judge), pane_rows folding text+generations to remove a TOCTOU race, inject returning the byte count, the flattened statechart, and deferring the host-External base to the exposure round.

Crate rename was contained (nothing depended on sprag-orchestrator yet); build stayed green at each phase. SCE needed nothing new (same usage as Round 8); pinion's vendored SCE remained content-identical to canonical.
carry_forward_bullets: Exposure round: OrchestratorExternal / a plugin host over RPC -- start/observe a Driver::run off the serve thread (background execution), so external AI peers drive plugins as scene-as-data -- and extract the shared host-External base (backends/repaint/thread_ownership/Debug/arg-parse) from the now three Externals at that point.

AI-tool adapters (claude/aider in panes with structured I/O) + bidirectional A<->B relay + character-level delta diffing (the pipe relays whole rows on a generation bump today) are the real AI<->AI layer beyond this substrate.
PaneAccess additions (cell/style read, scrollback) stay additive until a consumer needs them (YAGNI).

Round 13.decision_summary: Bidirectional AI<->AI: a Dialogue plugin runs two one-shot AI endpoints (claude -p) in alternating turns, spawning a fresh pane per turn via a new pane-lifecycle extension, capturing the threaded transcript.
changes_bullets: New crate file crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs: the Dialogue plugin. Each step() is one turn — spawn the active endpoint as a fresh pane with the OTHER side's last message as its argv prompt (claude -p "<msg>"; message-as-argv, not stdin, so there is no cooked-mode echo to strip and the fresh pane's whole screen is the reply), await child-exit (R12 pane_eof), capture the reply, close the pane, hand the reply to the other side. Never self-converges; the Driver's max_iterations IS the turn budget (ends Exhausted with the transcript as payload — the Pipe pattern). Pinion-free.

Pane-lifecycle extension: new PaneLifecycle sub-trait {spawn(argv, cols, rows)->PaneId, close(id)->bool} reached via PaneAccess::lifecycle()->Option<&dyn PaneLifecycle> (default None) — kept OFF the read/inject surface every plugin depends on (interface segregation, zero ripple to Orchestrator/Pipe/Agent/test-doubles). WorkspacePaneAccess impls it over Workspace::spawn/close; new InjectError::Spawn. A RAII PaneGuard closes the per-turn pane on EVERY exit path (no leaked PTY/child even on a mid-step failure); close binds the removed Pane so its blocking Drop runs OUTSIDE the workspace lock (R11 lesson).
Honest accounting: Dialogue injects nothing (the message rides as argv), so Step.injected_bytes is 0 and the turn budget is purely max_iterations — no faking a byte cost into the guardrail.

Host wiring (sprag-host/plugins.rs): PluginsExternal 'dialogue' run arm (endpoint_a/endpoint_b argv arrays + seed + optional cols/rows/timeout_ms; NO target-pane validation — Dialogue creates its own panes), BoxedPlugin::Dialogue, PLUGINS += 'dialogue', a require_string_array argv helper. The transcript rides the R12 captured()/RunState.output seam. No new pinion RPC methods, no new SCXML states/events.

Genuine AI<->AI verified manually: the #[ignore]d dialogue::tests::two_real_claudes_converse ran two real 'claude -p' turns and captured a non-empty transcript (~10.8s). Offline coverage uses deterministic printf fake endpoints; the turn-threading logic is pinned by bidirectional_turns_alternate_endpoints so the live test only proves the real-CLI end to end.

Round 14.decision_summary: Make Dialogue stateful: each turn passes the whole accumulated transcript (instruction-framed) so two AI tools converse coherently, not as a telephone game.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs: Dialogue is now STATEFUL — replaced current_message (last reply only) with history: Vec<String> of "<label>: <reply>". Each turn renders a prompt = a one-line instruction naming the current speaker + the seed + the labelled transcript so far (render_prompt; exactly one \n per logical line, no trailing newline), spawns the endpoint with that prompt as its final argv element, captures the reply, collapses it to one line, and appends "<label>: <reply>". captured() = history.join("\n"). DialogueSpec gains label_a/label_b (default A/B).

Instruction framing chosen empirically (a live claude -p probe before coding): 'You are A... reply with only A's next message' returns a bare message, vs 'A: 3' for transcript-completion — so the plugin owns the labelling. The R13 pane-lifecycle/PaneGuard/pane_eof/capture machinery is reused unchanged; the statechart is untouched (still never-converge -> Exhausted, transcript = payload).

Multi-line replies are collapsed to a single line (split_whitespace().join(" ")) so a reply cannot inject unlabelled lines into the next turn's prompt (a correctness flaw the Plan agent caught; invisible to single-line fakes).
Host (sprag-host/plugins.rs): the 'dialogue' run arm parses optional label_a/label_b (opt_str). No BoxedPlugin change, no new RPC method, no pinion/SCE change.

Round 17.decision_summary: Textbook remediation of the AI layer: fix the smells the session review found — RunContext cancel seam, shared poll_until, coherent cost guardrail, lossless capture, single-source screen text, and SSOT/comment sync — without reworking the verified-clean foundation.
changes_bullets: Cancel seam (ISP fix): removed PaneAccess::cancelled (a run-lifecycle signal smuggled onto a pane-scoped trait); new RunContext in crates/sprag-plugin/src/run.rs threaded into Plugin::step and Driver::run, built host-side from the run's Arc<AtomicBool>. Each client now depends only on what it uses.

De-duplicated the await loops: the three hand-rolled bounded-cancellable waits (Orchestrator::observe, Agent::await_reply, Dialogue's await) collapse to one shared run::poll_until returning a Waited enum; shared POLL_INTERVAL + DEFAULT_REPLY_TIMEOUT constants (the per-plugin copies are gone).

Coherent cost guardrail: Step.injected_bytes -> Step.cost, Guardrails.max_injected_bytes -> max_cost; Dialogue now reports its argv prompt bytes (was a hardcoded 0), so the budget binds every plugin in one currency rather than being inert for the heaviest one.

Lossless capture: Dialogue stops flattening replies (removed split_whitespace().join) — replies are kept verbatim in a structured Vec<Turn>, rendered blank-line-delimited (render_turn) so code/lists/multi-line answers survive and turn boundaries stay clear.

Single-source screen text + corrections: Screen::full_text (sprag-vt) is the one definition, read by both in-process pane_full_text and a NEW RPC full_text query on the pane External (RPC peers and plugins now see the same screen, scrollback included). ED-3 (ESC[3J) now clears scrollback (was a no-op under a now-false comment). InjectError -> PaneError (covers spawn); BoxedPlugin -> PluginKind. DESIGN §3/§5 got corrective caveats (scrollback modeled; status current through R16).
verification_bullets: 89 workspace tests pass (sprag-vt 19, sprag-plugin 20 +2 ignored, sprag-host 30, sprag-input 11, sprag-terminal 5, sprag-grid 4); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. New/reworked tests: port ed3_clears_scrollback + full_text_*; rpc full_text_query_includes_scrolled_off_lines; the dialogue accumulation/long-reply tests made format-robust (parse strictly-increasing counts; verbatim newline needles).
Both live AI paths re-verified AFTER the refactor: the #[ignore]d drives_real_claude and two_real_claudes_converse passed (~15.8s) — genuine single-shot and stateful AI<->AI behaviour preserved.

carry_forward_bullets: Real token/$ cost accounting is now structurally ready: the cost channel is named `cost`, and full_text survives scrolling so `claude -p --output-format json` usage is parseable. Switching Dialogue to JSON couples reply extraction to JSON parsing — design the extraction (result field -> next message, usage -> cost).
--resume optimization for Dialogue (avoid the O(n^2) whole-history resend and the MAX_ARG_STRLEN single-arg ceiling).

Agent capture is still visible-screen damage-delta (it injects into a non-fresh pane); a shared one-shot-exchange abstraction could unify Agent/Dialogue further IF a third consumer appears — poll_until already shares the wait, so don't over-abstract before then.

Round 18.decision_summary: Replace the byte-proxy cost in the AI dialogue with real billed tokens parsed from `claude -p --output-format json`, reading the envelope from a new raw-stdout producer tap (the grid corrupts the wrapped single-line JSON) and degrading gracefully on any parse failure.
changes_bullets: sprag-terminal raw tap (crates/sprag-terminal/src/session.rs): TerminalSession gains a bounded, HEAD-anchored RawCapture (Arc<Mutex>, RAW_CAPTURE_CAP=256 KiB) the reader thread tees into in the SAME loop iteration as emulator.advance, so once is_eof holds every byte is BOTH captured and rendered (the grid's completeness guarantee extended to the source stream). SessionHandle::raw_output()/TerminalSession::raw_output() snapshot (bytes, truncated). Head-anchored (append-until-cap then latch truncated) because a JSON envelope is parsed from its START -- a tail ring would drop the opening brace; the cap is the oversized-degradation point. The lock() helper was generalized to any Mutex<T>.

PaneAccess::pane_raw_output (crates/sprag-plugin/src/access.rs): new pane_raw_output(id)->Option<(Vec<u8>,bool)>, DEFAULT None (interface segregation, like lifecycle() -- the three PaneAccess test doubles compile untouched); WorkspacePaneAccess returns the handle's raw snapshot. Documented as a distinct read (source bytes) from the pane_*_text family (rendered grid: wrapped, trailing-trimmed, control-stripped) -- NOT a read-path divergence (R17 unified the grid-text read), a legitimately different datum.

Reply parser (new crates/sprag-plugin/src/reply.rs): parse_claude_json(&[u8])->Option<ClaudeReply{text:Option<String>,tokens:Option<u64>,is_error:bool}>, Value-walked (serde_json added to sprag-plugin as foreign-tool PERCEPTION, not type serialization -- the public surface stays serde-free, no derives). Brace-span ({..}) extraction tolerates a trailing newline / kernel ONLCR \r\n / framing noise. tokens = usage.input_tokens + usage.output_tokens (cache_creation/cache_read excluded -- large and bursty, would void a token budget). Requires a result/usage signature so a random JSON object is not claimed; any failure -> None.

ReplyFormat + Dialogue cost/capture (crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs): new ReplyFormat{Text(default), ClaudeJson} per-endpoint (DialogueSpec.format_a/format_b, mirroring label_a/label_b -- deferred the Endpoint-struct refactor). decode_reply: Text reads the rendered full_text (unchanged); ClaudeJson reads pane_raw_output, parses it, and on success records the result-text + real tokens. Graceful degradation: a truncated/over-cap/unparsable envelope falls back to the raw lossy text + the prompt-byte proxy cost -- never a PaneError, so a broken reply never fails the turn; the cancel path keeps the prompt-byte cost. Round 19.decision_summary: Neutralize the decoded-reply type name to mark the abstraction boundary surfaced by review: the decoded shape is tool-agnostic (AgentReply), while the parser and format variant stay tool-specific (parse_claude_json / ReplyFormat::ClaudeJson) because AI-tool JSON schemas are not standardized.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-plugin/src/reply.rs + lib.rs: renamed ClaudeReply -> AgentReply (the tool-agnostic decoded shape: text + tokens + is_error); parse_claude_json now returns AgentReply, and the struct/module doc generalized to 'a decoded agent reply, independent of which tool produced it'. The parser parse_claude_json and the per-endpoint ReplyFormat::ClaudeJson stay claude-named ON PURPOSE -- they encode claude's specific envelope schema (result / usage.input_tokens), and a generic 'Json' name would be a false abstraction since no cross-tool AI-JSON standard exists.

Made the extension path for a second print-mode-JSON agent explicit: add a ReplyFormat variant + a parser mapping that tool's envelope onto the SAME AgentReply + one decode_reply match arm + one host arg mapping (~30 lines). The raw-stdout tap (pane_raw_output), the cost channel (Step::cost), and the graceful-degradation fallback are already tool-agnostic, so no new result type and no foundation change. An interactive-TUI agent (non print-mode) remains the harder, separately-tracked capture problem.
verification_bullets: Pure rename, no behavior change: 106 workspace tests pass, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean; grep confirms zero ClaudeReply references remain. Prompted by a design question (could the R18 cost path serve a non-claude agent?) -- the answer is yes via the enum+parser seam, and the result type is now named so the shape reads as generic while the parser reads as specific.
carry_forward_bullets: When a second AgentReply producer lands, split the parsers into per-tool modules (e.g. reply::claude / reply::<tool>) under the shared AgentReply + a ReplyFormat variant each; only then is a trait-object decoder (vs the enum) worth its registry machinery (YAGNI until an out-of-tree decoder appears).

Round 20.decision_summary: Make a ClaudeJson Dialogue resume each side's server session (claude -p --resume <session_id>) and send only the peer's last message, replacing the O(n^2) whole-history resend; a resume that returns no session id self-heals to the fresh whole-history path.
changes_bullets: crates/sprag-plugin/src/reply.rs: AgentReply gains session_id: Option<String>, extracted from the envelope's session_id key (previously unread). A real-CLI probe confirmed the id is STABLE across a resume, so a side keeps ONE id for the whole run.

crates/sprag-plugin/src/dialogue.rs: Dialogue holds sessions: [Option<String>; 2] indexed by turn%2 and selected by the SAME parity branch as endpoint/label/format (one SSOT, no drifting second branch). A side's FIRST turn (session None) and every Text endpoint take the UNCHANGED whole-history render_prompt; a ClaudeJson side that already holds a session RESUMES: argv gets ['--resume', id] before the prompt, and the prompt is a new render_resume_prompt = just the peer's last turn (render_turn(history.last())) since the server holds this side's prior context. History still accumulates for the transcript and the fresh/Text path.

decode_reply / decode_claude_json now return a named DecodedTurn{text, cost, session_id} (was a (String,u64) tuple). step() stores the id on every reply that carries one (idempotent; an is_error reply WITH an id is still a continuable session), and RESETS the side to None only when a RESUME turn returns NO id (bad/expired id, or a garbled envelope) -- self-healing to the whole-history fresh path on the next same-side turn. A broken resume never fails the turn (the R18 graceful-degradation philosophy).

Resume is automatic and internal -- gated by ReplyFormat::ClaudeJson + session presence, so NO new spec field, NO RPC arg, NO sprag-host change. NO statechart change (the Step{cost,verdict} contract is unchanged; verdict stays Continue every turn). Only sprag-plugin (reply.rs + dialogue.rs) changed; lib.rs re-exports unchanged (the new AgentReply field rides the existing export).
verification_bullets: 109 workspace tests pass (+3 over R19's 106), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. New network-free tests: reply extracts_session_id_when_present + missing_session_id_yields_none; dialogue claude_json_resumes_after_the_first_turn (an argv-self-inspecting fake proves --resume appears on turn 2+ of EACH side but not turn 1) + resume_failure_self_heals_to_fresh (a fake emitting non-JSON on a --resume call -> the side resets and its next turn parses cleanly again). All prior tests unchanged -- the Text and json_fake paths emit no session_id so they stay on the fresh path.

Live AI re-verified: two_real_claudes_converse (now exercising --resume on turns 2-3) ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns (~14s) with a coherent count ACROSS the resumed turns (proves the server preserved context via --resume). Real token cost = 9129, roughly HALF of R18's 18214 for the same 4-turn conversation -- direct evidence resume cut the per-turn input tokens (delta-only prompts vs whole-history resend).

Probe-grounded (real 2-turn CLI run): claude -p --output-format json --resume <id> works with the prompt as the final positional arg; the session_id is stable across resume; context is preserved (a resumed turn recalled a fact from turn 1). Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent: it endorsed the single-parity-index session shape, the DecodedTurn struct over a tuple, and SHARPENED the resume-failure trigger to 'reset only when a resume turn returns no session_id', NOT on is_error:true-with-id (a tool-side error on a live session is still continuable). NO pinion/SCE/SCXML/host change.
carry_forward_bullets: The real claude behavior for a bad/expired --resume id is UNVERIFIED at the CLI -- the deterministic self-heal test covers the MECHANISM (no-session-id-on-a-resume-turn -> reset), and the detector is robust to both a valid {is_error, no-session} envelope and a non-JSON error. Pin it only if a live bad-id case surfaces.

render_resume_prompt sends the peer's last turn labelled; the turn-0/1 fresh prompt established the per-side instruction in each server session, so the minimal resume prompt relies on that persisting (probe-confirmed). If a future model drifts without re-instruction, re-add a tiny per-turn framing to the resume prompt.
Agent (one-shot) does not use resume; a future multi-turn Agent could reuse this per-side session pattern. Agent token cost + clean reply-region capture remains the separate backlog item.
The Endpoint{argv, format, label} struct refactor (collapse endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b into one per-side struct) is still the recommended cohesion follow-up.

Round 21.decision_summary: R21 remediation of the AI layer: a typed Cost (Bytes vs Tokens, one unit per plugin) replaces the unit-mixing u64 cost and retires the byte proxy; raw-byte capture moves off PaneAccess into a PaneRawCapture sub-trait; and the empty-result envelope leak, the unused AgentReply.is_error field, and stale cost/SSOT docs are fixed.
changes_bullets: Typed cost (plugin.rs/driver.rs): new enum Cost{Bytes(u64),Tokens(u64)} on Step::cost; the Driver accumulates Option<Cost> (one unit per run, a mid-run unit change is debug-asserted via Cost::try_add), Guardrails::max_cost and Outcome::cost become Option<Cost>, and budget_exhausted compares like-with-like via Cost::reaches. The byte-relay plugins (Orchestrator/Pipe/Agent) report Cost::Bytes; Dialogue is uniformly TOKEN-denominated, so the byte proxy (prompt_cost/fallback_cost) is fully RETIRED -- a Text endpoint, a degraded ClaudeJson reply, and a cancelled turn all report Tokens(0) (no measured spend), with max_iterations as the liveness floor.

Host (sprag-host/plugins.rs): DEFAULT_GUARDRAILS split into DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS / DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES / DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS(200k); PluginKind::default_cost() carries each plugin's unit; build_plugin now runs BEFORE parse_guardrails, which reads a bare wire max_cost in that unit (cost_in_unit_of); outcome_to_json emits a self-describing {cost, unit} so a peer reads the cost without knowing the plugin.

RawOutput struct (sprag-terminal/session.rs): the raw-capture (Vec<u8>,bool) tuple is now a named RawOutput{bytes,truncated}, re-exported and destructured at every seam (session.rs, access.rs, dialogue.rs) -- named like PaneRow.

PaneRawCapture sub-trait (sprag-plugin/access.rs): pane_raw_output moved OFF PaneAccess (the scene-as-data extension surface) into a PaneRawCapture trait reached via raw_capture()->Option<&dyn PaneRawCapture>, mirroring PaneLifecycle/lifecycle(). The core invariant 'a plugin reads structured screen data, never raw bytes' is now STRUCTURAL -- only a plugin that asks for the capability can reach raw bytes; Dialogue reaches it via panes.raw_capture().

Empty-result leak (dialogue.rs decode_claude_json): a cleanly-parsed envelope with an empty/missing result now records an EMPTY turn (reply.text.unwrap_or_default()), not the whole JSON envelope; the raw-text fallback is confined to the parse-FAILED arm, so a result-less reply no longer leaks usage/session_id into the transcript or the next prompt. Real tokens are still billed.

YAGNI + doc/SSOT: dropped the unused AgentReply.is_error field + its parse (no consumer read it -- self-heal keys on session_id); the error-envelope test now asserts text/tokens still extract through the ignored key. Restored the cache-token-exclusion rationale (large/bursty would void a token budget) on tokens/parse_tokens; corrected Step::cost's 'positive/monotonic' doc to 'non-negative, Tokens(0) possible, iterations is the liveness guarantee'; fixed render_turn's doc (the blank-line join is at the call sites, not in render_turn); threaded Guardrails through the dialogue test run_with() helper so the cost-binding test stops inlining a Driver.
verification_bullets: 110 workspace tests pass (+1: clean_empty_result_records_an_empty_turn_not_the_envelope), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. Cost tests migrated to the typed value: claude_json_degrades_on_unparsable_reply flips from cost>0 (the old byte proxy) to Some(Cost::Tokens(0)); claude_json_reply_reports_real_token_cost asserts Some(Cost::Tokens(100)); the orchestrator byte-budget test asserts Some(Cost::Bytes(n)); the RPC dialogue test asserts cost==100 AND unit=='tokens'.

Live-verified (touches the AI path): two_real_claudes_converse, now under typed Cost, ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns (~14s) and accumulated real token cost Some(Tokens(9095)) -- coherent with R20's ~9129 -- with a clean transcript and no envelope leak. Round 21.1.decision_summary: Post-R21 adversarial session review (refactoring + architecture lenses + direct SSOT cross-check) found R21 mechanically sound and the single-typed-Cost decision correct, but NOT fully textbook; the R21.1 clearance fixes the shared must-fix + the majors.
changes_bullets: Dead-API + open/closed (plugin.rs/plugins.rs): both reviewers independently flagged `Cost::amount()` as dead public API while the host re-matched variants inline. Added `Cost::unit() -> &'static str` (the single variant->label mapping), and `outcome_to_json` now does `outcome.cost.map_or((0,None), |c| (c.amount(), Some(c.unit())))` — so the host NEVER names a `Cost` variant. A new cost unit now edits only plugin.rs + `PluginKind::default_cost` (the legitimate plugin->unit map), not the host's render/parse.

Silent fail-open (plugin.rs): `Cost::reaches`'s unit-mismatch arm returned `false` with no guard — a disarmed spend guardrail failing silently. Added a `debug_assert!(false, ...)` (matching `accumulate`'s `try_add` guard) so a mismatch screams in debug and still reports not-reached (iteration-bounded) in release.

Self-describing guardrail wire (plugins.rs/rpc.rs): replaced the unit-BLIND bare `max_cost` (a dialogue caller could load a byte-intended number as a 64x-looser TOKEN bound with no feedback) with self-describing `max_bytes` XOR `max_tokens`, validated against the plugin's unit via `Cost::unit()` — wrong unit / both keys -> synchronous `Rejected` (new `parse_max_cost`, removed `cost_in_unit_of`). New test `rejects_a_wrong_unit_guardrail`; 6 RPC wire sites migrated.

Honest docs (plugins.rs): the module header + `parse_guardrails` no longer claim a cost bound that a `Tokens(0)`-only (print-mode Text) dialogue cannot deliver — they now state iterations are its sole effective bound, by design. `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` is documented as a COARSE backstop (cache tokens excluded; the iteration cap is primary), not a precise spend bound.

Stale-doc sweep (dialogue.rs/reply.rs): rewrote the PUBLIC `ReplyFormat::Text`/`ClaudeJson` docs (still said 'prompt-byte proxy' / 'degrades to the byte proxy' — false after R21 retired it; now `Tokens(0)`), fixed a degrades-test comment that CONTRADICTED its own `Tokens(0)` assertion, and swept the remaining byte-proxy mentions in reply.rs module/parse docs and the test contrast comments.
verification_bullets: 111 workspace tests pass (+1: rejects_a_wrong_unit_guardrail; sprag-host 33, sprag-plugin 37 +2 ignored), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean. R21.1 touches only docs, a new Cost::unit(), the release-inert reaches debug-guard, and the host wire (fully covered by the deterministic RPC tests) -- it does NOT touch the token decode/accumulate path R21 already live-verified, so the live AI test was consciously not re-run (unchanged, covered).

Driven by two independent adversarial reviewers (a refactoring lens + an architecture lens) over `git diff f1688a3 9b03d2a` plus a direct SSOT grep. They CONVERGED on the dead `amount()` + the stale byte-proxy docs (both must-fix). The architecture lens explicitly RULED the R21 single-typed-Cost decision correct over the Plan agent's two-balance (two-balance bakes 'exactly two units forever' into the Driver/Guardrails shape -- the real open/closed violation). The clearance addressed every must-fix and major they raised.
carry_forward_bullets: is_error (architecture lens, deferred WITH rationale): the review flagged that R21 dropped `AgentReply.is_error` -- the one structured ERROR bit in the tool-agnostic decoded shape -- as an implicit capability narrowing (a future 'stop the dialogue when a side errors' policy would want it). Decision: KEEP it removed (the project's own YAGNI / no-dead-surface rule; re-adding a consumer-less bool re-introduces the exact smell R21 removed), and re-add `is_error` + its parse line TOGETHER with the error-aware-orchestration policy that consumes it. The error-envelope parse-tolerance test already proves the flag's key does not derail parsing when it returns.

Cost open/closed is now clean: a hypothetical `Cost::Dollars` edits only plugin.rs (the enum + amount/unit/try_add/reaches arms, all next to the type) and `PluginKind::default_cost` (the plugin->unit assignment) -- the host's outcome rendering and guardrail parsing are variant-name-free via `unit()`/`amount()`.

The Outcome::cost `Option<Cost>` double-optionality (None only on a cancel-at-loop-top, 0-step run) was reviewed and kept: seeding a concrete zero needs a unit the Driver lacks when max_cost is None, so Option is the honest model.

Round 22.decision_summary: Decompose the Dialogue god-plugin into an Endpoint struct (collapsing the parallel endpoint/label/format field pairs) and a Session collaborator whose fresh/resumed/reset server-session lifecycle is sprag's second SCE statechart (the dogfood), unblocked by an upstream SCE +Send fix on Engine's boxed callbacks.
changes_bullets: Endpoint struct (sprag-plugin/dialogue.rs): collapsed the six parallel fields endpoint_a/b + label_a/b + format_a/b into Endpoint{argv,label,format} and DialogueSpec.endpoints: [Endpoint; 2]; the turn%2 parity now selects ONE Endpoint so argv/label/format cannot drift apart. DialogueSpec::new(argv_a,argv_b,seed) keeps its signature (defaults labels A/B + ReplyFormat::Text); Endpoint re-exported (a public field type).

Session collaborator (new sprag-plugin/session.rs + session.scxml): a per-endpoint server-session lifecycle modeled as a 2-state REACTIVE SCE statechart (states fresh/resumed, events opened/absent, NO <final>, datamodel=null) — sprag's SECOND SCE machine after the Driver's orchestration.scxml (the dogfood generalizing the build to N machines). Session{engine: Engine<SessionPolicy>, id} holds the id String beside the engine (a null datamodel cannot hold it, like the Driver's counters beside its lifecycle machine). resuming()->Option<&str> is Some iff resumed; record(Option<String>) folds a decoded id into the lifecycle, ordered store-then-Opened / Absent-then-clear.

Dialogue integration: replaced sessions:[Option<String>;2] + the hand-rolled match decoded.session_id { Some=>store, None if resume=>reset, None=>{} } with sessions:[Session;2] + Session::record. The resume gate format==ClaudeJson && session.is_some() collapsed to resuming().is_some() (state==resumed) — SUBSUMED because a Text turn decodes to no id so its Session stays fresh forever. The reset rule (a resume returning no id => fresh) is now the resumed--absent-->fresh transition. step() clones argv/label/format and the resume id out before the spawn (borrow discipline).

The state<->id invariant: after every record, (state==resumed) <=> id.is_some(), debug_asserted — LOAD-BEARING, a Plan-agent + adversarial design pass identified it as what makes the new state-based resume/reset gate equivalent to the old intent-based resume bool (documented in session.rs).

build/codegen (build.rs, lib.rs, driver.rs): build.rs compiles BOTH statecharts via a STATECHARTS stem list and generalizes the inner-attr strip to each generated file; the sm module split into sm::orchestration + sm::session submodules (each its own include! so the duplicate generated use lines stay isolated); driver.rs import path updated; PluginKind::Dialogue boxed (the two embedded session engines made it a clippy large_enum_variant).

Host (sprag-host/plugins.rs): the dialogue build arm bridges the FLAT wire keys (endpoint_a/label_a/format_a — the RPC protocol is UNCHANGED) into endpoints[0/1]; the Endpoint struct is an in-Rust cohesion fix, not a wire regrouping (the intra-struct drift hazard it prevents does not exist on the wire).

Upstream SCE unblock (stop-and-report rule, NOT worked around): Engine

was !Send because its completion_callback / on_http_send boxed closures lacked a +Send bound, blocking a plugin holding a Session engine from being moved into sprag's R11 background-run worker thread (the Driver dodges this by building its engine in-thread; a submit-time-built plugin cannot). Reported upstream and fixed in SCE (+Send bound => Engine

: Send when P is), pinned via the pinion vendor submodule bump 57e06f1e -> 3078f8bf7.
verification_bullets: 116 workspace tests pass (sprag-plugin 42 +2 ignored incl. 5 new Session unit tests: starts-fresh, an-id-opens-resume, id-less-stays-fresh, idempotent-latest-id, lost-resume-self-heals; sprag-host 33; sprag-vt 19; sprag-input 11; sprag-terminal 7; sprag-grid 4). cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets clean after boxing the large Dialogue variant.

Live-verified (the resume seam moved into the SCE Session, so the AI path was re-run): two_real_claudes_converse ran two real claude -p --output-format json instances over 4 turns THROUGH the new Session state machine and accumulated real token cost Some(Tokens(9129)) — coherent with R20/R21 (~9129/9095) and ~half R18's whole-history 18214, confirming --resume still cuts per-turn tokens via delta-only prompts driven by the SCE lifecycle.

Design pressure-tested by a Plan agent (verdict sound-with-changes, "no upstream gap halts" — which proved false at integration: the Engine !Send gap surfaced only at the host thread boundary and was fixed upstream). Confirmed SCE codegens AND runs a REACTIVE no-<final> statechart (the 5 Session tests exercise the live Engine end-to-end), confirmed the state<->id invariant underpins the gate equivalence, ruled Session (not a broader Conversation) the honest reusable seam, and kept the wire flat. The dogfood is justified by the multi-machine build proof + the legible lifecycle, NOT the 2-state complexity.
carry_forward_bullets: Session is the reusable resume collaborator: a future single-endpoint multi-turn Agent can hold one Session (resuming()/record()) to adopt --resume without copy-pasting the lifecycle. Promote Session from pub(crate) to pub WHEN that real second consumer lands (no premature public API).

A broader Conversation collaborator (two-party history + prompt rendering) was deliberately NOT extracted: it is Dialogue-specific (an Agent reuses the session lifecycle, not the transcript), so extracting it now would be a speculative/wrong abstraction. render_prompt/render_resume_prompt/decode_reply stay in dialogue.rs.
The Endpoint{argv,label,format} struct landed; a future per-endpoint knob (a model name, a temperature) is a new Endpoint field touched in one place, not a 4th parallel xxx_a/xxx_b pair.
Interactive-TUI agent seam + a ReplyDecoder trait the PLUGIN supplies (vs the closed in-crate ReplyFormat enum) remains the north star's defining event, due when a 2nd AI-tool adapter lands.

Agent still reports Cost::Bytes + reads the visible damage-delta; a clean reply-region read + parse_claude_json adoption + (now) a reusable Session is the natural third consumer that would justify a shared one-shot-exchange abstraction.

SCE Engine

is now Send (the +Send callback bound): an SCE state machine can live in any worker-movable value, removing the prior constraint that engines be Driver-in-thread only.

sprag-terminal: TerminalSession::resize and Workspace::resize are now &self (MasterPty::resize is &self; the emulator is Mutex-guarded), so a shared &Workspace reached through an Rc in the reflow Effect reflows without &mut; the (cols,rows) cache fields are dropped and dimensions() reads the emulator screen (single source - a latent dual-source repair).

Round 31.decision_summary: Round 31: IME-composed input (Hangul / CJK) routed to the PTY via a new literal-text seam. A composed commit is finished text, not a keystroke, so it must bypass the W3C key encoder: a sibling invoke("text", ...) action on SpragPaneExternal writes the committed UTF-8 directly to the child, and TerminalViewer::apply_composition (a WidgetCore override, focus-gated on ROOT_TAG, a faithful mirror of apply_key) drives it. Preedit stays off-grid, rendered by the platform IME; an inline on-grid preedit overlay is a later round.
changes_bullets: sprag-host: SpragPaneExternal gains a "text" invoke action (inject_text) writing literal UTF-8 to the PTY with no key-encoding - the seam for IME commits and paste, the same scene/invoke wire the AI peer drives (§2 #2). parse_text_args accepts a bare string or a {text:...} object (symmetric with the key parser); empty text is a no-op success (the IME cancel-via-empty-commit shape). The introspect schema lists text beside key.

sprag-gui: TerminalViewer::apply_composition (WidgetCore override) routes CompositionEvent::Commit to invoke("text", ...), focus-gated on ROOT_TAG and snapping the scrollback view to the live bottom - a faithful mirror of apply_key. Start/Update (preedit) and Cancel are not consumed; the platform IME renders the in-progress composition itself.

A composition commit is text, not a keystroke, so it deliberately bypasses sprag-input::encode (W3C key -> control bytes); the literal-text path is the textbook seam rather than fabricating synthetic keystrokes.

Round 33.decision_summary: Round 33: session-review remediation of R31's IME honesty. A four-lens adversarial review found the R31 e2e test was a masking test (it proves the commit->write seam but was named/doc'd as a live-IME test) and the round record overstated that 'IME input works' when live composition is unverified. R33 renames the test to what it proves, adds honest scope docs, corrects the root-cause framing (ime_caret_rect is sprag-overridable positioning, not a pinion gap nor the confirmed cause), and fixes pre-existing sprag-host doc-links. No behavior change.
changes_bullets: Renamed the R31 masking test apply_composition_routes_committed_ime_text_to_the_pane -> apply_composition_writes_committed_text_to_the_pane and rewrote its doc to state honest scope: it drives a SYNTHETIC CompositionEvent::Commit and proves the commit -> invoke("text") -> session.write SEAM, NOT the live platform IME (it does not reproduce the real Start/Update/Commit composition lifecycle, which is the IME's own and is not reproducible headlessly). Assertions unchanged.

Round 34.decision_summary: Round 34: Korean/CJK IME made usable via an inline preedit overlay. Root cause found with live data (ibus-hangul over X11+XIM, driven by XTEST, read back as scene/snapshot DATA): the commit->PTY seam and multi-jamo coalescence already worked, but the in-progress preedit was invisible — under winit+XIM the platform IME emits Ime::Preedit for the app to render (it does not paint over-the-spot), and sprag ignored Update, so nothing showed until commit (the 'jamo dont coalesce live' symptom). Fix is fully sprag-side, no pinion change: route_composition mirrors Start/Update/Commit/Cancel into an Owner::cache preedit Signal, view overlays it underlined at the cursor via new seams (sprag_grid::overlay_preedit + sprag_host::pane_view_scene_scrolled_with_preedit), and returns true so the shells R705.1 reactive dirty bridge repaints live. Display-only: the preedit never reaches the PTY. ime_caret_rect (Hanja candidate positioning) remains unwired polish.

Round 35.decision_summary: Round 35: session-review remediation of R34 (inline IME preedit overlay). Two independent adversarial agents (refactoring + architecture lens) over 1ba0807 + my SSOT/source cross-check converged on 3 structural issues; each verified against source. Fixed: M1 width-SSOT — overlay_preedit recomputed char width (a 2nd unicode-width model vs the emulator), now both the emulator print_str and the overlay classify through one sprag-vt::char_columns and sprag-grid drops its unicode-width dep; M2 — a wide preedit head whose trailer ran off the row edge was emitted as a malformed Narrow-tagged wide cell, now clipped whole. Plus S1 a single 'no visible cursor => no overlay' gate in overlay_preedit (host drops its duplicate offset==0 gate), S2 the winit+XIM rationale deduped 5 sites -> 1 (the renderer) + xrefs, S3 the masking host test now asserts the scrolled-no-overlay half it names, S4 scroll-snap once at route_composition top (fixes the empty-commit asymmetry), S5 dead unwrap->expect + naming, S6 a test pins the R705.1 dirty-bridge contract, S7 commit-echo doc scoped to echoing programs. Deferred with rationale: D1 a CellOverlay/view-spec seam (premature at 1 overlay consumer) and D2 per-pane preedit (consistent with the existing global scroll-offset; pane-scope all GUI state together in the multi-pane round) — both logged as multi-pane prerequisites. Verified: workspace tests + clippy clean; live ibus-hangul 한글 renders full-width (no regression).

Round 36.decision_summary: Round 36: multi-pane GUI — sprag-gui tiles N terminal panes (default 2, SPRAG_GUI_PANES), routes keystroke/IME input to the focused pane, cycles focus with Ctrl+PageUp/Down, and reflows each pane independently via pinion R1012 use_pane_viewport_size. No upstream gap (pinion already shipped the per-pane viewport seam for exactly this) and no window-side split math (the sub-rect is pinion's post-layout measure). D1 resolved with a PaneViewSpec struct; D2 with per-pane Owner::cache state; the host owns the tiling layout (the R25 lesson).
changes_bullets: sprag-host: PaneViewSpec struct + pane_view_scene(tag, spec) (a tagged flex-share pane Container) + workspace_view_scene(panes) (flex-Row tiling, AlignItems::Stretch, a divider gap) — the host owns scene assembly + layout (the R25 lesson), the GUI reuses it; resolves D1 (the positional offset/preedit tail became a named per-pane spec now that N consumers exist).

sprag-gui/terminal: pane_tag(i) / MAX_PANES=8 / PANE_TAGS static table + pane_count() (SPRAG_GUI_PANES, clamped [1,MAX_PANES]) = the single per-pane identity SSOT (model-scene input External tag, focus tag, paint-scene Container tag, reflow tag); use_terminal spawns N panes; pane(i) replaces boot_pane() as the one "which pane?" site.

sprag-gui/input: per-pane use_preedit(i) / use_scroll_offset(i) (Owner::cache keyed by tile index — resolves D2); route_key/route_composition route to the focused pane via find_external_with_tag_mut(focused); Ctrl+PageUp/Down focus-cycle chord (next_focus + pinion focus_request), the sibling of the Shift+PageUp/Down scrollback chord.

sprag-gui/main: the model scene is Container([pane0 primary, ...panesN extras]) each tagged pane_tag(i); focusable_tags() enumerates the live pane tags; pane 0 is focused at boot; the framework focus ring (auto-drawn around the focused tag, pinion R705/R1010) marks the active pane — no bespoke indicator.

sprag-gui/reflow: per-pane reflow Effects reading pinion R1012 use_pane_viewport_size(pane_tag(i)) — each pane reflows to its own measured sub-rect via grid_dims; reflow_target skips the (0,0) "unmeasured" sentinel; NO window-side split math (the authoritative sub-rect is pinion's post-layout measure, not a consumer-replicated flex calc — the SSOT trap).

sprag-gui/view + a11y: view tiles N panes (each built from its own live screen + scroll offset + IME preedit) through the host seam; access_node returns one AriaRole::Group region per pane, the focused one reporting focused.
verification_bullets: 149 workspace tests pass (sprag-gui 19, +2: the end-to-end multi-pane reflow test + the focus-cycle chord test) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets is clean.

End-to-end DATA proof (the project's debug-as-data method): ShellCore::<TerminalViewer>::compute_paint_scene drives the REAL viewer through the live paint path; both panes tile and each reflows to its own measured half-rect same-frame, asserted against the painted scene and the booted terminal's actual measured cell (not CellMetric::DEFAULT — the shell seeds the monospace provider).
Focus switching proven as data: route_key(Ctrl+PageDown) fires a pinion focus_request(pane_tag(next)) (read back via focus_request::drain) and reaches no PTY; next_focus wrap math is unit-tested.

Stop-and-report cleared — no upstream gap: pinion R1012 use_pane_viewport_size was already shipped for exactly this (its forcing test pane_viewport_seam.rs IS the two-pane sprag model); tiling = pinion flex (FlexDirection::Row + flex_grow); the focus ring is framework-drawn. No pinion/SCE edit.

Plan-agent design pressure-test before the build; every load-bearing pinion API was source-verified (the apply_key model-scene shape, find_external_with_tag_mut, ExtraExternal, focus_request, BoxStyle, and the R1012 publish/skip contract).
carry_forward_bullets: Dynamic split/close keybindings deferred: needs a VERIFIED pinion per-render focusable-tags refresh (pinion seeds focusable_tags once at boot, so a runtime/unbounded pane set needs a pinion seam — stop-and-report before building, do NOT reach into the focus manager GUI-side). The prefix-key command mode is then the idiomatic SCE input-mode statechart (sprag's 3rd dogfood); premature for a stateless focus-cycle now.

Draggable splitter deferred: pinion-widget-paint::view_splitter + SplitterExternal + a Signal<f32> ratio already exist; layer drag-to-resize onto the even flex tiling when wanted (the even split is the honest MVP).

Documented honest bounds: MAX_PANES=8 cap; each pane boots at full-window dims then reflows to its tile on the first layout (a one-frame transient, chosen over duplicating pinion's split math). Revisit if a real workflow needs more panes or a tighter first frame.

A live-window visual/interaction smoke (typing per pane, the focus ring, click-to-focus) reuses the R34 XTEST harness; the deterministic ShellCore data proof + pinion's seam test already cover the mechanism, so it is confirmation, not a gap. The natural next round is the established adversarial session-review remediation (the R25/R30/R35 rhythm).

Round 38.decision_summary: Round 38: draggable splitter — drag the divider between tiled panes to resize them (was an even split), via pinion's view_splitter + SplitterExternal (pinion-widget-paint, GPU-free). N panes nest N-1 splitters with position-keyed ratio Signals. The interactive layout lives GUI-side (new split.rs) since it needs reactive ratios + a registered External the headless host has no use for; the host keeps the per-pane projection (pane_view_scene) and the now-dead workspace_view_scene even-tiling is removed. Reflow-on-drag is automatic (ratio set -> re-layout -> R1012 pane-rect publish -> per-pane reflow; the reflow seam was built for it). DATA-proven (ratio 0.7 -> panes reflow ~70/30) AND LIVE-verified (XTEST pointer drag on the handle -> PTYs resize 47/47 -> 66/28). No pinion edit.
changes_bullets: sprag-gui/split (new module): the draggable-divider layout. use_splitter_ratio(j) (Owner::cache-shared Rc<Signal<f32>>, default 0.5) + SPLITTER_TAGS (static, the &'static str discipline of PANE_TAGS) + view_split_row(panes, theme) (fold: 0 -> empty, 1 -> lone pane, N -> N-1 nested view_splitter, Horizontal, sized Percent(100) to fill compose). Ratios are POSITION-keyed (divider j = docked tile j vs everything to its right) — the proportional split-tree model.

sprag-gui/main: create_extra_externals registers MAX_PANES-1 SplitterExternals (Horizontal, attach_ratio(use_splitter_ratio(j))) sharing the view's ratio Signal — inert when a handle is not painted; the shell's pointer router drives the on-screen ones (NO WidgetCore pointer method). Splitter tags are NOT focusable (pointer-only). New pinion-widget-paint dep (GPU-free, already transitive via pinion-shell).
sprag-gui/view: view_main arranges the docked panes via split::view_split_row instead of the even host tiling; build_pane_scene + the dock floating filter are unchanged.

sprag-host: removed the now-dead workspace_view_scene + WORKSPACE_VIEW_TAG + PANE_GAP_PX + its test + the AlignItems/FlexDirection imports (no-dead-surface — only the GUI used it, and the GUI now owns the interactive arrangement). Kept pane_view_scene (the per-pane projection SSOT); doc honesty: the host projects each pane, the GUI arranges them.

No reflow.rs change: a drag mutates the ratio -> view re-renders -> compute_layout moves each pane_tag(i) rect -> R1012 publishes it -> the per-pane reflow Effect resizes the PTY; equality-skip bounds it to cell-boundary crossings (reflow.rs already named "a future splitter drags").

No pinion edit / no new PR: pinion's view_splitter + SplitterExternal seam (pinion-widget-paint) was sufficient and pointer dispatch to the External is automatic. The interactive layout lives GUI-side because it needs reactive ratios + a registered External the headless host has no use for (R25 satisfied: host owns per-pane projection, GUI owns the interactive arrangement).
verification_bullets: 159 workspace tests pass (sprag-gui 30, +5: split shape x3 + ratio round-trip + the divider-drag reweight; sprag-host -1 = the removed workspace_view_scene test) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets is clean.

DATA proof: ShellCore::<TerminalViewer>::compute_paint_scene boots an even split, then setting divider 0's ratio to 0.7 (the exact write a pointer drag performs) re-weights the panes so the left pane reflows to ~70% (tracking 0.7 within tolerance) — the ratio -> layout -> R1012 reflow chain end-to-end.

LIVE-verified (the R37 XTEST harness extended with pointer events, ad-hoc): the real winit/GPU binary booted an even split (both panes 47 cols via stty size); a synthetic pointer drag of the handle to the 0.70 x-position (warp_pointer + ButtonPress/motion/ButtonRelease) reflowed the PTYs to 66/28 cols — the divider moved and the panes actually resized. Plus a boot-liveness smoke.
Split shape tests: 2 panes -> 1 divider handle, 3 -> 2 nested dividers, 1 -> none; the per-divider ratio Signals are independent and default even.

Plan-agent pressure-test before the build; load-bearing facts source-verified (view_splitter shape + apply_flex_main preserves the pane tag, SplitterExternal wants_pointer_capture + Gui backend + NO WidgetCore pointer method, pinion-widget-paint GPU-free + already transitive, the host-tiling-is-dead decision).
carry_forward_bullets: The divider ratios are POSITION-keyed, not pane-sticky: undock/dock re-compacts the docked set, so a remembered divider position then separates a different pane pair (the honest splitter-tree behavior; pane-identity-sticky ratios would need a real split-tree — premature at MAX_PANES=8). Nested splitters are proportional (divider j = tile j vs the rest), not independent columns.
Cosmetic gap (deferred, YAGNI): the handle does not visually brighten mid-drag (view_splitter dragging=false); the live highlight needs a per-splitter is_dragging mirror Signal.

Still gated on PR-9 (runtime focusable refresh) for dynamic split/close + per-pane tabs + DnD reorder + new-pane undock; PR-10 (per-window viewport publish) for resizable undock windows. Both reported as separate claudedocs docs.
